325.s:
īśvara uvāca
saubhāgyāderumāpūjāṃ vakṣye 'haṃ bhuktimuktidāṃ /
mantradhyānaṃ maṇḍalañca mudrāṃ homādisādhanam //
325.d:
ईश्वर उवाच
सौभाग्यादेरुमापूजां वक्ष्ये ऽहं भुक्तिमुक्तिदां /
मन्त्रध्यानं मण्डलञ्च मुद्रां होमादिसाधनम् //
325.m: The Lord said: / I will explain the worship of Umā that brings good fortune and other [blessings], bestowing worldly enjoyment and liberation, / along with the mantra, meditation, maṇḍala, ritual gesture, and the means [consisting of] fire oblation and the rest.

325.s:
citrabhānuṃ śivaṃ kālaṃ mahāśaktisamanvitam /
iḍādyaṃ paratodvṛtya sadevaḥ savikāraṇam //
325.d:
चित्रभानुं शिवं कालं महाशक्तिसमन्वितम् /
इडाद्यं परतोद्वृत्य सदेवः सविकारणम् //
325.m: Taking the Fire [‘r’], Śiva [‘h’], Time [‘m’], joined with the Great Power [‘ī’], / and having extracted [the seed-syllable] after Iḍā and the rest, together with the deity and the transformations,

325.s:
dvitīyaṃ dvārakākrāntaṃ gaurīprītipadānvitaṃ /
caturthyantaṃ prakartavyaṃ gauyyā vai mūlavācakaṃ //
oṃ hrīṃ saḥ śauṃ gauryai namaḥ
325.d:
द्वितीयं द्वारकाक्रान्तं गौरीप्रीतिपदान्वितं /
चतुर्थ्यन्तं प्रकर्तव्यं गौय्या वै मूलवाचकं //
ओं ह्रीं सः शौं गौर्यै नमः
325.m:
and the second [syllable] accompanied by the dvārakā, endowed with the phrase that pleases Gaurī, / which should be formed ending in the dative case, as the expression of the basic mantra of Gaurī:
“Oṃ hrīṃ saḥ śauṃ gauryai namaḥ” (Oṃ hrīṃ saḥ śauṃ, homage to Gaurī).

325.s:
tatrārṇatritayenaiva jātiyuktaṃ ṣaḍaṅgulam /
āsanaṃ praṇaveṇaiva mūrtiṃ vai hṛdayena tu //
325.d:
तत्रार्णत्रितयेनैव जातियुक्तं षडङ्गुलम् /
आसनं प्रणवेणैव मूर्तिं वै हृदयेन तु //
325.m: There, having six angulas, accompanied by the caste with the triad of letters; / the seat [is deposited] with the Praṇava, and the icon indeed with the heart[-mantra].

325.s:
udakāñca tathā kālaṃ śivavījaṃ samuddharet /
prāṇaṃ dīrghasvarākrāntaṃ ṣaḍaṅgaṃ jātisaṃyutam //
325.d:
उदकाञ्च तथा कालं शिववीजं समुद्धरेत् /
प्राणं दीर्घस्वराक्रान्तं षडङ्गं जातिसंयुतम् //
325.m: One should likewise extract the water [syllable], Time, and the seed-syllable of Śiva; / [then] the vital breath accompanied by a long vowel, as the six limbs together with the caste[-formulas].

325.s:
āsanaṃ praṇavenātra mūrtinyāsaṃ hṛdācaret /
yāmalaṃ kathitaṃ vatsa ekavīraṃ vadāmy atha //
325.d:
आसनं प्रणवेनात्र मूर्तिन्यासं हृदाचरेत् /
यामलं कथितं वत्स एकवीरं वदाम्य् अथ //
325.m: The seat [is deposited] here with the Praṇava, and one should perform the ritual deposition of the icon with the heart[-mantra]. / The paired [rite] has been taught, O child; now I will declare the solitary hero [rite].

325.s:
vyāpakaṃ sṛṣṭisaṃyuktaṃ vahnimāyākṛśānubhiḥ /
śivaśaktimayaṃ vījaṃ vījaṃ hṛdayādivivarjitaṃ //
325.d:
व्यापकं सृष्टिसंयुक्तं वह्निमायाकृशानुभिः /
शिवशक्तिमयं वीजं वीजं हृदयादिविवर्जितं //
325.m: The pervasive [syllable] conjoined with creation, through Fire, Māyā, and the flame, / the seed-syllable consisting of Śiva and Śakti, the seed-syllable devoid of the heart and other [limbs].

325.s:
gaurīṃ yajeddhemarūpyāṃ kāṣṭhajāṃ śailajādikāṃ /
pañcapiṇḍāṃ tathāvyaktāṃ koṇe madhye tu pañcamaṃ(1) //
325.d:
गौरीं यजेद्धेमरूप्यां काष्ठजां शैलजादिकां /
पञ्चपिण्डां तथाव्यक्तां कोणे मध्ये तु पञ्चमं(1) //
325.m: One should worship Gaurī [as an icon] made of gold, silver, wood, stone, and the like; / or as five lumps, or unmanifest, [worshipping them] in the corner and the fifth in the center:

325.s:
lalitā subhagā gaurī kṣobhaṇī cāgnitaḥ kramāt /
:n
1 pañcamī iti ña..
:p 180
vāmā jyeṣṭhā kriyā jñānā vṛtte pūrvādito yajet //
325.d:
ललिता सुभगा गौरी क्षोभणी चाग्नितः क्रमात् /
:न्
1 पञ्चमी इति ञ..
:प् 180
वामा ज्येष्ठा क्रिया ज्ञाना वृत्ते पूर्वादितो यजेत् //
325.m:
Lalitā, Subhagā, Gaurī, and Kṣobhaṇī, in order, starting from the southeast.
[Footnote]
[Reading note:] 'pañcamī' in MS ña. Page 180.
In the circular [area], starting from the east, one should worship Vāmā, Jyeṣṭhā, Kriyā, and Jñānā.

325.s:
sapīṭhe vāmabhāge tu śivasyāvyaktarūpakam /
vyaktā dvinetrā tryakṣarā śuddhā vā śaṅkarānvitā //
325.d:
सपीठे वामभागे तु शिवस्याव्यक्तरूपकम् /
व्यक्ता द्विनेत्रा त्र्यक्षरा शुद्धा वा शङ्करान्विता //
325.m: On the left side of the pedestal, [one should place] the unmanifest form of Śiva; / or the manifest one, two-eyed, of three syllables, pure, or accompanied by Śaṅkara,

325.s:
pīṭhapadmadvayaṃ tārā dvibhujā vā caturbhajā /
siṃhasthā vā vṛkasthā(1) vā aṣṭāṣṭādaśasatkarā //
325.d:
पीठपद्मद्वयं तारा द्विभुजा वा चतुर्भजा /
सिंहस्था वा वृकस्था(1) वा अष्टाष्टादशसत्करा //
325.m: having a pedestal and two lotuses, luminous, with two arms or four arms, / seated upon a lion or seated upon a wolf, with eight or eighteen auspicious hands,

325.s:
sragakṣasūtrakalikā galakotpalapiṇḍikā /
śaraṃ dhanurvā savyena pāṇinānyatamaṃ vahat //
325.d:
स्रगक्षसूत्रकलिका गलकोत्पलपिण्डिका /
शरं धनुर्वा सव्येन पाणिनान्यतमं वहत् //
325.m: holding a garland, a rosary, an unblown flower bud, a neck ornament, a blue lotus, a ball of food, / an arrow, or a bow, carrying any one with the right hand,

325.s:
vāmena pustatāmbūladaṇḍābhayakamaṇḍalum /
gaṇeśadarpaṇeṣvāsāndadyādekaikaśaḥ kramāt //
325.d:
वामेन पुस्तताम्बूलदण्डाभयकमण्डलुम् /
गणेशदर्पणेष्वासान्दद्यादेकैकशः क्रमात् //
325.m: and with the left hand a book, betel, a staff, the gesture of fearlessness, and a water-pot. / One should place Gaṇeśa, a mirror, and a bow one by one in succession.

325.s:
vyaktāvyaktāthavā kāryā padmamudrā smṛtāsane /
tiṅgamudrā śivasyoktā mudā cāvāhanī dvayoḥ //
325.d:
व्यक्ताव्यक्ताथवा कार्या पद्ममुद्रा स्मृतासने /
तिङ्गमुद्रा शिवस्योक्ता मुदा चावाहनी द्वयोः //
325.m: Or she should be made manifest-unmanifest; the lotus-mudrā is remembered for the seat. / The liṅga-mudrā is taught for Śiva, and the invocation mudrā for both of them.

325.s:
śaktimudrā tu yonyākhyā caturasrantu maṇḍalaṃ /
caturasraṃ tripatrābjaṃ madhyakoṣṭhacatuṣṭaye //
325.d:
शक्तिमुद्रा तु योन्याख्या चतुरस्रन्तु मण्डलं /
चतुरस्रं त्रिपत्राब्जं मध्यकोष्ठचतुष्टये //
325.m: The Śakti-mudrā is called the Yoni[-mudrā]. The maṇḍala is square; / a square three-petaled lotus is in the four central compartments.

325.s:
tryaśrordhe cārdhacandrastu dvipadaṃ dviguṇaṃ kramāt /
dviguṇaṃ dvārakaṇṭhantu dviguṇādupakaṇṭhataḥ //
325.d:
त्र्यश्रोर्धे चार्धचन्द्रस्तु द्विपदं द्विगुणं क्रमात् /
द्विगुणं द्वारकण्ठन्तु द्विगुणादुपकण्ठतः //
325.m: Above the triangle is a crescent moon, progressively two padas, doubled; / doubled at the neck of the doorway, doubled from the outer neck,

325.s:
dvāratrayaṃ trayaṃ dikṣu atha vā bhadrake yajet /
sthaṇḍile vātha saṃsyāpya pañcagavyāmṛtādinā //
325.d:
द्वारत्रयं त्रयं दिक्षु अथ वा भद्रके यजेत् /
स्थण्डिले वाथ संस्याप्य पञ्चगव्यामृतादिना //
325.m: with three doorways, three in the cardinal directions; or one should worship upon a bhadraka [maṇḍala], / or having established [the icon] on an altar with the five products of the cow, nectar, and the rest,

325.s:
raktapuṣpāṇi deyāni pūjayitvā hy udaṅmukhaḥ /
śataṃ hutvāmṛtājyañca pūrṇādaḥ sarvasiddhibhāk //
325.d:
रक्तपुष्पाणि देयानि पूजयित्वा ह्य् उदङ्मुखः /
शतं हुत्वामृताज्यञ्च पूर्णादः सर्वसिद्धिभाक् //
325.m: red flowers are to be offered. Having worshipped facing north, / and having offered a hundred oblations of nectar and clarified butter, one who offers the complete oblation enjoys all perfections.

325.s:
balindatvā kumārīś ca tisro vā cāṣṭa bhojayet(2) /
naivedyaṃ śivabhakteṣu dadyānna svayamācaret //
:n
1 siṃhasthāvāhyasiṃhastheti kha.. , cha.. , ña.. , ṭa.. ca
2 striyo vāṣṭa ca bhojayediti kha.. , cha.. ca
:p 181
325.d:
बलिन्दत्वा कुमारीश् च तिस्रो वा चाष्ट भोजयेत्(2) /
नैवेद्यं शिवभक्तेषु दद्यान्न स्वयमाचरेत् //
:न्
1 सिंहस्थावाह्यसिंहस्थेति ख.. , छ.. , ञ.. , ट.. च
2 स्त्रियो वाष्ट च भोजयेदिति ख.. , छ.. च
:प् 181
325.m:
Having offered an animal sacrifice, one should feed three or eight maiden girls. / One should distribute the food offering among the devotees of Śiva and not consume it oneself.
[Footnote]
[Reading note:] 'siṃhasthāvāhyasiṃhasthā' in MSS kha, cha, ña, and ṭa.
[Reading note:] 'striyo vāṣṭa ca bhojayet' in MSS kha and cha. Page 181.

325.s:
kanyārthau labhate kanyāṃ aputraḥ putramāpnuyāt /
durbhagā caiva saubhāgyaṃ rājā rājyaṃ jayaṃ raṇe //
325.d:
कन्यार्थौ लभते कन्यां अपुत्रः पुत्रमाप्नुयात् /
दुर्भगा चैव सौभाग्यं राजा राज्यं जयं रणे //
325.m: One who desires a maiden obtains a maiden; one without a son obtains a son; / an unfortunate woman [obtains] good fortune; a king obtains a kingdom and victory in battle.

325.s:
aṣṭalakṣaiś ca vāksiddhirdevādyā vaśamāpnuyuḥ /
na nivedya na cāsnīyādvāmahastena cārcayet //
325.d:
अष्टलक्षैश् च वाक्सिद्धिर्देवाद्या वशमाप्नुयुः /
न निवेद्य न चास्नीयाद्वामहस्तेन चार्चयेत् //
325.m: With eight hundred thousand [recitations], one achieves perfection of speech, and the gods and others come under control. / One should never eat without having first offered [the food], and one should worship with the left hand.

325.s:
aṣṭamyāñca caturdaśyāṃ tṛtīyāyāṃ viśeṣataḥ /
mṛtyuñcayārcanaṃ vakṣye pūjayet kalasodare //
325.d:
अष्टम्याञ्च चतुर्दश्यां तृतीयायां विशेषतः /
मृत्युञ्चयार्चनं वक्ष्ये पूजयेत् कलसोदरे //
325.m: On the eighth, the fourteenth, and especially on the third lunar day, / I will declare the worship of the Conqueror of Death (Mṛtyuñjaya); one should worship inside a water jar.

325.s:
hūyamānañca praṇavo mūrtirojasa īdṛśaṃ /
mūlañca vauṣaḍantena kumbhamudrāṃ pradarśayet //
325.d:
हूयमानञ्च प्रणवो मूर्तिरोजस ईदृशं /
मूलञ्च वौषडन्तेन कुम्भमुद्रां प्रदर्शयेत् //
325.m: The oblation and the Praṇava; the icon of vigor is of such a nature; / and the root mantra ending in ‘vauṣaṭ’; one should display the water-pot mudrā.

325.s:
homayet kṣīradurvājyamamṛtāñca punarnavām /
pāyasañca purāḍāśamayutantu japenmanuṃ //
325.d:
होमयेत् क्षीरदुर्वाज्यममृताञ्च पुनर्नवाम् /
पायसञ्च पुराडाशमयुतन्तु जपेन्मनुं //
325.m: One should offer into the fire milk, dūrvā grass, clarified butter, amṛtā, and punarnavā, / as well as milk-rice and sacrificial cake, and recite the mantra ten thousand times.

325.s:
caturmukhaṃ caturvāhuṃ dvābhyāñca kalasandadhat /
varadābhayakaṃ dvābhyāṃ snāyādvaikumbhamudrayā //
325.d:
चतुर्मुखं चतुर्वाहुं द्वाभ्याञ्च कलसन्दधत् /
वरदाभयकं द्वाभ्यां स्नायाद्वैकुम्भमुद्रया //
325.m: Four-faced, four-armed, holding a water jar with two [hands], / and [bestowing] the boon and fearlessness with two, one should bathe with the water-pot mudrā.

325.s:
ārogyaiś caryadīrghāyurauṣadhaṃ mantritaṃ śubham /
apamṛtyuharo dhyātaḥ pūjito 'dbhuta eva saḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe gauryādipūjā nāma
pañcaviṃśatyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha ṣaḍviṃśatyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
devālayamāhātmyam
325.d:
आरोग्यैश् चर्यदीर्घायुरौषधं मन्त्रितं शुभम् /
अपमृत्युहरो ध्यातः पूजितो ऽद्भुत एव सः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे गौर्यादिपूजा नाम
पञ्चविंशत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ षड्विंशत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
देवालयमाहात्म्यम्
325.m:
Health, prosperity, long life, and blessed consecrated medicine [are attained]; / meditated upon and worshipped, he is indeed wondrous, dispelling untimely death.
Thus in the great Agni Purāṇa, the three hundred and twenty-fifth chapter, entitled 'The Worship of Gaurī and Others.'
Now, the three hundred and twenty-sixth chapter.
The Greatness of the Temple.

326.s:
īśvara+uvāca
vrateśvarāṃś ca satyādīniṣṭvā vratasamarpaṇam /
ariṣṭaśamane śastamariṣṭaṃ sūtranāyakam //
:p 182
326.d:
ईश्वर+उवाच
व्रतेश्वरांश् च सत्यादीनिष्ट्वा व्रतसमर्पणम् /
अरिष्टशमने शस्तमरिष्टं सूत्रनायकम् //
:प् 182
326.m:
The Lord said: / Having worshipped the lords of vows, Satya and the others, the dedication of the vow [is made]. / The soapberry bead as the central bead of a rosary is praised for the pacification of calamities;
Page 182.

326.s:
hemaratramayaṃ bhūtyai mahāśaṅkhañca māraṇe /
āpyāyane śaṅkhasūtraṃ mauktikaṃ putravardhanam //
326.d:
हेमरत्रमयं भूत्यै महाशङ्खञ्च मारणे /
आप्यायने शङ्खसूत्रं मौक्तिकं पुत्रवर्धनम् //
326.m: a [rosary] made of gold and gems brings prosperity, and a great conch shell [is used] in rites of killing; / a rosary of conch brings nourishment, and one of pearls increases sons;

326.s:
sphāṭikaṃ bhūtidaṃ kauśaṃ muktidaṃ(1) rudranetrajaṃ /
dhādhīphalapramāṇena rudrākṣaṃ cottamantataḥ //
326.d:
स्फाटिकं भूतिदं कौशं मुक्तिदं(1) रुद्रनेत्रजं /
धाधीफलप्रमाणेन रुद्राक्षं चोत्तमन्ततः //
326.m: one of crystal brings prosperity; one of kuśa grass brings liberation; one born of the eye of Rudra (rudrākṣa), / a rudrākṣa with the size of an āmalaka fruit, is the best among them.

326.s:
sameruṃ meruhīnaṃ vā sūtraṃ japyantu mānasam /
anāmāṅguṣṭhamākramya japaṃ bhāṣyantu kārayet //
326.d:
समेरुं मेरुहीनं वा सूत्रं जप्यन्तु मानसम् /
अनामाङ्गुष्ठमाक्रम्य जपं भाष्यन्तु कारयेत् //
326.m: With a meru bead or without a meru bead, the string [is used] for mental recitation. / Gripping with the ring finger and the thumb, one should perform spoken recitation;

326.s:
tarjanyaṅguṣṭhamākramya na meruṃ laṅghyejjape /
pramādāt patite sūtre japtavyantu śatadvayam //
326.d:
तर्जन्यङ्गुष्ठमाक्रम्य न मेरुं लङ्घ्येज्जपे /
प्रमादात् पतिते सूत्रे जप्तव्यन्तु शतद्वयम् //
326.m: gripping with the forefinger and the thumb, one must not cross over the meru in recitation. / If the rosary falls through carelessness, two hundred [recitations] must be performed.
The bell consists of all musical instruments; ringing it produces wealth. / With cow dung, cow urine, anthill earth, ashes, and water,

326.s:
vesmāyatanaliṅgādeḥ kāryamevaṃ viśodhanam /
skando namaḥ śivāyeti mantraḥ sarvārthasādhakaḥ //
326.d:
वेस्मायतनलिङ्गादेः कार्यमेवं विशोधनम् /
स्कन्दो नमः शिवायेति मन्त्रः सर्वार्थसाधकः //
326.m: such purification of a temple, dwelling, liṅga, and the like must be performed. / O Skanda, the mantra ‘Homage to Śiva’ accomplishes all aims;

326.s:
gītaḥ pañcākṣaro vede loke gītaḥṣaḍakṣaraḥ /
omityante sthitaḥ śambhurmudrārthaṃ vaṭavījavat //
326.d:
गीतः पञ्चाक्षरो वेदे लोके गीतःषडक्षरः /
ओमित्यन्ते स्थितः शम्भुर्मुद्रार्थं वटवीजवत् //
326.m: it is sung as five-syllabled in the Veda, and sung as six-syllabled in the world. / At the end of ‘oṃ’ stands Śambhu, for the purpose of the seal, like the seed of a banyan tree.

326.s:
kramānnamaḥ śivāyeti īśānādyāni vai viduḥ /
ṣaḍakṣarasya sūtrasya bhāṣyadvidyākadambakaṃ //
326.d:
क्रमान्नमः शिवायेति ईशानाद्यानि वै विदुः /
षडक्षरस्य सूत्रस्य भाष्यद्विद्याकदम्बकं //
326.m: In order, ‘namaḥ śivāya’ is known [to represent] Īśāna and the other [faces]. / The collection of sciences is explained through the six-syllabled string [of letters].

326.s:
yadoṃnamaḥ śivāyeti etāvat paramaṃ padam /
anena pūjayelliṅgaṃ liṅge yasmāt sthitaḥ śivaḥ //
326.d:
यदोंनमः शिवायेति एतावत् परमं पदम् /
अनेन पूजयेल्लिङ्गं लिङ्गे यस्मात् स्थितः शिवः //
326.m: That which is ‘oṃ namaḥ śivāya’ is the supreme state to this extent. / With this one should worship the liṅga, because Śiva resides in the liṅga,

326.s:
anugrahāya lokānāṃ dharmakāmārthamuktidaḥ /
yo na pūjayate liṅganna sa dharmādibhājanaṃ //
326.d:
अनुग्रहाय लोकानां धर्मकामार्थमुक्तिदः /
यो न पूजयते लिङ्गन्न स धर्मादिभाजनं //
326.m: for the grace of all worlds, bestowing righteousness, desire, wealth, and liberation. / He who does not worship the liṅga is not a vessel for righteousness and the rest.

326.s:
liṅgārcanādbhuktimuktiryāvajjīvamato yajet /
varaṃ prāṇaparityāgo bhuñjītāpūjya naiva taṃ //
:n
1 bhaktidamiti kha..
:p 183
326.d:
लिङ्गार्चनाद्भुक्तिमुक्तिर्यावज्जीवमतो यजेत् /
वरं प्राणपरित्यागो भुञ्जीतापूज्य नैव तं //
:न्
1 भक्तिदमिति ख..
:प् 183
326.m:
Worldly enjoyment and liberation arise from worshipping the liṅga; therefore one should worship as long as one lives. / Relinquishing one's life is preferable to eating without having worshipped it.
[Footnote]
[Reading note:] 'bhaktidam' in MS kha. Page 183.

326.s:
rudrasya pūjanādrudro viṣṇuḥ syādviṣṇupūjanāt /
sūryaḥ syāt suryapūjātaḥ śaktyādiḥ śaktipūjanāt //
326.d:
रुद्रस्य पूजनाद्रुद्रो विष्णुः स्याद्विष्णुपूजनात् /
सूर्यः स्यात् सुर्यपूजातः शक्त्यादिः शक्तिपूजनात् //
326.m: From the worship of Rudra one becomes Rudra; one becomes Viṣṇu from the worship of Viṣṇu; / one becomes Sūrya from the worship of Sūrya; one becomes Śakti and the like from the worship of Śakti.

326.s:
sarvayajñatapodāne tīrthe vedeṣu yat phalaṃ /
tat phalaṃ koṭiguṇitaṃ sthāpya liṅgaṃ labhennaraḥ //
326.d:
सर्वयज्ञतपोदाने तीर्थे वेदेषु यत् फलं /
तत् फलं कोटिगुणितं स्थाप्य लिङ्गं लभेन्नरः //
326.m: Whatever fruit is found in all sacrifices, ascetic austerities, gifts, sacred fords, and the Vedas, / having installed a liṅga, a person obtains ten million times that fruit.

326.s:
trisandhyaṃ yorcayelliṅgaṃ kṛtvā vilvena pārthivam /
śataikādaśikaṃ yāvat kulamuddhṛtya nākabhāk //
326.d:
त्रिसन्ध्यं योर्चयेल्लिङ्गं कृत्वा विल्वेन पार्थिवम् /
शतैकादशिकं यावत् कुलमुद्धृत्य नाकभाक् //
326.m: Whoever worships an earthen liṅga with bilva leaves at the three junctures of the day, / having liberated his family up to the one hundred and eleventh [ancestor], enjoys heaven.

326.s:
bhaktyā vittānusāreṇa kuryāt prasādasañcayam /
alpe mahati vā tulyaphalamāḍhyadaridrayoḥ //
326.d:
भक्त्या वित्तानुसारेण कुर्यात् प्रसादसञ्चयम् /
अल्पे महति वा तुल्यफलमाढ्यदरिद्रयोः //
326.m: With devotion and according to one's wealth, one should undertake the construction of a temple; / whether it is small or great, the fruit is equal for the wealthy and the poor.

326.s:
bhāgadvayañca dharmārthaṃ kalpayejjīvanāya ca /
dhanasya bhāgamekantu(1)anityaṃ jīvitaṃ yataḥ //
326.d:
भागद्वयञ्च धर्मार्थं कल्पयेज्जीवनाय च /
धनस्य भागमेकन्तु(1)अनित्यं जीवितं यतः //
326.m: One should allocate two parts [of one's wealth] for dharma and for livelihood, / and only one part of the wealth [for enjoyment], since life is impermanent.

326.s:
trisaptakulamuddhṛtya devāgārakṛdarthabhāk /
mṛtkāṣṭheṣṭakaśailādyaiḥ kramāt koṭiguṇaṃ phalam //
326.d:
त्रिसप्तकुलमुद्धृत्य देवागारकृदर्थभाक् /
मृत्काष्ठेष्टकशैलाद्यैः क्रमात् कोटिगुणं फलम् //
326.m: Having delivered twenty-one generations of his family, the builder of a temple attains his desires; / by using clay, wood, brick, and stone respectively, the fruit is multiplied ten million fold.

326.s:
aṣṭeṣṭakasurāgārakārī svargamavāpnuyāt /
pāṃśunā krīḍamānopi devāgārakṛdarthabhāk //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe devālayamāhatmyādirnāma
ṣaḍviṃśatyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha saptaviṃśatyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
chandaḥsāraḥ
326.d:
अष्टेष्टकसुरागारकारी स्वर्गमवाप्नुयात् /
पांशुना क्रीडमानोपि देवागारकृदर्थभाक् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे देवालयमाहत्म्यादिर्नाम
षड्विंशत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ सप्तविंशत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
छन्दःसारः
326.m:
One who constructs a temple even with eight bricks attains heaven; / even one playing with dust who makes a temple attains his desires.
Thus ends the three hundred and twenty-sixth chapter in the Great Purāṇa of Agni, entitled 'The Greatness of the Temple and Related Topics.'
Now begins the three hundred and twenty-seventh chapter.
The Essence of Prosody.

327.s:
agnir uvāca
chando vakṣye mūlajaistaiḥ piṅgaloktaṃ yathākramam /
sarvādimadhyāntagaṇau mlau dvau jau stau trikau gaṇāḥ //
:n
1 dhanasyānnāthamekantviti kha..
:p 184
327.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
छन्दो वक्ष्ये मूलजैस्तैः पिङ्गलोक्तं यथाक्रमम् /
सर्वादिमध्यान्तगणौ म्लौ द्वौ जौ स्तौ त्रिकौ गणाः //
:न्
1 धनस्यान्नाथमेकन्त्विति ख..
:प् 184
327.m:
Agni said: / I shall explain prosody as taught by Piṅgala, according to proper order, from its roots: / The [eight] triplets are the metrical feet (gaṇas)—the m-foot and the l-foot [referring to all], two having initial, middle, or final [long or short syllables]—the two [sets of] three.
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: In ms. kha: dhanasyānnārthamekantviti.] / [Page 184]

327.s:
hrasvo gururvā pādānte pūrvo yogād visargataḥ /
anusvārādvyañjanāt sthāt jihvāmūlīyatas tathā //
327.d:
ह्रस्वो गुरुर्वा पादान्ते पूर्वो योगाद् विसर्गतः /
अनुस्वाराद्व्यञ्जनात् स्थात् जिह्वामूलीयतस् तथा //
327.m: A short syllable at the end of a quarter may be long; it is long before a conjunct consonant, before a visarga, / before an anusvāra, before a conjunct consonant, and before a jihvāmūlīya;

327.s:
upādhmānīyato dīrgho gururglau nau gaṇāviha /
vasavoṣṭau ca catvāro vedādityādilopataḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe chandaḥsāro nāma
saptaviṃśatyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś athāṣṭāviṃśatyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
chandaḥsāraḥ
327.d:
उपाध्मानीयतो दीर्घो गुरुर्ग्लौ नौ गणाविह /
वसवोष्टौ च चत्वारो वेदादित्यादिलोपतः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे छन्दःसारो नाम
सप्तविंशत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथाष्टाविंशत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
छन्दःसारः
327.m:
before an upadhmanīya, and a long vowel is long. G and L denote a single long and short syllable here; the Vasus are eight and the Vedas are four, or through the elision of the Adityas and others.
Thus ends the three hundred and twenty-seventh chapter in the Great Purāṇa of Agni, entitled 'The Essence of Prosody.'
Now begins the three hundred and twenty-eighth chapter.
The Essence of Prosody.

328.s:
agnir uvāca
chandodhikāre gāyatrī devī caikākṣarī bhavet /
pañcadaśākṣarī sā syāt prājāpatyāṣṭavirṇikā //
328.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
छन्दोधिकारे गायत्री देवी चैकाक्षरी भवेत् /
पञ्चदशाक्षरी सा स्यात् प्राजापत्याष्टविर्णिका //
328.m: Agni said: / In the treatment of metres, Gāyatrī can be a single syllable; / divine [Gāyatrī] has fifteen syllables; Prājāpatyā has eight syllables.

328.s:
yajuṣāṃ ṣaḍarṇā gāyatrī sāmnāṃ syāddvādaśākṣarā /
ṛcāmaṣṭādaśārṇā syātsāmnāṃ vardheta ca dvayaṃ //
328.d:
यजुषां षडर्णा गायत्री साम्नां स्याद्द्वादशाक्षरा /
ऋचामष्टादशार्णा स्यात्साम्नां वर्धेत च द्वयं //
328.m: The Gāyatrī of the Yajurveda has six syllables; of the Sāmaveda it has twelve syllables; / of the Ṛgveda it has eighteen syllables; and for the Sāmaveda it increases by two.

328.s:
ṛcāṃ turyañca vardheta prājāpatyācatuṣṭayaṃ /
vardhedekaikakaṃ śeṣe āturyādekramutsṛjet //
328.d:
ऋचां तुर्यञ्च वर्धेत प्राजापत्याचतुष्टयं /
वर्धेदेकैककं शेषे आतुर्यादेक्रमुत्सृजेत् //
328.m: For the Ṛgveda it increases by a fourth; the Prājāpatyā increases by four; / for the rest, it increases by one at a time, up to four one should abandon the order.

328.s:
uṣṇiganuṣṭub vṛhatī paṅktistriṣṭubjagatyapi /
tāni jñeyāni kramaśo gāyatryo brahma eva tāḥ //
328.d:
उष्णिगनुष्टुब् वृहती पङ्क्तिस्त्रिष्टुब्जगत्यपि /
तानि ज्ञेयानि क्रमशो गायत्र्यो ब्रह्म एव ताः //
328.m: Uṣṇih, Anuṣṭubh, Bṛhatī, Paṅkti, Triṣṭubh, and Jagatī: / these should be known in succession as Gāyatrīs; indeed, they are Brahman.

328.s:
tisrastisraḥ samānyaḥ syurekaikā ārya eva ca /
ṛgyajuṣāṃ saṃjñāḥ syuś catuḥṣaṣṭipade likhet //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe chandaḥsāro
nāmāṣṭāviṃśatyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:p 185
:ś athonatriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
chandaḥsāraḥ
328.d:
तिस्रस्तिस्रः समान्यः स्युरेकैका आर्य एव च /
ऋग्यजुषां संज्ञाः स्युश् चतुःषष्टिपदे लिखेत् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे छन्दःसारो
नामाष्टाविंशत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:प् 185
:श् अथोनत्रिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
छन्दःसारः
328.m:
Three by three they are equal, and each single one belongs to the noble ones; / these are the designations of the Ṛgveda and Yajurveda; one should write them down in a diagram of sixty-four squares.
Thus ends the three hundred and twenty-eighth chapter in the Great Purāṇa of Agni, entitled 'The Essence of Prosody.' / [Page 185]
Now begins the three hundred and twenty-ninth chapter.
The Essence of Prosody.

329.s:
agnir uvāca
pāda āpadapūraṇe gāyatryo vasavaḥ smṛtāḥ /
jagatyā ādityāḥ pādo virājo diśa īritāḥ //
329.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
पाद आपदपूरणे गायत्र्यो वसवः स्मृताः /
जगत्या आदित्याः पादो विराजो दिश ईरिताः //
329.m: Agni said: / A quarter serves to complete a verse: the quarters of Gāyatrī are taught as eight syllables; / the quarter of Jagatī has twelve syllables; the quarters of Virāj are declared to be ten.

329.s:
viṣṇuto rudrāḥ pādaḥ syācchanda ekādipādakaṃ /
ādyaṃ catuṣpāccaturbhistripāt saptākṣaraiḥ kvacit //
329.d:
विष्णुतो रुद्राः पादः स्याच्छन्द एकादिपादकं /
आद्यं चतुष्पाच्चतुर्भिस्त्रिपात् सप्ताक्षरैः क्वचित् //
329.m: From Viṣṇu, the quarter has eleven syllables; a metre may have one or more quarters: / the first has four quarters of four syllables, sometimes three quarters of seven syllables.

329.s:
sā gāyatrī pade nīvṛt tatpratiṣṭhādi ṣaṭ tripāt /
bardhamānā ṣaḍaṣṭāṣṭā tripāt ṣaḍvasubhūdharaiḥ //
329.d:
सा गायत्री पदे नीवृत् तत्प्रतिष्ठादि षट् त्रिपात् /
बर्धमाना षडष्टाष्टा त्रिपात् षड्वसुभूधरैः //
329.m: That Gāyatrī is Nīvṛt in a single quarter; Pratiṣṭhā and the like have six syllables in three quarters; / Vardhamānā has six, eight, and eight syllables; [another] three-quartered metre has six, eight, and seven syllables.

329.s:
gāyatrī tripadā nīvṛt nāgī navanavartubhiḥ /
vārāhī rasadvirasā chandaścātha tṛtīyakam //
329.d:
गायत्री त्रिपदा नीवृत् नागी नवनवर्तुभिः /
वाराही रसद्विरसा छन्दश्चाथ तृतीयकम् //
329.m: Gāyatrī of three quarters is Nīvṛt; Nāgī has nine, nine, and six syllables; / Vārāhī has six, two, and six syllables; and then the third metre

329.s:
dvipād ddvādaśavasvantaiḥ tripāttu traiṣṭubhaiḥ smṛtam /
uṣṇik chando 'ṣṭavasukaiḥ pādair vede prakīrtitaḥ //
329.d:
द्विपाद् द्द्वादशवस्वन्तैः त्रिपात्तु त्रैष्टुभैः स्मृतम् /
उष्णिक् छन्दो ऽष्टवसुकैः पादैर् वेदे प्रकीर्तितः //
329.m: is two-quartered ending with twelve and eight syllables, while the three-quartered is taught to be composed of Triṣṭubh quarters; / Uṣṇih metre is proclaimed in the Veda as having quarters of eight and eight syllables.

329.s:
kakubuṣṇigaṣṭasūryavasvarṇāṃ tribhireva saḥ /
punaruṣṇik sūryavasuvasvarṇaiś ca tripādbhavet //
329.d:
ककुबुष्णिगष्टसूर्यवस्वर्णां त्रिभिरेव सः /
पुनरुष्णिक् सूर्यवसुवस्वर्णैश् च त्रिपाद्भवेत् //
329.m: Kakubh-uṣṇih has quarters of eight, twelve, and eight syllables, with just three quarters; / further, Uṣṇih consists of three quarters of twelve, eight, and eight syllables.

329.s:
paroṣṇik paratastasmāccatuṣpādāt tribhirbhavet /
sāṣṭākṣarair anuṣṭup syāt catuṣpācca tripāt kvacit //
329.d:
परोष्णिक् परतस्तस्माच्चतुष्पादात् त्रिभिर्भवेत् /
साष्टाक्षरैर् अनुष्टुप् स्यात् चतुष्पाच्च त्रिपात् क्वचित् //
329.m: Paroṣṇih is subsequent to that, consisting of three quarters from the four-quartered form; / Anuṣṭubh consists of [four quarters of] eight syllables, and sometimes it has three quarters.

329.s:
aṣṭārkasūryavarṇaiḥ syāt madhye 'nte ca kvacidbhavet /
vṛhatījagatyastrayo gāyatryāḥ pūrvako yadi //
329.d:
अष्टार्कसूर्यवर्णैः स्यात् मध्ये ऽन्ते च क्वचिद्भवेत् /
वृहतीजगत्यस्त्रयो गायत्र्याः पूर्वको यदि //
329.m: It may have quarters of eight, twelve, and twelve syllables, sometimes in the middle and at the end; / if three quarters are of Bṛhatī and Jagatī, and the first is of Gāyatrī,

329.s:
tṛtīyaḥ pathyā bhavati dvitīyānyaṃ kusāriṇī /
skandhau grīvā krauṣṭuke syād yakṣe syadvo vṛhatyapi //
:p 186
329.d:
तृतीयः पथ्या भवति द्वितीयान्यं कुसारिणी /
स्कन्धौ ग्रीवा क्रौष्टुके स्याद् यक्षे स्यद्वो वृहत्यपि //
:प् 186
329.m:
the third is Pathyā; another is Kusāriṇī; / shoulders and neck are found in Krauṣṭukā; or in Yakṣa it may also be Bṛhatī.
[Page 186]

329.s:
upariṣṭādvṛhatyante purastādvṛhatī punaḥ /
kvacinnavakāś catvāro digvidikṣvaṣṭavarṇikāḥ //
329.d:
उपरिष्टाद्वृहत्यन्ते पुरस्ताद्वृहती पुनः /
क्वचिन्नवकाश् चत्वारो दिग्विदिक्ष्वष्टवर्णिकाः //
329.m: Upariṣṭādbṛhatī has it at the end; further, Purastādbṛhatī has it at the beginning; / sometimes there are four quarters of nine syllables, or eight syllables in the cardinal and intermediate directions.

329.s:
mahāvṛhatī jāgataiḥ syāt tribhiḥ sato vṛhatyapi /
bhaṇḍilaḥ paṅkricchandaḥ syātsūryārkāṣṭāṣṭavarṇakaiḥ //
329.d:
महावृहती जागतैः स्यात् त्रिभिः सतो वृहत्यपि /
भण्डिलः पङ्क्रिच्छन्दः स्यात्सूर्यार्काष्टाष्टवर्णकैः //
329.m: Mahābṛhatī has three Jagatī quarters; Sato-bṛhatī is likewise; / Bhaṇḍila is a Paṅkti metre with quarters of twelve, twelve, eight, and eight syllables.

329.s:
pūrvau vedayujau sataḥ paṅktiś ca viparītakau /
prastārapaṅktiḥ purataḥ pavādāstārapaṅktikā //
329.d:
पूर्वौ वेदयुजौ सतः पङ्क्तिश् च विपरीतकौ /
प्रस्तारपङ्क्तिः पुरतः पवादास्तारपङ्क्तिका //
329.m: When the first two quarters have four syllables and are Sato-paṅkti, the reverse also occurs; / Prastārapaṅkti has it in front, and Āstārapaṅkti has it in the quarters behind.

329.s:
akṣarapaṅktiḥ pañcakāś catvāraścālpaśo dvayaṃ /
padapaṅktiḥ pañca bhaveccatuṣkaṃ ṣaṭkakatrayam //
329.d:
अक्षरपङ्क्तिः पञ्चकाश् चत्वारश्चाल्पशो द्वयं /
पदपङ्क्तिः पञ्च भवेच्चतुष्कं षट्ककत्रयम् //
329.m: Akṣarapaṅkti has four quarters of five syllables, or rarely two; / Padapaṅkti has five quarters of four syllables, or three of six syllables.

329.s:
ṣaṭkapañcabhirgāyatraiḥ ṣaḍbhiś ca jagatī bhavet /
ekena triṣṭuvjyotiṣmatī tathaiva jagatīritā //
329.d:
षट्कपञ्चभिर्गायत्रैः षड्भिश् च जगती भवेत् /
एकेन त्रिष्टुव्ज्योतिष्मती तथैव जगतीरिता //
329.m: With five quarters of six syllables of Gāyatrī, and with six quarters, it is Jagatī; / Triṣṭubh with one [additional] is taught as Jyotiṣmatī, and Jagatī is likewise.

329.s:
purastājyotiḥ prathame madhye jyotiś ca madhyataḥ /
upariṣṭājyotirantyādekasmin pañcake tathā //
329.d:
पुरस्ताज्योतिः प्रथमे मध्ये ज्योतिश् च मध्यतः /
उपरिष्टाज्योतिरन्त्यादेकस्मिन् पञ्चके तथा //
329.m: Purastājjyotis has it in the first; Madhyejyotis has it in the middle; / Upariṣṭājjyotis has it from the last, and similarly in one quarter of five syllables.

329.s:
bhavecchandaḥ śaṅkumatī ṣaṭke chandaḥkakudmatī /
tripādaśiśumadhyā syāt sā pipīlikamadhyamā(1) //
329.d:
भवेच्छन्दः शङ्कुमती षट्के छन्दःककुद्मती /
त्रिपादशिशुमध्या स्यात् सा पिपीलिकमध्यमा(1) //
329.m: The metre becomes Śaṅkumatī, and with six syllables the metre is Kakudmatī; / that which has a slender middle quarter of three quarters is Pipīlikamadhyā.

329.s:
viparītā yavamadhyā trivṛdekena varjitā /
bhūmijaikenādhikena dvihīnā ca cirādbhavet //
329.d:
विपरीता यवमध्या त्रिवृदेकेन वर्जिता /
भूमिजैकेनाधिकेन द्विहीना च चिराद्भवेत् //
329.m: The reverse is Yavamadhyā; Trivṛt is diminished by one syllable; / Bhūmija has one syllable in excess, and that lacking two syllables becomes Cirā.

329.s:
avarāṭsyāddvābhyāmadhikaṃ sandigdho daivatāditaḥ /
ādipādānniś cayaḥ syācchandasaṃ devatā kramāt //
329.d:
अवराट्स्याद्द्वाभ्यामधिकं सन्दिग्धो दैवतादितः /
आदिपादान्निश् चयः स्याच्छन्दसं देवता क्रमात् //
329.m: Avarāj has an excess of two syllables; where there is doubt, [one determines it] from the deity and so forth; / the metre is ascertained from the initial quarter, and its deities in sequence are:

329.s:
agniḥ sūryaḥ śaśī jīvo varuṇaś candra eva ca /
viśvedevāś ca ṣaḍjādyāḥ svarāḥ ṣaḍjo vṛṣaḥkramāt //
329.d:
अग्निः सूर्यः शशी जीवो वरुणश् चन्द्र एव च /
विश्वेदेवाश् च षड्जाद्याः स्वराः षड्जो वृषःक्रमात् //
329.m: Agni, Sūrya, the Moon, Bṛhaspati, Varuṇa, the Moon, / and the Viśvedevas; the musical notes beginning with ṣaḍja are ṣaḍja, ṛṣabha, in order,

329.s:
gāndhāro madhyamaś caiva pañcamo dhaivatas tathā /
niṣādavarṇāḥ śvetaś ca sāraṅgaś ca pisaṅgakaḥ //
:n
1 sapipīlikamadhyageti kha..
:p 187
329.d:
गान्धारो मध्यमश् चैव पञ्चमो धैवतस् तथा /
निषादवर्णाः श्वेतश् च सारङ्गश् च पिसङ्गकः //
:न्
1 सपिपीलिकमध्यगेति ख..
:प् 187
329.m:
gāndhāra, madhyama, pañcama, dhaivata, / and niṣāda; their colours are white, variegated, tawny,
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: In ms. kha: sapipīlikamadhyageti.] / [Page 187]

329.s:
kṛṣṇo nīlo lohitaś ca gaurī gāyatrimukhyake /
gaurīcanābhāḥ kṛtayo jyotiśchando hi śyāmalaṃ //
329.d:
कृष्णो नीलो लोहितश् च गौरी गायत्रिमुख्यके /
गौरीचनाभाः कृतयो ज्योतिश्छन्दो हि श्यामलं //
329.m: black, blue, red, and yellowish-white in the foremost Gāyatrī; / the modifications have the lustre of Gaurī, and the Jyotis metre is dark.

329.s:
agnirvaiśyaḥ kāśyapaś ca gautamāṅgirasau kramāt /
bhārgavaḥ kauśikaś caiva vāśiṣṭo gotramīritaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe chandaḥsāro
nāmonatriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha triṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
chandojātinirūpaṇam
329.d:
अग्निर्वैश्यः काश्यपश् च गौतमाङ्गिरसौ क्रमात् /
भार्गवः कौशिकश् चैव वाशिष्टो गोत्रमीरितं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे छन्दःसारो
नामोनत्रिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ त्रिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
छन्दोजातिनिरूपणम्
329.m:
Agni, the Vaiśya caste, and Kāśyapa, Gautama, and Āṅgirasa in order, / Bhārgava, Kauśika, and Vāsiṣṭha are declared to be the lineages.
Thus ends the three hundred and twenty-ninth chapter in the Great Purāṇa of Agni, entitled 'The Essence of Prosody.'
Now begins the three hundred and thirtieth chapter.
Ascertainment of the Classes of Metres.

330.s:
agnir uvāca
catuḥśatamutkṛtiḥ syādukṛteś caturastyajet /
abhisaṃvyā pratyakṛtistāni chandāṃśi vai pṛthak //
330.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
चतुःशतमुत्कृतिः स्यादुकृतेश् चतुरस्त्यजेत् /
अभिसंव्या प्रत्यकृतिस्तानि छन्दांशि वै पृथक् //
330.m: Agni said: / Utkṛti has one hundred and four syllables; from Utkṛti one should deduct four syllables each time: / Abhisaṃvyā, Pratyakṛti—these are the individual metres.

330.s:
kṛtiścātighṛtivṛtto(1) atyaṣṭiścāṣṭirityataḥ /
atiśarkarī śakkarīti atijagatī jagatyapi //
330.d:
कृतिश्चातिघृतिवृत्तो(1) अत्यष्टिश्चाष्टिरित्यतः /
अतिशर्करी शक्करीति अतिजगती जगत्यपि //
330.m: Then Kṛti, and the metre Atidhṛti, Atyaṣṭi, and Aṣṭi, / Atiśakkarī, Śakkarī, Atijagatī, and Jagatī.

330.s:
chando 'tra laukikaṃ syācca ārṣamātraiṣṭubhāt smṛtam /
triṣuppaṅktivṛhatī anuṣṭuvuṣṇigīritam //
330.d:
छन्दो ऽत्र लौकिकं स्याच्च आर्षमात्रैष्टुभात् स्मृतम् /
त्रिषुप्पङ्क्तिवृहती अनुष्टुवुष्णिगीरितम् //
330.m: The metre here is classical, while the Vedic metre is taught up to Triṣṭubh: / Triṣṭubh, Paṅkti, Bṛhatī, Anuṣṭubh, and Uṣṇih are declared,

330.s:
gāyatrī syāt supratiṣṭā pratiṣṭhā madhyayā saha /
atyuktātyukta ādiś ca ekaikākṣaravarjitam //
330.d:
गायत्री स्यात् सुप्रतिष्टा प्रतिष्ठा मध्यया सह /
अत्युक्तात्युक्त आदिश् च एकैकाक्षरवर्जितम् //
330.m: along with Gāyatrī, Supratiṣṭhā, Pratiṣṭhā, Madhyā, / Atyuktā, and Ukthā as the first, each diminished by one syllable.

330.s:
caturbhāgo bhavet pādo gaṇacchandaḥ pradarśyate /
tāvantaḥ samudrā gaṇā hy ādimadhyāntasarvagāḥ //
:n
1 kṛtiścānighṛtirvṛttīti ña.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 188
330.d:
चतुर्भागो भवेत् पादो गणच्छन्दः प्रदर्श्यते /
तावन्तः समुद्रा गणा ह्य् आदिमध्यान्तसर्वगाः //
:न्
1 कृतिश्चानिघृतिर्वृत्तीति ञ.. , ट.. च
:प् 188
330.m:
A quarter consists of four parts; now the metres measured by syllabic feet (gaṇacchandas) are shown; / the gaṇas are as many as the oceans (four), having [a long or short syllable] at the beginning, middle, end, or everywhere.
[Footnote]
[Variant readings].

330.s:
caturṇaḥ pañca ca gaṇā āryālakṣanamucyate /
svarārdhañcāryārdhaṃ syādāryāyāṃ viṣamena jaḥ //
330.d:
चतुर्णः पञ्च च गणा आर्यालक्षनमुच्यते /
स्वरार्धञ्चार्यार्धं स्यादार्यायां विषमेन जः //
330.m: The definition of the Āryā is stated as having four and five gaṇas: / half the vowels should form the half-Āryā; in the Āryā, ja-gaṇa is not in the odd [places].

330.s:
ṣaṣṭho jo nalapūrvā syāddvitīyādipadaṃ nale /
saptame 'nte prathamā ca dvitīye pañcame nale //
330.d:
षष्ठो जो नलपूर्वा स्याद्द्वितीयादिपदं नले /
सप्तमे ऽन्ते प्रथमा च द्वितीये पञ्चमे नले //
330.m: The sixth should be ja-gaṇa or preceded by na-gaṇa with a laghu; the foot begins from the second when na-gaṇa is with a laghu; / in the seventh at the end, the first; and in the second and fifth when na-gaṇa has a laghu.

330.s:
ārdhe padaṃ prathamādi ṣaṣṭha eko laghurbhavet /
triṣu gaṇeṣu pādaḥ syādāryā pañcārdhake smṛtā //
330.d:
आर्धे पदं प्रथमादि षष्ठ एको लघुर्भवेत् /
त्रिषु गणेषु पादः स्यादार्या पञ्चार्धके स्मृता //
330.m: In the half, the foot begins from the first; the sixth should be a single laghu; / the foot consists of three gaṇas; the Āryā is taught with five half-gaṇas.

330.s:
vipulānyātha capalā gurumadhyagatau ca jau /
dvitīyacaturthau pūrve ca capalā mukhapūrvikā //
330.d:
विपुलान्याथ चपला गुरुमध्यगतौ च जौ /
द्वितीयचतुर्थौ पूर्वे च चपला मुखपूर्विका //
330.m: Another is the Vipulā; then the Capalā has ja-gaṇas positioned between gurus; / when the second and fourth are such in the first [half], it is the Capalā preceded by Mukha [i.e., Mukhacapalā].

330.s:
dvitīye jaghanapūrvā capalāryā prakīrtitā /
ubhayormahācapalā gītavādyārdhatulyakā //
330.d:
द्वितीये जघनपूर्वा चपलार्या प्रकीर्तिता /
उभयोर्महाचपला गीतवाद्यार्धतुल्यका //
330.m: In the second, it is proclaimed as Jaghanacapalā Āryā; / in both, it is Mahācapalā; the Gīti is equal to the first half.

330.s:
antyenārdhenopagītirudgītiścotkramāt smṛtā /
ardhe rakṣagaṇā āryā gīṭacchando 'tha mātrayā //
330.d:
अन्त्येनार्धेनोपगीतिरुद्गीतिश्चोत्क्रमात् स्मृता /
अर्धे रक्षगणा आर्या गीटच्छन्दो ऽथ मात्रया //
330.m: The Upagīti is taught with the final half, and the Udgīti by reversal; / in half are the rakṣa-gaṇas of the Āryā; now the Gīta metre according to mātrās [is described].

330.s:
vaitālīyaṃ dvisvarā syādayuṣpāde same nalaḥ /
vasavo 'nte vanagāś ca gopucchandaśakaṃ bhavet //
330.d:
वैतालीयं द्विस्वरा स्यादयुष्पादे समे नलः /
वसवो ऽन्ते वनगाश् च गोपुच्छन्दशकं भवेत् //
330.m: The Vaitālīya has two vowels in the odd quarter, and na-la in the even quarter; / at the end are eight [mātrās], and with va-na-ga it becomes the Gopuccha of ten.

330.s:
bhagaṇāntā pāṭalikā śeṣe pare ca pūrvavat(1) /
sākaṃ ṣaḍvā miśrāyuk prācyavṛttiḥ pradarśyate //
330.d:
भगणान्ता पाटलिका शेषे परे च पूर्ववत्(1) /
साकं षड्वा मिश्रायुक् प्राच्यवृत्तिः प्रदर्श्यते //
330.m: The Pāṭalikā ends with bha-gaṇa, the rest in the following [quarter] being as before; / with six or mixed in odd quarters, the Prācyavṛtti is shown.

330.s:
pañcamena pūrvasākaṃ tṛtīyena sahasrayuk /
udīcyavṛttirvācyāṃ syād yugapacca pravartakaṃ //
330.d:
पञ्चमेन पूर्वसाकं तृतीयेन सहस्रयुक् /
उदीच्यवृत्तिर्वाच्यां स्याद् युगपच्च प्रवर्तकं //
330.m: With the fifth, along with the former; with the third, endowed with a thousand; / the Udīcyavṛtti should be in the even quarters, and Pravartaka simultaneously.
The odd is Cāruhāsinī, and simultaneously it becomes Antikā. //15

330.s:
saptārcirvasavaś caiva mātrāsamakamīritam /
bhavennalavamau laś ca dvādaśo vā navāsikā //
330.d:
सप्तार्चिर्वसवश् चैव मात्रासमकमीरितम् /
भवेन्नलवमौ लश् च द्वादशो वा नवासिका //
330.m: Seven flames [i.e. seven] and the eight Vasus make what is declared as Mātrāsamaka; / there should be na, la, va, ma, and la, or the twelfth is Navāsikā.

330.s:
viśvokaḥ pañcamāṣṭau mo citrā lavamakaś calaḥ /
:n
1 pucchalamiti kha..
:p 189
parayuktenopacitrā pādākulakamityataḥ //
330.d:
विश्वोकः पञ्चमाष्टौ मो चित्रा लवमकश् चलः /
:न्
1 पुच्छलमिति ख..
:प् 189
परयुक्तेनोपचित्रा पादाकुलकमित्यतः //
330.m:
The Viśvoka has fifth and eighth as ma; Citrā has la, va, ma, and ca, la;
[Footnote]
[Variant readings].
by the subsequent addition it is Upacitrā; from this comes the Pādākulaka.

330.s:
gītāryā lopaścet saumyā laḥ pūrvaḥ(1) jyotirīritā /
syācchikhā viparyāstārdhā tūlikā samudāhṛtā //
330.d:
गीतार्या लोपश्चेत् सौम्या लः पूर्वः(1) ज्योतिरीरिता /
स्याच्छिखा विपर्यास्तार्धा तूलिका समुदाहृता //
330.m: If there is elision in Gītāryā, it is Saumyā; when preceded by la, it is called Jyotis; / Śikhā has its halves reversed; Tūlikā is declared.

330.s:
ekonatriṃśadante gaḥ syājjñejanasamāvalā /
gu ity ekaguruṃ(2) saṃkhyāvarṇāddaśaviparyayāt //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe chandojātinirūpaṇaṃ nāma
triṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś athaikatriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
viṣamakathanam
330.d:
एकोनत्रिंशदन्ते गः स्याज्ज्ञेजनसमावला /
गु इत्य् एकगुरुं(2) संख्यावर्णाद्दशविपर्ययात् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे छन्दोजातिनिरूपणं नाम
त्रिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथैकत्रिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
विषमकथनम्
330.m:
At the end of twenty-nine is ga; it is known as Janasamāvalā; / 'gu' indicates a single guru, from the number of syllables by reversal of ten.
Thus ends the three hundred and thirtieth chapter in the great Agnipurāṇa, entitled 'Examination of Metrical Classes.'
Now begins the three hundred and thirty-first chapter.
Account of Uneven Metres

331.s:
agnir uvāca
vṛttaṃ samañcārdhasamaṃ viṣamañca tridhā vade /
samantāvat kṛtvakṛtamardhasamañca kārayet //
331.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
वृत्तं समञ्चार्धसमं विषमञ्च त्रिधा वदे /
समन्तावत् कृत्वकृतमर्धसमञ्च कारयेत् //
331.m: Agni said: / I shall state the three kinds of metre: even, half-even, and uneven. / One should make the even everywhere, and make the half-even;
and the uneven or defective, the hypermetric, and the even metres. / Glau is the Catuḥpramāṇī; from these two comes another, the Vitānaka.

331.s:
pādasyādyantu vakraṃ syāt śanau na prathmāsmṛtau /
vālyamuś caturthādvarṇāt pathyā varṇaṃ yujoyataḥ //
331.d:
पादस्याद्यन्तु वक्रं स्यात् शनौ न प्रथ्मास्मृतौ /
वाल्यमुश् चतुर्थाद्वर्णात् पथ्या वर्णं युजोयतः //
331.m: The beginning of the quarter is Vakra; śa and nau are not taught as the first; / from the fourth syllable is the Vālyam; Pathyā joins syllables from that [pattern];

331.s:
viparītapathyānyāsāccapalā vā yujasvanaḥ /
vipulāyugnasaptamaḥ sarvaṃ tasyaiva tasya ca //
:n
1 naḥ pūrva iti kha..
2 hy a tiyekanurumiti ña..
:p 190
331.d:
विपरीतपथ्यान्यासाच्चपला वा युजस्वनः /
विपुलायुग्नसप्तमः सर्वं तस्यैव तस्य च //
:न्
1 नः पूर्व इति ख..
2 ह्य् अ तियेकनुरुमिति ञ..
:प् 190
331.m:
from another arrangement it is Viparītapathyā; Capalā or of an even tone; / Vipulā has the seventh even; everything belongs to that and to that.
[Footnote]
[Variant readings].
[Variant readings].

331.s:
tauntau vā vipulānekā cakrajātiḥ samīritā /
bhavet padacaturūddhvaṃ caturvṛddhyā padeṣu ca //
331.d:
तौन्तौ वा विपुलानेका चक्रजातिः समीरिता /
भवेत् पदचतुरूद्ध्वं चतुर्वृद्ध्या पदेषु च //
331.m: Tau and ntau make Vipulā, and several Cakra classes are taught; / there is Pada-caturūrdhva by the increase of four in the quarters.

331.s:
gurudvayānta āpīḍaḥ pratyāpīḍo gaṇādikaḥ /
prathamasya viparyāse mañjarī lavaṇī kramāt //
331.d:
गुरुद्वयान्त आपीडः प्रत्यापीडो गणादिकः /
प्रथमस्य विपर्यासे मञ्जरी लवणी क्रमात् //
331.m: Āpīḍa ends in two gurus; Pratyāpīḍa begins with a gaṇa; / by reversal of the first, it is Mañjarī and Lavaṇī in order;

331.s:
bhavedamṛtadhārākhyā uddhatādyucyate 'dhunā /
ekataḥ samajasānaḥsyurna sau jo go 'tha bhaunajau //
331.d:
भवेदमृतधाराख्या उद्धताद्युच्यते ऽधुना /
एकतः समजसानःस्युर्न सौ जो गो ऽथ भौनजौ //
331.m: there is that called Amṛtadhārā; now the Uddhatā and others are stated: / in one quarter are sa, ma, ja, sa, and na; or na, sau, jo, go; then bha, u, na, and jau;

331.s:
nogo 'tha sajasā gogastṛtīyacaraṇasya ca /
saurabhe kecanabhagā lalitañca namau jasau //
331.d:
नोगो ऽथ सजसा गोगस्तृतीयचरणस्य च /
सौरभे केचनभगा ललितञ्च नमौ जसौ //
331.m: no and go; then sa, ja, sā, and go, ga for the third quarter; / in the Saurabha are some bha-gaṇas; and Lalita has na, mau, ja, and sau;

331.s:
upasthitaṃ pracupitaṃ prathamādyaṃ samau jasau /
gogatho malajā rogaḥ samo nagarajayāḥ pade //
331.d:
उपस्थितं प्रचुपितं प्रथमाद्यं समौ जसौ /
गोगथो मलजा रोगः समो नगरजयाः पदे //
331.m: Upasthitapracupita has the first like the even quarters: ja, sau, / go, ga; then ma, la, jā, and ro, ga; the even quarter has na, ga, ra, ja, and yāḥ;

331.s:
vardhamānaṃ malau svau nasau atho bhojova iritā /
śuddhavirāḍārṣabhākhyaṃ vakṣye cārdhasamantataḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe viṣamakathanaṃ
nāmaikatriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha dvātriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
ardhasamanirūpaṇam
331.d:
वर्धमानं मलौ स्वौ नसौ अथो भोजोव इरिता /
शुद्धविराडार्षभाख्यं वक्ष्ये चार्धसमन्ततः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे विषमकथनं
नामैकत्रिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ द्वात्रिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
अर्धसमनिरूपणम्
331.m:
Vardhamāna has ma, lau, svau, na, and sau; then bho, jo, and va are proclaimed; / I shall state Śuddhavirāḍārṣabha, and next the half-even metre.
Thus ends the three hundred and thirty-first chapter in the great Agnipurāṇa, entitled 'Account of Uneven Metres.'
Now begins the three hundred and thirty-second chapter.
Determination of Half-Even Metres

332.s:
agnir uvāca
upacitrakaṃ sasamanāmathabhojabhagāmatha(1) /
drūtamadhyā tatabhagāgathonanajayāḥ smṛtāḥ //
332.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
उपचित्रकं ससमनामथभोजभगामथ(1) /
द्रूतमध्या ततभगागथोननजयाः स्मृताः //
332.m: Agni said: / Upacitraka has sa, sa, ma, and nā; then bho, ja, bha, and gā; / Drutamadhyā has ta, ta, bha, gā, ga; then na, na, ja, and yāḥ are taught;

332.s:
vegavatī sasamagā bhabhabhagogatho smṛtā /
:n
1 sasamanāgathatobhayāgatha iti kha..
:p 191
rudravistārastosabhagāsamajāgogathā smṛtā //
332.d:
वेगवती ससमगा भभभगोगथो स्मृता /
:न्
1 ससमनागथतोभयागथ इति ख..
:प् 191
रुद्रविस्तारस्तोसभगासमजागोगथा स्मृता //

332.m: ra, ja, sā, go, ga, then dro, ṇau, go, gau is indeed Ketumatī; / Ākhyānikī is ta, ta, ja, gā, ga, then ta, ta, ja, gā, ga;

332.s:
viparītākhyānikī ttau jayāgātau jagogatha /
saumalau gathalabhabhāvau bhaveddhariṇavallabhā //
332.d:
विपरीताख्यानिकी त्तौ जयागातौ जगोगथ /
सौमलौ गथलभभावौ भवेद्धरिणवल्लभा //
332.m: Viparītākhyānikī is ttau, ja, yā, gā, tau, ja, go, ga; / sau, ma, lau, ga, then la, bha, bhā, vau becomes Hariṇavallabhā;

332.s:
lauvanaugāthanajajā yaḥ syādaparākramaṃ /
puṣpitā nanavayānajajāvogatho rajau //
332.d:
लौवनौगाथनजजा यः स्यादपराक्रमं /
पुष्पिता ननवयानजजावोगथो रजौ //
332.m: lau, va, nau, gā, then na, ja, jā, yaḥ would be Aparākrāntā; / Puṣpitāgrā has na, na, ra, ya, and na, ja, ja, va, go; then ra and jau;

332.s:
vījatho javajavāgo mūle panamatī śikhā /
aṣṭāviṃśatināgābhā triṃśannāgantato yuji /
khañjā tadviparītā syāt samavṛttaṃ pradarśyate //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe ardhasamanirūpaṇaṃ nāma
dvātriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha trayastriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
samavṛttanirūpaṇaṃ
332.d:
वीजथो जवजवागो मूले पनमती शिखा /
अष्टाविंशतिनागाभा त्रिंशन्नागन्ततो युजि /
खञ्जा तद्विपरीता स्यात् समवृत्तं प्रदर्श्यते //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे अर्धसमनिरूपणं नाम
द्वात्रिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ त्रयस्त्रिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
समवृत्तनिरूपणं
332.m:
vī, then ja, va, ja, vā, go; at the root Panamatī is Śikhā; / twenty-eight like elephants, then thirty at the even [quarter]; / Khañjā is the reverse of that; the even metre is now shown.
Thus ends the three hundred and thirty-second chapter in the great Agnipurāṇa, entitled 'Determination of Half-Even Metres.'
Now begins the three hundred and thirty-third chapter.
Determination of Even Metres

333.s:
agnir uvāca
yatirviccheda ity uktastattanmadhyāntayau gaṇau /
yausaḥ kumāralālitā tau gau citrapadā smṛtā //
333.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
यतिर्विच्छेद इत्य् उक्तस्तत्तन्मध्यान्तयौ गणौ /
यौसः कुमारलालिता तौ गौ चित्रपदा स्मृता //
333.m: Agni said: / A caesura is declared to be a pause; gaṇas are of that, middle, and final; / ya and u, saḥ is Kumāralalitā; tau and gau is Citrapadā;

333.s:
vidyunmālā mamamāgaṇair bhūtagaṇair bhavet /
māṇavakā krīḍitakaṃ vanau halamukhī vasaḥ //
333.d:
विद्युन्माला मममागणैर् भूतगणैर् भवेत् /
माणवका क्रीडितकं वनौ हलमुखी वसः //
333.m: Vidyunmālā consists of ma, ma, ma gaṇas and elements; / Māṇavakākrīḍitaka has va, nau; Halamukhī has va, saḥ;

333.s:
syādbhujaṅgaśiśusūtānau mehanaṃ marutaṃ nanau /
bhavecchuddhavirāḍvṛttaṃ samau jagau //
:p 192
333.d:
स्याद्भुजङ्गशिशुसूतानौ मेहनं मरुतं ननौ /
भवेच्छुद्धविराड्वृत्तं समौ जगौ //
:प् 192
333.m:
Bhujaṅgaśiśusṛtā has nau; nanau is Mehana and Marut; / Śuddhavirāj metre has sa, mau, ja, and gau;
[Page 192]

333.s:
paṇavomalayomaḥ(1) syājjau gau mayūrasāriṇī /
sattāmabhasagā vṛttaṃ bhajatādyuparisthitā //
333.d:
पणवोमलयोमः(1) स्याज्जौ गौ मयूरसारिणी /
सत्तामभसगा वृत्तं भजताद्युपरिस्थिता //
333.m: Paṇava has ma, la, yo, maḥ; Mayūrasāriṇī has jau and gau; / the metre Sattāmabhasagā stands above the first with bha, ja, tā;

333.s:
rukmavatī bhasasagāvindrāvajrā tajau gajau /
jatau jagau gūpapūrvāvādyantādyupajātayaḥ //
333.d:
रुक्मवती भससगाविन्द्रावज्रा तजौ गजौ /
जतौ जगौ गूपपूर्वावाद्यन्ताद्युपजातयः //
333.m: Rukmavatī has bha, sa, sa, gā; Indravajrā has ta, jau, ga, and jau; / when preceded by Upendravajrā with ja, tau, ja, gau, and gū, they form the Upajāti varieties;

333.s:
dodhakaṃ bhagabhāgau syāt śālinī matabhāgagau /
yatiḥ samudrā ṛṣayaḥ vātormī mabhatāgagau //
333.d:
दोधकं भगभागौ स्यात् शालिनी मतभागगौ /
यतिः समुद्रा ऋषयः वातोर्मी मभतागगौ //
333.m: Dodhaka consists of bha, ga, bhā, and gau; Śālinī of ma, ta, bhā, ga, and gau, / with caesura at the oceans [four] and the sages [seven]; Vātormī has ma, bha, tā, ga, and gau;

333.s:
catuḥsvarā syādbhramarī vilāsitā mabhaunalau /
samudrā atha ṛṣayo vanau laugau rathoddhatā //
333.d:
चतुःस्वरा स्याद्भ्रमरी विलासिता मभौनलौ /
समुद्रा अथ ऋषयो वनौ लौगौ रथोद्धता //
333.m: Bhramaravilasitā has four vowels, with ma, bha, u, na, and lau, / [with pause at] oceans and sages; Rathoddhatā has va, nau, lau, and gau.

333.s:
sāmatādhanabhāgogovṛttānanasamāś ca saḥ /
śyenī vajavanāgaḥ syādramyā naparagāgagaḥ //
333.d:
सामताधनभागोगोवृत्ताननसमाश् च सः /
श्येनी वजवनागः स्याद्रम्या नपरगागगः //
333.m: [When it consists of] sa, ma, ta, dha, na, bha, ga, go, [it is known as] the vṛtta Mukhasamā and so on. / Śyenī has va, ja, va, na, ga; Ramyā has na, pa, ra, ga, ga, ga.

333.s:
jagatī vaṃśasthā vṛttaṃ jatau jāvatha tau javau /
indravaṃśā toṭakaṃ saiś caturbhiḥ pratipādataḥ //
333.d:
जगती वंशस्था वृत्तं जतौ जावथ तौ जवौ /
इन्द्रवंशा तोटकं सैश् चतुर्भिः प्रतिपादतः //
333.m: In the Jagatī [class], Vaṃśasthā is the meter [formed by] ja, ta, ja, then ra. Indravaṃśā has ta, ta, ja, ra. / Toṭaka has four sa-gaṇas in each quarter-verse.

333.s:
bhaveddrutavilambitā nabhau bhavāvathau nalau /
syau śrīpuṭho vasuvedā jalogatijalau jamau //
333.d:
भवेद्द्रुतविलम्बिता नभौ भवावथौ नलौ /
स्यौ श्रीपुठो वसुवेदा जलोगतिजलौ जमौ //
333.m: Drutavilambitā has na, bha, bha, ra. Then [the meter with] na, la, / sa, ya is Śrīpuṭa, with the caesura at eight (vasu) and four (veda). Jaloddhatagati has ja, sa, ja, sa; [another has] ja, ma,

333.s:
jasau vasarvavaścātha tataṃ nanamarāḥ smṛtaṃ /
kusumavicitrā nyau dyau nau nau rau syāccalāmbikā(2) //
333.d:
जसौ वसर्ववश्चाथ ततं ननमराः स्मृतं /
कुसुमविचित्रा न्यौ द्यौ नौ नौ रौ स्याच्चलाम्बिका(2) //
333.m: ja, sa, [with the pause at] six (rasa) and six (ṛtu). Then Tata is remembered as na, na, ma, ra. / Kusumavicitrā has na, ya, na, ya. Calāmbikā has na, na, ra, ya.

333.s:
bhujaṅgaprayātaṃ thaiḥ syāccaturbhiḥ sragvinībhavaiḥ /
pramitākṣarā gajau sau kāntotpīḍā matau samau(3) //
333.d:
भुजङ्गप्रयातं थैः स्याच्चतुर्भिः स्रग्विनीभवैः /
प्रमिताक्षरा गजौ सौ कान्तोत्पीडा मतौ समौ(3) //
333.m: Bhujaṅgaprayāta is formed by four ya-gaṇas. Sragviṇī is formed by four ra-gaṇas. / Pramitākṣarā has sa, ja, sa, sa. Kāntotpīḍā has ma, ta, sa, ma.

333.s:
vaiśvadevī(4) mamayāyāḥ pañcāṅgā navamālinī /
:n
1 malaghāga iti kha..
2 caraṇātmikā iti kha.. / cañcalāmbikā iti ṭa..
3 mamāviti kha..
4 viśvadevīti kha
:p 193
najau bhayau pratipādaṃ gaṇā yadi jagatyapi //
333.d:
वैश्वदेवी(4) ममयायाः पञ्चाङ्गा नवमालिनी /
:न्
1 मलघाग इति ख..
2 चरणात्मिका इति ख.. / चञ्चलाम्बिका इति ट..
3 ममाविति ख..
4 विश्वदेवीति ख
:प् 193
नजौ भयौ प्रतिपादं गणा यदि जगत्यपि //
333.m:
Vaiśvadevī has ma, ma, ya, ya, [with pauses at] five and six (aṅga). Navamālinī [has]
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: "malaghāga" according to ms. kha.]
[Footnote 2: "caraṇātmikā" according to ms. kha; "cañcalāmbikā" according to ms. ṭa.]
[Footnote 3: "mamau" according to ms. kha.]
[Footnote 4: "viśvadevī" according to ms. kha.]
na, ja, bha, ya in each quarter-verse, if the gaṇas are in the Jagatī [class].

333.s:
praharṣaṇī mavajavā gopatirvahnidikṣu ca /
rucirā jabhasajagā cchinnā vedair grahaiḥ smṛtā //
333.d:
प्रहर्षणी मवजवा गोपतिर्वह्निदिक्षु च /
रुचिरा जभसजगा च्छिन्ना वेदैर् ग्रहैः स्मृता //
333.m: Praharṣaṇī has ma, na, ja, ra, ga, with [pauses at] three (gopati/vahni) and ten (diś). / Rucirā has ja, bha, sa, ja, ga, split at four (veda) and nine (graha).

333.s:
mattamayūraṃ matayā sagau vedarahe yatiḥ /
gaurīnalanasāgaḥ syādasambādhā natau nagau //
333.d:
मत्तमयूरं मतया सगौ वेदरहे यतिः /
गौरीनलनसागः स्यादसम्बाधा नतौ नगौ //
333.m: Mattamayūra has ma, ta, ya, sa, ga, with a pause at four (veda) and nine (graha). / Gaurī has na, la, na, sa, ga. Asambādhā has ma, ta, na, sa, ga,

333.s:
goga indriyanavakau nanau vasanagāḥ svarāḥ /
svarāścāparājitā syānnanabhānanagāḥ svarāḥ //
333.d:
गोग इन्द्रियनवकौ ननौ वसनगाः स्वराः /
स्वराश्चापराजिता स्यान्ननभाननगाः स्वराः //
333.m: ga, [with pauses at] five (indriya) and nine. [The meter having] na, na, / sa, na, ga has pauses at eight (vasu) and seven (svara). Aparājitā has na, na, bha, na, la, ga, with pauses at seven (svara) [and eight].

333.s:
dviḥpraharaṇakalitā(1) vasantatilakā nabhau /
jau gau siṃhonnatā sā syānmuneruddharṣaṇī ca sā //
333.d:
द्विःप्रहरणकलिता(1) वसन्ततिलका नभौ /
जौ गौ सिंहोन्नता सा स्यान्मुनेरुद्धर्षणी च सा //
333.m: Dvipraharaṇakalitā is [formed by] … Vasantatilakā has ta, bha, / ja, ja, ga, ga; that same [meter] is [called] Siṃhonnati, and it is also [called] Uddharṣaṇī by the sage.

333.s:
candrāvartā nanau somāvartartunavakaḥ smṛtaḥ /
maṇiguṇanikarā sau mālinau nau mayau yayaḥ //
333.d:
चन्द्रावर्ता ननौ सोमावर्तर्तुनवकः स्मृतः /
मणिगुणनिकरा सौ मालिनौ नौ मयौ ययः //
333.m: Candrāvartā has na, na, … Somāvartā is taught with pauses at six (ṛtu) and nine. / Maṇiguṇanikara has sa, ma, [na, na, ya]. Mālinī has na, na, ma, ya, ya,

333.s:
yatirvasusvarā bhau vau natalamitrasagrahāḥ(2) /
ṛṣabhagajavilāsitaṃ jñeyā śikhariṇī jagau //
333.d:
यतिर्वसुस्वरा भौ वौ नतलमित्रसग्रहाः(2) /
ऋषभगजविलासितं ज्ञेया शिखरिणी जगौ //
333.m: with caesura at eight (vasu) and seven (svara). [The meter having] bha, va, na, ta, la, ma, ra, sa, ga, [with pauses at] seven (ṛṣi) and ten (graha) / is known as Ṛṣabhagajavilāsita. Śikhariṇī has ya, ma, na, sa, bha, la, ga,

333.s:
rasabhālabhṛgurudrāḥ pṛthvījasajasā janau /
govasugrahavicchinnā piṅgaleneritā purā //
333.d:
रसभालभृगुरुद्राः पृथ्वीजसजसा जनौ /
गोवसुग्रहविच्छिन्ना पिङ्गलेनेरिता पुरा //
333.m: [with pauses at] six (rasa) and eleven (rudra). Pṛthvī has ja, sa, ja, sa, ya, la, ga, / broken at eight (vasu) and nine (graha), as declared of old by Piṅgala.

333.s:
vaṃśapatrapatitaṃ syād bhavanā bhau nagau sadik /
hariṇī nasamāraḥ so nagau rasacatuḥsvarāḥ //
333.d:
वंशपत्रपतितं स्याद् भवना भौ नगौ सदिक् /
हरिणी नसमारः सो नगौ रसचतुःस्वराः //
333.m: Vaṃśapatrapatita has bha, ra, na, bha, na, la, ga, with [pauses at] ten (dik) [and eight]. / Hariṇī has na, sa, ma, ra, sa, la, ga, with [pauses at] six (rasa), four, and seven (svara).

333.s:
mandākrāntā nabhanataṃ tagaugachirasasvarāḥ /
kusumitalatā vellitā yayayāḥ śarāḥ //
333.d:
मन्दाक्रान्ता नभनतं तगौगछिरसस्वराः /
कुसुमितलता वेल्लिता यययाः शराः //
333.m: Mandākrāntā has ma, bha, na, ta, ta, ga, ga, with [pauses at] four, six (rasa), and seven (svara). / Kusumitalatāvellitā has ma, ta, na, ya, ya, ya, [with pauses at] five (śara),

333.s:
rathāḥ svarāḥ pratirathasasajāḥ satatāś ca gaḥ /
śārdūlavikrīḍitaṃ syādādityamunayo yatiḥ //
:n
1 dviḥpraharaṇañcaliteti kha..
2 lananāgātrasagrahā iti ña..
:p 194
333.d:
रथाः स्वराः प्रतिरथससजाः सतताश् च गः /
शार्दूलविक्रीडितं स्यादादित्यमुनयो यतिः //
:न्
1 द्विःप्रहरणञ्चलितेति ख..
2 लननागात्रसग्रहा इति ञ..
:प् 194
333.m:
six (ratha), and seven (svara). [The meter with] sa, sa, ja, sa, ta, ta, and ga / is Śārdūlavikrīḍita, having its caesura at twelve (āditya) and seven (muni).
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: "dviḥpraharaṇañcalitā" according to ms. kha.]
[Footnote 2: "lananāgātrasagrahāḥ" according to ms. ña.]

333.s:
kṛtiḥ suvadanā moro bhanayā bhanagāḥ surāḥ /
yatirmunirasāścātha iti vṛttaṃ kramāt smṛtam //
333.d:
कृतिः सुवदना मोरो भनया भनगाः सुराः /
यतिर्मुनिरसाश्चाथ इति वृत्तं क्रमात् स्मृतम् //
333.m: In the Kṛti [class], Suvadanā has ma, ra, bha, na, ya, bha, na, ga, [pauses at] seven (muni) and seven (sura), / and then a pause at six (rasa). Thus the meters are taught in succession.

333.s:
snagdharā maratānomoyapau triḥsaptakā yatiḥ /
samudrakaṃ bharajānovanago daśabhāskarāḥ //
333.d:
स्नग्धरा मरतानोमोयपौ त्रिःसप्तका यतिः /
समुद्रकं भरजानोवनगो दशभास्कराः //
333.m: Sragdharā has ma, ra, bha, na, ya, ya, ya, with caesura three times at seven (triḥsaptaka). / Samudraka has bha, ra, ja, no, va, na, ga, [with pauses at] ten and twelve (bhāskara).

333.s:
aśvalalitaṃ najabhā jabhajā bhanamīśataḥ /
mattākrīḍā mamananā naunagnau goṣṭamātithiḥ //
333.d:
अश्वललितं नजभा जभजा भनमीशतः /
मत्ताक्रीडा ममनना नौनग्नौ गोष्टमातिथिः //
333.m: Aśvalalita has na, ja, bha, ja, bha, ja, bha, na, [with pauses at] eleven (īśa) [and twelve]. / Mattākrīḍā has ma, ma, ma, ma, na, na, na, na, ga, ga, [with pauses at] eight (goṣṭha) and fifteen (tithi).

333.s:
tanvī bhanatasābhobho layo vāṇasurārkakāḥ /
krauñcapadā bhamatatā nau nau vāṇaśarāṣṭataḥ //
333.d:
तन्वी भनतसाभोभो लयो वाणसुरार्ककाः /
क्रौञ्चपदा भमतता नौ नौ वाणशराष्टतः //
333.m: Tanvī has bha, na, ta, sa, bha, bha, na, la, ga, [with pauses at] five (vāṇa), eight (sura), and twelve (arka). / Krauñcapadā has bha, ma, sa, bha, na, na, na, na, [with pauses at] five (vāṇa), five (śara), and eight.

333.s:
bhujaṅgavijṛmbhitaṃ mamatanā nanavāsanau /
goṣṭeśamunibhiśchedo hy upahārākhyamīdṛaśam //
333.d:
भुजङ्गविजृम्भितं ममतना ननवासनौ /
गोष्टेशमुनिभिश्छेदो ह्य् उपहाराख्यमीदृअशम् //
333.m: Bhujaṅgavijṛmbhita has ma, ma, ta, na, na, na, ra, sa, la, ga, / with the division at eight (goṣṭha), eleven (īśa), and seven (muni). Such is also named Upahāra.

333.s:
mananānatānaḥ so gagau graharaso rasāt(1) /
nau saptarodaṇḍadaḥ syāccaṇḍavṛṣṭipraghātakaṃ(2) //
333.d:
मननानतानः सो गगौ ग्रहरसो रसात्(1) /
नौ सप्तरोदण्डदः स्याच्चण्डवृष्टिप्रघातकं(2) //
333.m: [The meter having] ma, na, na, na, ta, na, sa, ga, ga, with [pauses at] nine (graha), six (rasa), and six (rasa) / [is named …]. The Daṇḍaka meter having na, na and seven ra-gaṇas is Caṇḍavṛṣṭipraghāta.

333.s:
rephavṛddhyā ṇaṇavā syurvyālajīmūtamukhyakāḥ /
śeṣe vai pracitā jñeyā gāthāprastāra ucyate //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe samavṛttanirūpaṇaṃ nāma
trayastriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha catustriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
prastāranirūpaṇam
333.d:
रेफवृद्ध्या णणवा स्युर्व्यालजीमूतमुख्यकाः /
शेषे वै प्रचिता ज्ञेया गाथाप्रस्तार उच्यते //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे समवृत्तनिरूपणं नाम
त्रयस्त्रिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ चतुस्त्रिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
प्रस्तारनिरूपणम्
333.m:
By increasing the ra-gaṇas, Vyāla, Jīmūta and others are formed. / For the remainder, Pracita should be known. Now the expansion of meters (prastāra) is spoken.
Thus ends the three hundred and thirty-third chapter, named "Description of Even Metres," in the Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Agni.
Now begins the three hundred and thirty-fourth chapter:
Description of the Permutation of Metres (Prastāra)

334.s:
agnir uvāca
chando 'tra siddhaṃ gāthā syāt pāde sarva gurau tathā /
prastāra ādyagāthonaḥ paratulyo 'tha pūrvagaḥ //
:n
1 grahavaso vasāditi ga..
2 caṇḍavṛṣṭiprayānaka iti ṭa..
:p 195
334.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
छन्दो ऽत्र सिद्धं गाथा स्यात् पादे सर्व गुरौ तथा /
प्रस्तार आद्यगाथोनः परतुल्यो ऽथ पूर्वगः //
:न्
1 ग्रहवसो वसादिति ग..
2 चण्डवृष्टिप्रयानक इति ट..
:प् 195
334.m:
Agni said: / A meter established here is a gāthā when all [syllables] in a quarter are heavy (guru). / In the expansion (prastāra), the preceding line is reduced by one [syllable], equal to the subsequent, or precedes it.
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: "grahavaso vasāt" according to ms. ga.]
[Footnote 2: "caṇḍavṛṣṭiprayānaka" according to ms. ṭa.]

334.s:
naṣṭamadhye same 'ṅkenaḥ same 'rdha viṣame guruḥ /
pratilomaguṇaṃ nādyaṃ dviruddiṣṭaga ekanut //
334.d:
नष्टमध्ये समे ऽङ्केनः समे ऽर्ध विषमे गुरुः /
प्रतिलोमगुणं नाद्यं द्विरुद्दिष्टग एकनुत् //
334.m: In determining the lost [form] (naṣṭa), if the number is even, [a light syllable is placed] and it is halved; if odd, a heavy [syllable is placed and one is added]. / Multiplied in reverse order, not the first; doubled for an indicated heavy syllable, removing one.

334.s:
saṅkhyādvirardhe rūpe tu śūnyaṃ śūnye dvirīritaṃ /
tāvadardhatadguṇitaṃ dvidvyūnañca tadantataḥ //
334.d:
सङ्ख्याद्विरर्धे रूपे तु शून्यं शून्ये द्विरीरितं /
तावदर्धतद्गुणितं द्विद्व्यूनञ्च तदन्ततः //
334.m: In the number [process], when halved, [write] two; when one [remains], [write] zero; when zero, it is said to double. / So much is halved, multiplied by that, and diminished two by two until its end.

334.s:
pare pūrṇaṃ pare pūrṇaṃ meruprastārato bhavet /
nagasaṃkhyā vṛttasaṃkhyā cādhvāṅgulamadhordhataḥ /
saṅkhyaiva dviguṇaikonā chandaḥsāro 'yamīritaḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe prastāranirūpaṇaṃ nāma
catustriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha pañcatriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
śikṣānirūpaṇam
334.d:
परे पूर्णं परे पूर्णं मेरुप्रस्तारतो भवेत् /
नगसंख्या वृत्तसंख्या चाध्वाङ्गुलमधोर्धतः /
सङ्ख्यैव द्विगुणैकोना छन्दःसारो ऽयमीरितः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे प्रस्तारनिरूपणं नाम
चतुस्त्रिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ पञ्चत्रिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
शिक्षानिरूपणम्
334.m:
Filled in the subsequent, filled in the subsequent, through the Meru expansion it arises: / the number of meters, the calculation of verses, the distance in finger-breadths from below to above; / the number doubled and diminished by one. This essence of metrics has been declared.
Thus ends the three hundred and thirty-fourth chapter, named "Description of the Permutation of Metres," in the Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Agni.
Now begins the three hundred and thirty-fifth chapter:
Description of Phonetics (Śikṣā)

335.s:
agnir uvāca
vakṣye śikṣāntriṣaṣṭiḥ syurvarṇā vā caturādhikāḥ /
svarā viṃśatirekaś ca sparśānāṃ pañcaviṃśatiḥ //
335.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
वक्ष्ये शिक्षान्त्रिषष्टिः स्युर्वर्णा वा चतुराधिकाः /
स्वरा विंशतिरेकश् च स्पर्शानां पञ्चविंशतिः //
335.m: Agni said: / I shall state the phonetics: the speech-sounds (varṇa) are sixty-three or sixty-four; / the vowels are twenty-one, and the stops (sparśa) are twenty-five;

335.s:
yādayaś ca smṛtā hy aṣṭau catvāraś ca samāḥ smṛtāḥ /
anusvāro visargaś ca paukhyau cāpi parānvitau //
335.d:
यादयश् च स्मृता ह्य् अष्टौ चत्वारश् च समाः स्मृताः /
अनुस्वारो विसर्गश् च पौख्यौ चापि परान्वितौ //
335.m: the eight beginning with ya are taught [as semivowels and sibilants], and four are taught as the neutrals (samāḥ); / the anusvāra and the visarga, and pau and khyau (upadhmānīya and jihvāmūlīya), accompanied by another [sound];

335.s:
duṣpṛṣṭaśceti vijñeyā ḷkāraḥ pluta eva ca /
raṅgaś ca khe araṃ proktaṃ(1) hakāraḥ pañcamair yutaḥ //
335.d:
दुष्पृष्टश्चेति विज्ञेया ऌकारः प्लुत एव च /
रङ्गश् च खे अरं प्रोक्तं(1) हकारः पञ्चमैर् युतः //
335.m: and the duḥspṛṣṭa is to be known as the vowel ḷ and the protracted vowel (pluta); / and the nasalized resonance (raṅga) is declared in the empty space; the letter ha combined with the fifth [nasal consonants],

335.s:
antasthābhiḥ samāyukta aurasyaḥ kaṇṭhya eva saḥ /
ātmabuddhyā samasyarthaṃ manoyukte vivakṣayā //
335.d:
अन्तस्थाभिः समायुक्त औरस्यः कण्ठ्य एव सः /
आत्मबुद्ध्या समस्यर्थं मनोयुक्ते विवक्षया //
335.m: and joined with semivowels, is pectoral (aurasya), but alone it is guttural (kaṇṭhya). / The self, grasping the object with the intellect, sets the mind [to work] with the desire to speak.

335.s:
manaḥ kāyāgnimāhanti sa prerayati mārutam /
:n
1 vargamukhe araṃ proktamiti kha..
:p 196
mārutastūrasi caran mantraṃ(1) janayati svaraṃ //
335.d:
मनः कायाग्निमाहन्ति स प्रेरयति मारुतम् /
:न्
1 वर्गमुखे अरं प्रोक्तमिति ख..
:प् 196
मारुतस्तूरसि चरन् मन्त्रं(1) जनयति स्वरं //
335.m:
The mind strikes the bodily fire, and that [fire] impels the breath (māruta).
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: "vargamukhe araṃ proktam" according to ms. kha.]
The breath, moving in the chest, generates the sacred murmur (mantra) and tone (svara).

335.s:
prātaḥsavanayogastu chando gāyatramāśritam /
kaṇṭhe mādhyandinayutaṃ madhyamantreṣu bhānugam //
335.d:
प्रातःसवनयोगस्तु छन्दो गायत्रमाश्रितम् /
कण्ठे माध्यन्दिनयुतं मध्यमन्त्रेषु भानुगम् //
335.m: In the morning pressing (prātaḥsavana), it is associated with the Gāyatrī meter; / in the throat, it is connected with the midday pressing, following the sun in the intermediate mantras;

335.s:
tārantārtīyasavanaṃ(2) śīrṣaṇyaṃ jāgatānugam /
sodīrṇo mūrdhnyabhihito vakramāpadya mārutaḥ //
335.d:
तारन्तार्तीयसवनं(2) शीर्षण्यं जागतानुगम् /
सोदीर्णो मूर्ध्न्यभिहितो वक्रमापद्य मारुतः //
335.m: in the head, high-pitched, it belongs to the third pressing, following the Jagatī meter. / That breath, having risen and struck against the head, reaches the mouth,

335.s:
varṇān janayate teṣāṃ vibhāgaḥ pañcadhā smṛtaḥ /
svarataḥ kālataḥ sthānāt prayatnārthapradānataḥ //
335.d:
वर्णान् जनयते तेषां विभागः पञ्चधा स्मृतः /
स्वरतः कालतः स्थानात् प्रयत्नार्थप्रदानतः //
335.m: and generates speech-sounds. Their division is remembered as fivefold: / by accent, by duration, by place of articulation, by effort, and by semantic signification.

335.s:
aṣṭau sthānāni varṇānāmuraḥ kaṇṭhaḥ śiras tathā /
jihvāmūlañca dantāś ca nāsikauṣṭhau ca tālu ca //
335.d:
अष्टौ स्थानानि वर्णानामुरः कण्ठः शिरस् तथा /
जिह्वामूलञ्च दन्ताश् च नासिकौष्ठौ च तालु च //
335.m: The eight places of articulation for sounds are the chest, the throat, and the head, / the root of the tongue, the teeth, the nose, the two lips, and the palate.

335.s:
svabhāvaś ca vivṛttiś ca śaṣasā repha eva ca /
jihvāmūlamupadhmā ca gatiraṣṭavidhoṣmaṇaḥ //
335.d:
स्वभावश् च विवृत्तिश् च शषसा रेफ एव च /
जिह्वामूलमुपध्मा च गतिरष्टविधोष्मणः //
335.m: Natural state, hiatus (vivṛtti), śa, ṣa, sa, and r, / the root of the tongue (jihvāmūlīya), and the upadhmānīya: such is the eightfold manifestation of the breath-sounds (ūṣman).

335.s:
padyo bhāvaprasandhānamukārādi parampadaṃ /
svarāntaṃ tādṛśaṃ vidyādyadanyadvyaktamūṣmaṇaḥ //
335.d:
पद्यो भावप्रसन्धानमुकारादि परम्पदं /
स्वरान्तं तादृशं विद्याद्यदन्यद्व्यक्तमूष्मणः //
335.m:
Pertaining to a pāda, the conjunction of states, the supreme word beginning with the letter u—
one should know that which ends in a vowel to be such, which differs from the manifested aspirate.

335.s:
ūtīrthādāgataṃ(3) dagdhamapavarṇañca bhakṣitaṃ /
evamuccāraṇaṃ pāpamevamuccāraṇaṃ śubham //
335.d:
ऊतीर्थादागतं(3) दग्धमपवर्णञ्च भक्षितं /
एवमुच्चारणं पापमेवमुच्चारणं शुभम् //
335.m:
Derived from an unapproved source, burnt, corrupted in sound, or swallowed—
such pronunciation is bad, [whereas] such [proper] pronunciation is auspicious.

335.s:
atīrthādāgataṃ dravyaṃ sāmnāyaṃ suvyavasthitaṃ /
susvareṇa suvaktreṇa prayuktaṃ brahmarājani //
335.d:
अतीर्थादागतं द्रव्यं साम्नायं सुव्यवस्थितं /
सुस्वरेण सुवक्त्रेण प्रयुक्तं ब्रह्मराजनि //
335.m:
Material obtained from a proper tradition, properly arranged together with sacred scripture,
uttered with correct tone and an able mouth among royal sages and Brahmā:

335.s:
na karālo na lamvoṣṭho nāvyakto nānunāsikaḥ /
gadgado bahujihvaś ca na varṇān vaktum arhati //
335.d:
न करालो न लम्वोष्ठो नाव्यक्तो नानुनासिकः /
गद्गदो बहुजिह्वश् च न वर्णान् वक्तुम् अर्हति //
335.m:
One who has protruding teeth, who has pendulous lips, who is indistinct, who is nasal,
who stammers, or who has a multiple tongue is not fit to utter the sounds.

335.s:
evaṃ varṇāḥ prayoktavyā nāvyaktā na ca pīḍintāḥ /
:n
1 mātramiti kha..
2 bhāvantārtīyasavanamiti kha..
3 kutīrthādāgatamiti ṭa.. / kṣatīrthadāgatamiti kha..
:p 197
samyagvarṇaprayogeṇa brahmaloke mahīyate //
335.d:
एवं वर्णाः प्रयोक्तव्या नाव्यक्ता न च पीडिन्ताः /
:न्
1 मात्रमिति ख..
2 भावन्तार्तीयसवनमिति ख..
3 कुतीर्थादागतमिति ट.. / क्षतीर्थदागतमिति ख..
:प् 197
सम्यग्वर्णप्रयोगेण ब्रह्मलोके महीयते //
335.m:
Thus the sounds should be pronounced, neither indistinctly nor compressed.
[Footnote]
1. 'mātraṃ' thus in manuscript kha.
2. 'bhāvantārtīyasavanam' thus in manuscript kha.
3. 'kutīrthādāgatam' thus in manuscript ṭa; 'kṣatīrthadāgatam' thus in manuscript kha. / [p. 197]
Through the proper use of sounds, one is magnified in the world of Brahmā.

335.s:
udāttaścānudāttaś ca svaritaś ca svarāstrayaḥ /
hrasvo dīrghaḥ pluta iti kālato niyamāvadhi //
335.d:
उदात्तश्चानुदात्तश् च स्वरितश् च स्वरास्त्रयः /
ह्रस्वो दीर्घः प्लुत इति कालतो नियमावधि //
335.m:
Acute, grave, and circumflex are the three vowel accents;
short, long, and protracted: thus the limit of regulation according to duration.

335.s:
kaṇṭhyā vahāvicuyaśāstālavyā oṣṭhajā vupu /
syurmūrdhanyā ṛhurasāḥ(1) dantyāḥ ḷ+olasāḥ smṛtāḥ //
335.d:
कण्ठ्या वहाविचुयशास्तालव्या ओष्ठजा वुपु /
स्युर्मूर्धन्या ऋहुरसाः(1) दन्त्याः ऌ+ओलसाः स्मृताः //
335.m:
a, ha, and the guttural class are velar; i, cu, and ya and śa are palatal; u and the labials arise from the lips;
ṛ, the retroflex class, ra, and ṣa are retroflex; ḷ, the dental class, la, and sa are held to be dental.

335.s:
jihvāmūle tu hvaḥ prokto dantyoṣṭho vaḥ smṛto budhaiḥ /
edaitau kaṇṭatālavyau o au kaṇṭhyauṣṭhajau smṛtau //
335.d:
जिह्वामूले तु ह्वः प्रोक्तो दन्त्योष्ठो वः स्मृतो बुधैः /
एदैतौ कण्टतालव्यौ ओ औ कण्ठ्यौष्ठजौ स्मृतौ //
335.m:
The jihvāmūlīya is declared at the root of the tongue; va is considered dentolabial by the wise;
e and ai are palatovelar; o and au are held to be labiovelar.

335.s:
ardhamātrā tu kaṇṭhasya ekāraikārayorbhavet /
ayogavāhā vijñeyā āśrayasthānabhāginaḥ //
335.d:
अर्धमात्रा तु कण्ठस्य एकारैकारयोर्भवेत् /
अयोगवाहा विज्ञेया आश्रयस्थानभागिनः //
335.m:
A half-mora belonging to the throat occurs in the case of e and ai.
The ayogavāhas are to be known as sharing the place of their base sound.

335.s:
aco 'spṛṣṭāpaṇastvīṣannomāḥ spṛṣtā halaḥsmṛtāḥ /
śeṣāḥ spṛṣṭā halaḥ proktā nibodhātra pradhānataḥ //
335.d:
अचो ऽस्पृष्टापणस्त्वीषन्नोमाः स्पृष्ता हलःस्मृताः /
शेषाः स्पृष्टा हलः प्रोक्ता निबोधात्र प्रधानतः //
335.m:
Vowels are uncontacted; semivowels are slightly contacted; consonants are held to be contacted.
The remaining consonants are declared contacted: learn them here primarily.

335.s:
amo 'nunāsikānakrau nādimau hasaṣaḥ smṛtāḥ /
īṣannādopaṇayaśaḥ śvāsinaś ca thakādayaḥ /
īṣacchāsaṃ svaraṃ vidyāddīrghametat pracakṣate //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe śikṣānirūpaṇaṃ nāma
pañcatriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:n
1 khaṭavasā iti kha..
:p 198
:ś atha ṣaṭtriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
kāvyādilakṣaṇaṃ
335.d:
अमो ऽनुनासिकानक्रौ नादिमौ हसषः स्मृताः /
ईषन्नादोपणयशः श्वासिनश् च थकादयः /
ईषच्छासं स्वरं विद्याद्दीर्घमेतत् प्रचक्षते //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे शिक्षानिरूपणं नाम
पञ्चत्रिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:न्
1 खटवसा इति ख..
:प् 198
:श् अथ षट्त्रिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
काव्यादिलक्षणं
335.m:
The nasals are nasal; ha, sa, ṣa are held not to have initial voice;
semivowels have slight voice; tha and the like have breath;
one should know that a vowel has slight breath; they declare this [as] long.
Thus ends the three hundred thirty-fifth chapter, entitled 'Determination of Phonetics', in the Mahāpurāṇa called Āgneya.
[Footnote]
1. 'khaṭavasā' thus in manuscript kha. / [p. 198]
Now begins the three hundred thirty-sixth chapter.
Characteristics of Poetry and the Like

336.s:
agnir uvāca
kāvyasya nāṭakādeś ca alaṅkārān vadāmy atha /
dhvanirvarṇāḥ padaṃ vākyamityetadvāṅmayaṃ mataṃ //
336.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
काव्यस्य नाटकादेश् च अलङ्कारान् वदाम्य् अथ /
ध्वनिर्वर्णाः पदं वाक्यमित्येतद्वाङ्मयं मतं //
336.m:
Agni said:
I shall now state the ornaments of poetry, drama, and the like:
sound, phonemes, word, sentence—such is considered literature.

336.s:
śāstretihāsavākyānāṃ trayaṃ yatra samāpyate /
śāstre śabdapradhānatvamitihāseṣu niṣṭhatā //
336.d:
शास्त्रेतिहासवाक्यानां त्रयं यत्र समाप्यते /
शास्त्रे शब्दप्रधानत्वमितिहासेषु निष्ठता //
336.m:
Where the triad of the statements of technical treatises, legendary histories, and [poetry] is completed:
in a technical treatise, primacy belongs to the word; in legendary histories, adherence [to the meaning].

336.s:
abhidhāyāḥ pradhānatvāt kāvyaṃ tābhyāṃ vibhidyate /
naratvaṃ durlabhaṃ loke vidyā tatra ca durlabhā //
336.d:
अभिधायाः प्रधानत्वात् काव्यं ताभ्यां विभिद्यते /
नरत्वं दुर्लभं लोके विद्या तत्र च दुर्लभा //
336.m:
Because of the primacy of literal expression, poetry differs from both of those.
Human birth is rare in the world, and learning there is rare;

336.s:
kavitvaṃ durlabhaṃ tatra śaktistatra ca durlabhā /
vyutpātirdurlabhā tatra vivekastatra durlabhaḥ //
336.d:
कवित्वं दुर्लभं तत्र शक्तिस्तत्र च दुर्लभा /
व्युत्पातिर्दुर्लभा तत्र विवेकस्तत्र दुर्लभः //
336.m:
poetic faculty is rare there, and innate genius there is rare;
scholarly culture is rare there, and critical discernment is rare there.

336.s:
sarvaṃ śāstramavidvadbhirmṛgyamāṇanna sidhyati /
ādivarṇā dvitīyāś ca mahāprāṇasturīyakaḥ //
336.d:
सर्वं शास्त्रमविद्वद्भिर्मृग्यमाणन्न सिध्यति /
आदिवर्णा द्वितीयाश् च महाप्राणस्तुरीयकः //
336.m:
Any technical treatise sought by the unwise is not mastered.
The first and second sounds [in a class], and the fourth is the aspirated.

336.s:
vargeṣu varṇavṛndaṃ syāt padaṃ suptiḍprabhedataḥ /
saṅkṣepādvākyamiṣṭārthavyavachinnā padābalī //
336.d:
वर्गेषु वर्णवृन्दं स्यात् पदं सुप्तिड्प्रभेदतः /
सङ्क्षेपाद्वाक्यमिष्टार्थव्यवछिन्ना पदाबली //
336.m:
In consonant classes there is a group of sounds; a word consists of nominal and verbal endings;
in brief, a sentence is a series of words delimited by a desired meaning.

336.s:
kāvyaṃ sphuṭadalaṅkāraṃ guṇavaddoṣavarjitam /
yonirvedaś ca lokaś ca siddhamannādayonijaṃ //
336.d:
काव्यं स्फुटदलङ्कारं गुणवद्दोषवर्जितम् /
योनिर्वेदश् च लोकश् च सिद्धमन्नादयोनिजं //
336.m:
Poetry possesses distinct poetic ornaments, is endowed with qualities, and is free from faults.
Its source is the Veda and the world, established, and born from other sources.

336.s:
devādīnām saṃskṛtaṃ syāt prākṛtaṃ trividhaṃ nṛṇāṃ /
gadyaṃ padyañca miśrañca kāvyādi trividhaṃ smṛtam //
336.d:
देवादीनाम् संस्कृतं स्यात् प्राकृतं त्रिविधं नृणां /
गद्यं पद्यञ्च मिश्रञ्च काव्यादि त्रिविधं स्मृतम् //
336.m:
For gods and others it is Sanskrit; for humans it is threefold Prakrit.
Poetry and the like are known to be threefold: prose, verse, and mixed.

336.s:
apadaḥ padasantāno gadyantadapi gadyate /
cūrṇakotkalikāgandhivṛttabhedāt trirūpakam //
336.d:
अपदः पदसन्तानो गद्यन्तदपि गद्यते /
चूर्णकोत्कलिकागन्धिवृत्तभेदात् त्रिरूपकम् //
336.m:
A continuum of words without metrical feet is prose; that too is narrated
as having three forms by distinction of cūrṇaka, utkalikāprāya, and vṛttagandhi.

336.s:
alpālpavigrahaṃ nātimṛdusandarbhanirbharaṃ /
:p 199
cūrṇakaṃ nāmto dīrghasamāsāt kalikā bhavet //
336.d:
अल्पाल्पविग्रहं नातिमृदुसन्दर्भनिर्भरं /
:प् 199
चूर्णकं नाम्तो दीर्घसमासात् कलिका भवेत् //
336.m:
Having very short compounds, not overloaded with overly soft texture,
[p. 199]
it is called cūrṇaka; from long compounds, it is an utkalikā.

336.s:
bhavenmadhyamasandarbhannātikutsitavigraham /
vṛttacchāyāharaṃ vṛttaṃ gandhinaitat kilotkaṭam //
336.d:
भवेन्मध्यमसन्दर्भन्नातिकुत्सितविग्रहम् /
वृत्तच्छायाहरं वृत्तं गन्धिनैतत् किलोत्कटम् //
336.m:
That which has a moderate texture, not overly ugly compounds,
and captures the shadow of a meter is vṛtta[-gandhi]; this indeed is striking.

336.s:
ākhyāyikā kathā khaṇḍakathā parikathā tathā /
kathāniketi manyante gadyakāvyañca pañcadhā //
336.d:
आख्यायिका कथा खण्डकथा परिकथा तथा /
कथानिकेति मन्यन्ते गद्यकाव्यञ्च पञ्चधा //
336.m:
Ākhyāyikā, kathā, khaṇḍakathā, parikathā,
and kathānikā: prose poetry is thus considered to be fivefold.

336.s:
kartṛvaṃśapraśaṃsā syādyatra gadyena vistarāt /
kanyāharaṇasaṃgrāmavipralambhavipattayaḥ //
336.d:
कर्तृवंशप्रशंसा स्याद्यत्र गद्येन विस्तरात् /
कन्याहरणसंग्रामविप्रलम्भविपत्तयः //
336.m:
Where there is praise of the author's lineage at length in prose,
and abductions of maidens, battles, separations, and calamities,

336.s:
bhavanti yatra dīptāś ca rītivṛttipravṛttayaḥ /
ucchāsaiś ca paricchedo yatra yā cūrṇakottarā //
336.d:
भवन्ति यत्र दीप्ताश् च रीतिवृत्तिप्रवृत्तयः /
उच्छासैश् च परिच्छेदो यत्र या चूर्णकोत्तरा //
336.m:
where styles, dramatic manners, and regional usages are radiant,
where division is by chapters, and which abounds in cūrṇaka prose,

336.s:
vaktraṃ vāparavaktraṃ vā yatra sākhyāyikā smṛtā /
ślokaiḥ svavaṃśaṃ saṃkṣepāt kaviryatra praśaṃsati //
336.d:
वक्त्रं वापरवक्त्रं वा यत्र साख्यायिका स्मृता /
श्लोकैः स्ववंशं संक्षेपात् कविर्यत्र प्रशंसति //
336.m:
and where there is a vaktra or aparavaktra [meter], that is known as an ākhyāyikā.
Where the poet praises his own lineage briefly in verses,

336.s:
sukhyasyārthāvatārāya bhavedyatra kathāntaram /
paricchedo na yatra syādbhavedvālambhakaiḥ kvacit //
336.d:
सुख्यस्यार्थावताराय भवेद्यत्र कथान्तरम् /
परिच्छेदो न यत्र स्याद्भवेद्वालम्भकैः क्वचित् //
336.m:
where another story is introduced for introducing the main plot,
where there are no chapter divisions, or sometimes divisions called lambhakas,

336.s:
sā kathā nāma tadgarbhe nibadhnīyāccatuṣpadīṃ /
bhavet khaṇḍakathā yāsau yāsau parikathā tayoḥ //
336.d:
सा कथा नाम तद्गर्भे निबध्नीयाच्चतुष्पदीं /
भवेत् खण्डकथा यासौ यासौ परिकथा तयोः //
336.m:
that is called a kathā; inside it one should compose four-line stanzas.
As for khaṇḍakathā, that which is a parikathā of the two:

336.s:
amātyaṃ sārthakaṃ vāpi dvijaṃ vā nāyakaṃ viduḥ /
syāttayoḥ karuṇaṃ viddhi vipralambhaś caturvidhaḥ //
336.d:
अमात्यं सार्थकं वापि द्विजं वा नायकं विदुः /
स्यात्तयोः करुणं विद्धि विप्रलम्भश् चतुर्विधः //
336.m:
they know the hero to be a minister, a merchant, or a twice-born;
know the pathetic [sentiment] in them, and the fourfold love in separation.

336.s:
samāpyate tayor nādyā sā kathāmanudhāvati /
kathākhyāyikayormiśrabhāvāt parikathā smṛtā //
336.d:
समाप्यते तयोर् नाद्या सा कथामनुधावति /
कथाख्यायिकयोर्मिश्रभावात् परिकथा स्मृता //
336.m:
The first of the two does not reach completion; it follows a kathā.
From the mixture of kathā and ākhyāyikā, it is known as a parikathā.

336.s:
bhayānakaṃ sukhaparaṃ garbhe ca karuṇo rasaḥ /
adbhuto 'nte sukḷptārtho nodāttā sā kathānikā //
336.d:
भयानकं सुखपरं गर्भे च करुणो रसः /
अद्भुतो ऽन्ते सुकॢप्तार्थो नोदात्ता सा कथानिका //
336.m:
Having the terrible [sentiment], ending in happiness, with the pathetic sentiment in the middle,
marvellous at the end, well composed in meaning, not elevated: that is a kathānikā.

336.s:
padyaṃ catuṣpadī tacca vṛttaṃ jātirititridhā /
vṛttamakṣarasaṃkhyeyamukthaṃ tat kṛtiśeṣajam //
:p 200
336.d:
पद्यं चतुष्पदी तच्च वृत्तं जातिरितित्रिधा /
वृत्तमक्षरसंख्येयमुक्थं तत् कृतिशेषजम् //
:प् 200
336.m:
Verse is a four-line stanza, and that is threefold: vṛtta, jāti,
and [miśra]. Vṛtta is counted by syllables, spoken as arising from remnants of kṛti meters.
[p. 200]

336.s:
mātrābhirgaṇanā sā jātiriti kāśyapaḥ(1) /
samamardhasamaṃ vṛttaṃ viṣamaṃ paiṅgalaṃ tridhā //
336.d:
मात्राभिर्गणना सा जातिरिति काश्यपः(1) /
सममर्धसमं वृत्तं विषमं पैङ्गलं त्रिधा //
336.m:
Enumeration by morae is called jāti: thus says Kāśyapa.
Vṛtta is threefold in the system of Piṅgala: even, half-even, and uneven.

336.s:
sā vidyā naustitīṣūrṇāṃ gabhīraṃ kāvyasāgaraṃ /
mahākāvyaṃ kalāpaś ca paryābandho viśeṣakam //
336.d:
सा विद्या नौस्तितीषूर्णां गभीरं काव्यसागरं /
महाकाव्यं कलापश् च पर्याबन्धो विशेषकम् //
336.m:
That science is a boat for those wishing to cross the deep ocean of poetry.
Mahākāvya, kalāpa, paryāyabandha, viśeṣaka,

336.s:
kulakaṃ muktakaṃ koṣa iti padyakuṭumbakam /
sargabandho mahākāvyamārabdhaṃ saṃskṛtena yat //
336.d:
कुलकं मुक्तकं कोष इति पद्यकुटुम्बकम् /
सर्गबन्धो महाकाव्यमारब्धं संस्कृतेन यत् //
336.m:
kulaka, muktaka, and koṣa: this is the family of metrical poetry.
A mahākāvya is composed in cantos, begun in Sanskrit;

336.s:
tādātmyamajahattatra(2) tatsamaṃ nāti duṣyati /
itihāsakathodbhūtamitaradvā sadāśrayaṃ //
336.d:
तादात्म्यमजहत्तत्र(2) तत्समं नाति दुष्यति /
इतिहासकथोद्भूतमितरद्वा सदाश्रयं //
336.m:
words identical to Sanskrit there, not abandoning identity with it, are not very faulty.
It originates from legendary history or from another noble source,

336.s:
mantradūtaprayāṇājiniyataṃ nātivistaram /
śakkaryātijagatyātiśakkaryā triṣṭubhā(3) tathā //
336.d:
मन्त्रदूतप्रयाणाजिनियतं नातिविस्तरम् /
शक्कर्यातिजगत्यातिशक्कर्या त्रिष्टुभा(3) तथा //
336.m:
constrained by counsel, envoys, expeditions, and battles, not excessively diffuse;
with śakkarī, atijagatī, atiśakkarī, and triṣṭubh meters,

336.s:
puṣpitāgrādibhirvakrābhijanaiścārubhiḥ samaiḥ /
muktā(4) tu bhinnavṛttāntā nātisaṃkṣiptasargakam //
336.d:
पुष्पिताग्रादिभिर्वक्राभिजनैश्चारुभिः समैः /
मुक्ता(4) तु भिन्नवृत्तान्ता नातिसंक्षिप्तसर्गकम् //
336.m:
with beautiful, regular [meters] such as puṣpitāgrā and vakra;
loose, yet with varied meters at the end, having cantos that are not overly brief.

336.s:
atiśarkvarikāṣṭibhyāmekasaṅkīrṇakaiḥ paraḥ /
mātrayāpyaparaḥ sargaḥ prāśastyeṣu ca paścimaḥ //
336.d:
अतिशर्क्वरिकाष्टिभ्यामेकसङ्कीर्णकैः परः /
मात्रयाप्यपरः सर्गः प्राशस्त्येषु च पश्चिमः //
336.m:
Another canto may be in atiśakvarī and aṣṭi, or in singular mixed meters;
yet another canto may be in moraic meter; and the last [canto] among the praised ones.

336.s:
kalpo 'tininditastasminviśeṣānādaraḥ satāṃ /
nagarārṇavaśailartu candrārkāśramapādapaiḥ //
336.d:
कल्पो ऽतिनिन्दितस्तस्मिन्विशेषानादरः सतां /
