नगरार्णवशैलर्तु चन्द्रार्काश्रमपादपैः //
336.m:
A scheme that is overly condemned meets with disregard among the wise.
With cities, oceans, mountains, seasons, the moon, the sun, hermitages, trees,

336.s:
udyānasalilakrīḍāmadhupānaratotsavaiḥ /
dūtīvacanavinyāsair asatīcaritādbhūtaiḥ //
336.d:
उद्यानसलिलक्रीडामधुपानरतोत्सवैः /
दूतीवचनविन्यासैर् असतीचरिताद्भूतैः //
336.m:
gardens, water sports, wine-drinking, love-festivals,
arrangements of words of female messengers, wonder at the deeds of unchaste women,

336.s:
tamasā marutāpyanyair vibhāvair atinirbharaiḥ /
:n
1 kaśyapa iti ja.. , ña.. , ṭa.. ca
2 tādarthamajahattatreti ja..
3 anuṣṭubheti ja..
4 vyakteti ña..
:p 201
sarvavṛttipravṛttañca sarvabhāvaprabhāvitam //
336.d:
तमसा मरुताप्यन्यैर् विभावैर् अतिनिर्भरैः /
:न्
1 कश्यप इति ज.. , ञ.. , ट.. च
2 तादर्थमजहत्तत्रेति ज..
3 अनुष्टुभेति ज..
4 व्यक्तेति ञ..
:प् 201
सर्ववृत्तिप्रवृत्तञ्च सर्वभावप्रभावितम् //
336.m:
with darkness, wind, and other fully developed determinants,
[Footnote]
1. 'kaśyapa' thus in manuscripts ja, ña, and ṭa.
2. 'tādarthyamajahattatra' thus in manuscript ja.
3. 'anuṣṭubhā' thus in manuscript ja.
[Variant reading] 4 "vyaktā" in manuscript ña.
[Page 201]
proceeding in all dramatic styles and animated by all emotional states,

336.s:
sarvarītirasaiḥ puṣṭaṃ(1) puṣṭaṅguṇavibhūṣaṇaiḥ /
ata eva mahākāvyaṃ tatkartā ca mahākaviḥ //
336.d:
सर्वरीतिरसैः पुष्टं(1) पुष्टङ्गुणविभूषणैः /
अत एव महाकाव्यं तत्कर्ता च महाकविः //
336.m: nourished by all diction styles and aesthetic sentiments, nourished by the ornaments of poetic qualities— / for this reason it is a great epic poem, and its author is a great poet.

336.s:
vāgvaidagdhyapradhānepi rasa evātra jīvitam /
pṛthakprayatnanirvartyaṃ vāgvakrimni rasādvapuḥ //
336.d:
वाग्वैदग्ध्यप्रधानेपि रस एवात्र जीवितम् /
पृथक्प्रयत्ननिर्वर्त्यं वाग्वक्रिम्नि रसाद्वपुः //
336.m: Although witty verbal ingenuity is predominant, aesthetic sentiment alone is its life here; / in crookedness of speech, its body is produced from aesthetic sentiment by a separate effort.

336.s:
caturvargaphalaṃ viśvagvyākhyātaṃ nāyakākhyayā /
samānavṛttinirvyūṭaḥ kauśikīvṛttikomalaḥ //
336.d:
चतुर्वर्गफलं विश्वग्व्याख्यातं नायकाख्यया /
समानवृत्तिनिर्व्यूटः कौशिकीवृत्तिकोमलः //
336.m: Yielding the fruit of the four goals of life, comprehensively explained by the title of the hero, / composed in uniform metres, delicate through the playful dramatic style,

336.s:
kalāpo 'tra pravāsaḥ prāganurāgāhvayo rasaḥ /
saviśeṣakañca prāptyādi saṃskṛtenetreṇa ca //
336.d:
कलापो ऽत्र प्रवासः प्रागनुरागाह्वयो रसः /
सविशेषकञ्च प्राप्त्यादि संस्कृतेनेत्रेण च //
336.m: wherein the aesthetic sentiment named love in separation preceded by mutual attraction is an aggregate, / with distinctive features such as attainment [of the objective], in Sanskrit and other languages.

336.s:
ślokair anekaiḥ kulakaṃ syāt sandānitakāni tat /
muktakaṃ śloka ekaikaś camatkārakṣamaḥ satā ṃ //
336.d:
श्लोकैर् अनेकैः कुलकं स्यात् सन्दानितकानि तत् /
मुक्तकं श्लोक एकैकश् चमत्कारक्षमः सता ं //
336.m: A syntactic group consisting of multiple verses is a kulaka, or it may be a sandānitaka; / a solitary verse capable of causing wonder to the wise is a muktaka.

336.s:
sūktibhiḥ kavisiṃhānāṃ sundarībhiḥ samanvitaḥ /
koṣo brahmāparicchinnaḥ sa vidagdhāya rocate //
336.d:
सूक्तिभिः कविसिंहानां सुन्दरीभिः समन्वितः /
कोषो ब्रह्मापरिच्छिन्नः स विदग्धाय रोचते //
336.m: Endowed with beautiful eloquent sayings of lion-like poets, / a treasury uncircumscribed like Brahmā pleases the cultured connoisseur.

336.s:
ābhāsopamaśaktiś ca sarge yadbhinnavṛttatā /
miśraṃ vapuriti khyātaṃ prakīrṇamiti ca dvidhā /
śravyañcaivābhineyañca prakīrṇaṃ sakaloktibhiḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe alaṅkāre kāvyādilakṣaṇaṃ nāma
ṣaṭtriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:n
1 juṣṭamiti ja.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 202
:ś atha saptatriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
nāṭakanirūpaṇam
336.d:
आभासोपमशक्तिश् च सर्गे यद्भिन्नवृत्तता /
मिश्रं वपुरिति ख्यातं प्रकीर्णमिति च द्विधा /
श्रव्यञ्चैवाभिनेयञ्च प्रकीर्णं सकलोक्तिभिः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे अलङ्कारे काव्यादिलक्षणं नाम
षट्त्रिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:न्
1 जुष्टमिति ज.. , ट.. च
:प् 202
:श् अथ सप्तत्रिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
नाटकनिरूपणम्
336.m:
And the power of apparent simile, the change of metre within a canto: / the mixed form is known as twofold, called miscellaneous, / to be heard and to be enacted, miscellaneous with all manners of expression.
Thus ends the three hundred and thirty-sixth chapter, named "Definition of Poetry and so forth" under Poetics, in the great Agni Purāṇa.
[Footnote]
1 "juṣṭam" in manuscripts ja and ṭa.
[Page 202]
Now begins the three hundred and thirty-seventh chapter:
Examination of Drama.

337.s:
agnir uvāca
nāṭakaṃ saprakaraṇaṃ ḍima īhāmṛgo 'pi vā /
jñeyaḥ samavakāraś ca bhavet prahasanantathā //
337.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
नाटकं सप्रकरणं डिम ईहामृगो ऽपि वा /
ज्ञेयः समवकारश् च भवेत् प्रहसनन्तथा //
337.m: Agni said: / The nāṭaka, along with the prakaraṇa, the ḍima, or the īhāmṛga, / the samavakāra should be known, and likewise the prahasana,

337.s:
vyāyogabhāṇavīthyaṅkatroṭakānyatha nāṭikā /
saṭṭakaṃ śilpakaḥ karṇā eko durmallikā tathā //
337.d:
व्यायोगभाणवीथ्यङ्कत्रोटकान्यथ नाटिका /
सट्टकं शिल्पकः कर्णा एको दुर्मल्लिका तथा //
337.m: the vyāyoga, bhāṇa, vīthī, aṅka, and troṭakas; then the nāṭikā, / saṭṭaka, śilpaka, karṇā, one durmallikā, likewise

337.s:
prasthānaṃ bhāṇikā bhāṇī goṣṭhī hallīśakāni ca /
kāvyaṃ śrīgaditaṃ nāṭyarāsakaṃ rāsakaṃ tathā //
337.d:
प्रस्थानं भाणिका भाणी गोष्ठी हल्लीशकानि च /
काव्यं श्रीगदितं नाट्यरासकं रासकं तथा //
337.m: the prasthāna, bhāṇikā, bhāṇī, goṣṭhī, and hallīśakas, / the kāvya, śrīgadita, nāṭyarāsaka, and likewise the rāsaka,

337.s:
ullāpyakaṃ preṅkṣaṇañca saptaviṃśatireva tat /
sāmānyañca viśeṣaś ca lakṣaṇasya dvayī gatiḥ //
337.d:
उल्लाप्यकं प्रेङ्क्षणञ्च सप्तविंशतिरेव तत् /
सामान्यञ्च विशेषश् च लक्षणस्य द्वयी गतिः //
337.m: the ullāpyaka, and the preṅkṣaṇa—these are indeed twenty-seven. / The scope of their definition has a two-fold course: general and specific.

337.s:
sāmānyaṃ sarvaviṣayaṃ śeṣaḥ kvāpi pravartate /
pūrvaraṅge nivṛtte dvau deśakālāvubhāvapi //
337.d:
सामान्यं सर्वविषयं शेषः क्वापि प्रवर्तते /
पूर्वरङ्गे निवृत्ते द्वौ देशकालावुभावपि //
337.m: The general applies to all, the rest functions somewhere [specifically]. / When the preliminary rites have ceased, both place and time,

337.s:
rasabhāvavibhāvānubhāvā abhinayās tathā /
aṅkaḥ sthitiś ca sāmānyaṃ sarvatraivopasarpaṇāt //
337.d:
रसभावविभावानुभावा अभिनयास् तथा /
अङ्कः स्थितिश् च सामान्यं सर्वत्रैवोपसर्पणात् //
337.m: aesthetic sentiment, emotional states, excitant determinants, consequent expressions, and likewise dramatic representations, / the act, and the structural situation—these are general, since they apply everywhere.

337.s:
viśeṣo 'vasare vācyaḥ sāmānyaṃ pūrvamucyate /
trivargasādhanannāṭyamityāhuḥ karaṇañca yat //
337.d:
विशेषो ऽवसरे वाच्यः सामान्यं पूर्वमुच्यते /
त्रिवर्गसाधनन्नाट्यमित्याहुः करणञ्च यत् //
337.m: The specific is to be stated at the appropriate occasion; the general is stated first. / Drama is said to be the means of accomplishing the three goals of life, and that which is its procedure,

337.s:
itikartavyatā tasya pūrvaraṅgo yathāvidhi /
nāndīmukhāni dvātriṃśadaṅgāni pūrvaraṅgake //
337.d:
इतिकर्तव्यता तस्य पूर्वरङ्गो यथाविधि /
नान्दीमुखानि द्वात्रिंशदङ्गानि पूर्वरङ्गके //
337.m: its mandatory duty is the preliminary rite according to rule; / in the preliminary rite there are thirty-two elements beginning with the benediction.

337.s:
devatānāṃ namaskāro gurūṇāmapi ca stutiḥ /
gobrāhmaṇanṛpādīnāmāśīrvādādi gīyate //
337.d:
देवतानां नमस्कारो गुरूणामपि च स्तुतिः /
गोब्राह्मणनृपादीनामाशीर्वादादि गीयते //
337.m: Homage to deities, praise of preceptors, / and a blessing for cows, brāhmaṇas, kings, and others are sung.

337.s:
nāndyante sūtradhāro 'sau rūpakeṣu nibadhyate /
gurupūrvakramaṃ vaṃśapraśaṃsā pauruṣaṃ kaveḥ //
:p 203
337.d:
नान्द्यन्ते सूत्रधारो ऽसौ रूपकेषु निबध्यते /
गुरुपूर्वक्रमं वंशप्रशंसा पौरुषं कवेः //
:प् 203
337.m:
At the conclusion of the benediction, the stage director is introduced in theatrical compositions: / the succession of teachers, praise of the lineage, the prowess of the poet,
[Page 203]

337.s:
sambandhārthau ca kāvyasya pañcaitāneṣa nirdiśet /
naṭī vidūṣako vāpi pāripārśvika eva vā //
337.d:
सम्बन्धार्थौ च काव्यस्य पञ्चैतानेष निर्दिशेत् /
नटी विदूषको वापि पारिपार्श्विक एव वा //
337.m: and the subject-matter and purpose of the work: these five he should point out. / When an actress, or a jester, or indeed an assistant,

337.s:
sahitāḥ sūtradhāreṇa saṃlāpaṃ yatra kurvate /
citrair vākyaiḥ svakāryotthaiḥ prastutākṣepibhirmithaḥ //
337.d:
सहिताः सूत्रधारेण संलापं यत्र कुर्वते /
चित्रैर् वाक्यैः स्वकार्योत्थैः प्रस्तुताक्षेपिभिर्मिथः //
337.m: together with the stage director, hold a conversation / with multifaceted remarks arising from their own concerns, mutually hinting at the matter at hand,

337.s:
āmukhaṃ tattu vijñeyaṃ budhaiḥ prastāvanāpi sā /
pravṛttakaṃ kathodghātaḥ prayogātiśayas tathā //
337.d:
आमुखं तत्तु विज्ञेयं बुधैः प्रस्तावनापि सा /
प्रवृत्तकं कथोद्घातः प्रयोगातिशयस् तथा //
337.m: that should be known by the wise as the prologue, and it is also called the prelude. / The incident entrance, the abrupt opening, and the heightened presentation:

337.s:
āmukhasya trayo bhedā vījāṃśeṣūpajāyate /
kālaṃ pravṛttamāśritya sūtradhṛgyatra varṇayet //
337.d:
आमुखस्य त्रयो भेदा वीजांशेषूपजायते /
कालं प्रवृत्तमाश्रित्य सूत्रधृग्यत्र वर्णयेत् //
337.m: these are the three varieties of the prologue; it arises in connection with portions of the germinal plot. / Where the stage director describes [something] having taken recourse to an ongoing season,

337.s:
tadāśrayaś ca pātrasya praveśastat pravṛttakaṃ /
sūtradhārasya vākyaṃ vā yatra vākyārthameva vā //
337.d:
तदाश्रयश् च पात्रस्य प्रवेशस्तत् प्रवृत्तकं /
सूत्रधारस्य वाक्यं वा यत्र वाक्यार्थमेव वा //
337.m: and the entrance of a character takes support from that, it is the incident entrance. / Where the words of the stage director, or the meaning of his statement,

337.s:
gṛhītvā praviśet pātraṃ kathodghātaḥ sa ucyate /
prayogeṣu prayogantu sūtradhṛgyatra varṇayet //
337.d:
गृहीत्वा प्रविशेत् पात्रं कथोद्घातः स उच्यते /
प्रयोगेषु प्रयोगन्तु सूत्रधृग्यत्र वर्णयेत् //
337.m:
When [a character] enters taking up the word or sense of the stage manager's speech, that is called kathodghāta (the opening of the story).
Where the stage manager mentions an action among actions,

337.s:
tataś ca praviśet pātraṃ prayogātiśayo hi saḥ /
śarīraṃ nāṭakādīnāmitivṛttaṃ pracakṣate //
337.d:
ततश् च प्रविशेत् पात्रं प्रयोगातिशयो हि सः /
शरीरं नाटकादीनामितिवृत्तं प्रचक्षते //
337.m:
and from that a character enters, that indeed is prayogātiśaya (excess of performance).
The plot is declared to be the body of dramas and other forms.

337.s:
siddhamutprekṣitañceti tasya bhedābubhau smṛtau /
siddhamāgamadṛṣṭañca sṛṣṭamutprekṣitaṃ kaveḥ //
337.d:
सिद्धमुत्प्रेक्षितञ्चेति तस्य भेदाबुभौ स्मृतौ /
सिद्धमागमदृष्टञ्च सृष्टमुत्प्रेक्षितं कवेः //
337.m:
Both of its divisions are remembered as established and invented:
the established is seen in tradition, and the invented is created by the poet.

337.s:
vījaṃ vinduḥ patākā ca prakarī kāryameva ca /
arthaprakṛtayaḥ pañca pañca ceṣṭā api kramāt //
337.d:
वीजं विन्दुः पताका च प्रकरी कार्यमेव च /
अर्थप्रकृतयः पञ्च पञ्च चेष्टा अपि क्रमात् //
337.m:
The seed (vīja), the drop (bindu), the episodic plot (patākā), the episodic incident (prakarī), and the action (kārya)
are the five elements of the plot (arthaprakṛti); and in order there are five stages of action (ceṣṭā):

337.s:
prārambhaś ca prayatnaś ca prāptiḥ sadbhāva eva ca /
niyatā ca phalaprāptiḥ phalayogaś ca pañcamaḥ //
337.d:
प्रारम्भश् च प्रयत्नश् च प्राप्तिः सद्भाव एव च /
नियता च फलप्राप्तिः फलयोगश् च पञ्चमः //
337.m:
Beginning (prārambha), effort (prayatna), possibility of attainment (prāptisadbhāva),
certainty of attainment (niyatā phalaprāpti), and the fifth is the attainment of the fruit (phalayoga).

337.s:
mukhaṃ pratimukhaṃ garbho vimarṣaś ca tathaiva ca /
tathā nirvahaṇañceti kramāt pañcaiva sandhayaḥ //
337.d:
मुखं प्रतिमुखं गर्भो विमर्षश् च तथैव च /
तथा निर्वहणञ्चेति क्रमात् पञ्चैव सन्धयः //
337.m:
The opening (mukha), progression (pratimukha), development (garbha), and pause (vimarṣa),
and similarly the conclusion (nirvahaṇa): these are precisely the five junctures (sandhi) in order.

337.s:
alpamātraṃ samuddiṣṭaṃ bahudhā yat prasarpati /
:p 204
phalāvasānaṃ yaccaiva vījaṃ tadabhidhīyate //
337.d:
अल्पमात्रं समुद्दिष्टं बहुधा यत् प्रसर्पति /
:प् 204
फलावसानं यच्चैव वीजं तदभिधीयते //
337.m:
That which is indicated in only small measure, spreads out manifoldly,
[Page 204]
and terminates in the fruit, is called the seed (vīja).

337.s:
yatra vījasamutpattirnānārtharasasambhavā /
kāvye śarīrānugataṃ tanmukhaṃ parikīrtitaṃ //
337.d:
यत्र वीजसमुत्पत्तिर्नानार्थरससम्भवा /
काव्ये शरीरानुगतं तन्मुखं परिकीर्तितं //
337.m:
Where the origin of the seed arises, possessing various purposes and sentiments,
accompanying the body of the poetic work, that is proclaimed as the opening (mukha).

337.s:
iṣṭasyārthasya racanā vṛttāntasyānupakṣayaḥ /
rāgaprāptiḥ prayogasya guhyānāñcaiva gūhanam //
337.d:
इष्टस्यार्थस्य रचना वृत्तान्तस्यानुपक्षयः /
रागप्राप्तिः प्रयोगस्य गुह्यानाञ्चैव गूहनम् //
337.m:
Arrangement of the desired purpose, non-destruction of the narrative,
attainment of interest in the performance, concealment of what is to be concealed,

337.s:
āś caryavadabhikhyātaṃ prakāśānāṃ prakāśanam /
aṅgahīnaṃ naro yadvanna śreṣṭhaṃ kāvyameva ca //
337.d:
आश् चर्यवदभिख्यातं प्रकाशानां प्रकाशनम् /
अङ्गहीनं नरो यद्वन्न श्रेष्ठं काव्यमेव च //
337.m:
wondrous disclosure, manifestation of what is manifest:
just as a person lacking limbs is not excellent, so is a poetic work [without the junctures].

337.s:
deśakālau vinā kiñcinnetivṛttaṃ pravartate /
atastayorupādānaniyamāt padamucyate //
337.d:
देशकालौ विना किञ्चिन्नेतिवृत्तं प्रवर्तते /
अतस्तयोरुपादाननियमात् पदमुच्यते //
337.m:
No plot proceeds without place and time;
therefore, following the rule of adopting both, their position is stated:

337.s:
deśeṣu bhārataṃ varṣaṃ kāle kṛtayugatrayaṃ /
narte tābhyāṃ prāṇabhṛtāṃ sukhaduḥkhodayaḥ kvacit /
sarge sargādivārtā ca prasajjantī na duṣyati //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe alaṅkāre nāṭakanirūpaṇaṃ nāma
saptatriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś athāṣṭatriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
śṛṅgārādirasanirūpaṇam
337.d:
देशेषु भारतं वर्षं काले कृतयुगत्रयं /
नर्ते ताभ्यां प्राणभृतां सुखदुःखोदयः क्वचित् /
सर्गे सर्गादिवार्ता च प्रसज्जन्ती न दुष्यति //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे अलङ्कारे नाटकनिरूपणं नाम
सप्तत्रिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथाष्टत्रिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
शृङ्गारादिरसनिरूपणम्
337.m:
among places, the land of Bhārata; in time, the triad of ages beginning with the Kṛta age;
without these two, there is never any arising of happiness and suffering for living beings.
In a creation, mention of the origin of creation and the like is connected without defect.
Thus in the great Agni Purāṇa, in the [section on] poetics, the thirty-seventh chapter above three hundred, entitled "Description of Drama."
Now the thirty-eighth chapter above three hundred.
Description of the sentiments beginning with the erotic (śṛṅgāra).

338.s:
agnir uvāca
akṣaraṃ paramaṃ brahma sanātanamajaṃ vibhuṃ /
vedānteṣu vadantyekaṃ caitanyaṃ jyotirīśvaram //
338.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
अक्षरं परमं ब्रह्म सनातनमजं विभुं /
वेदान्तेषु वदन्त्येकं चैतन्यं ज्योतिरीश्वरम् //
338.m:
Agni said:
The imperishable, supreme Brahman, eternal, unborn, omnipresent,
in the Upaniṣads they speak of as one consciousness, light, the Lord.

338.s:
ānandaḥ sahajastasya vyajyate sa kadācana /
vyaktiḥ sā tasya caitanyacamatkārarasāhvayā //
:p 205
338.d:
आनन्दः सहजस्तस्य व्यज्यते स कदाचन /
व्यक्तिः सा तस्य चैतन्यचमत्काररसाह्वया //
:प् 205

338.s:
ādyastasya vikāro yaḥ so 'haṅkāra iti smṛtaḥ /
tato 'bhimānastatredaṃ samāptaṃ bhuvanatrayaṃ //
338.d:
आद्यस्तस्य विकारो यः सो ऽहङ्कार इति स्मृतः /
ततो ऽभिमानस्तत्रेदं समाप्तं भुवनत्रयं //
338.m:
His first modification is remembered as ego-sense (ahaṅkāra);
from that comes self-regard (abhimāna), in which these three worlds are contained.

338.s:
abhimānādratiḥ sā ca paripoṣamupeyuṣī /
vyabhicāryādisāmānyāt śṛṅgāra iti gīyate //
338.d:
अभिमानाद्रतिः सा च परिपोषमुपेयुषी /
व्यभिचार्यादिसामान्यात् शृङ्गार इति गीयते //
338.m:
From self-regard comes pleasure (rati), and that, attaining full nourishment,
is called the erotic (śṛṅgāra) through association with transitory states and the like.

338.s:
tadbhedāḥ kāmamitare hāsyādyā apyanekaśaḥ /
svasvasthādiviśeṣotthaparighoṣasvalakṣaṇāḥ //
338.d:
तद्भेदाः काममितरे हास्याद्या अप्यनेकशः /
स्वस्वस्थादिविशेषोत्थपरिघोषस्वलक्षणाः //
338.m:
Its divisions are desire, and the others—the comic (hāsya) and the rest, manifoldly,
characterized by their own sounds arising from their respective states and distinctions.

338.s:
sattvādiguṇasantānājjāyante paramātmanaḥ /
rāgādbhavati śṛṅgāro raudrastaikṣṇāt prajāyate //
338.d:
सत्त्वादिगुणसन्तानाज्जायन्ते परमात्मनः /
रागाद्भवति शृङ्गारो रौद्रस्तैक्ष्णात् प्रजायते //
338.m:
They arise from the series of qualities such as sattva belonging to the Supreme Self:
the erotic arises from passion (rāga); the furious (raudra) arises from sharpness;

338.s:
vīro 'vaṣṭambhajaḥ saṅkocabhūrvībhatsa iṣyate /
śṛṅgārājjyāyate hāso raudrāttu karuṇo rasaḥ //
338.d:
वीरो ऽवष्टम्भजः सङ्कोचभूर्वीभत्स इष्यते /
शृङ्गाराज्ज्यायते हासो रौद्रात्तु करुणो रसः //
338.m:
the heroic (vīra) is born of resolve; the odious (vībhatsa) is held to arise from revulsion;
from the erotic is born the comic; from the furious comes the pathetic sentiment (karuṇa rasa);

338.s:
vīrāccādbhutaniṣpattiḥ syādvībhatsādbhayānakaḥ /
śṛṅgārahāsyakaruṇā raudravīrabhayānakāḥ //
338.d:
वीराच्चाद्भुतनिष्पत्तिः स्याद्वीभत्साद्भयानकः /
शृङ्गारहास्यकरुणा रौद्रवीरभयानकाः //
338.m:
from the heroic arises the marvelous (adbhuta); from the odious comes the terrible (bhayānaka).
The erotic, comic, pathetic, furious, heroic, terrible,

338.s:
vībhatsādbhutaśāntākhyāḥ svabhāvāccaturo rasāḥ /
lakṣmīriva vinā tyāgānna vāṇī bhāti nīrasā //
338.d:
वीभत्साद्भुतशान्ताख्याः स्वभावाच्चतुरो रसाः /
लक्ष्मीरिव विना त्यागान्न वाणी भाति नीरसा //
338.m:
odious, marvelous, and that named peaceful (śānta)—[these are] four sentiments by natural origin.
Speech devoid of sentiment does not shine, just as Lakṣmī does not shine without generosity.

338.s:
apāre kāvyasaṃsāre kavireva prajāpatiḥ /
yathā vai rocate viśvaṃ tathedaṃ parivartate //
338.d:
अपारे काव्यसंसारे कविरेव प्रजापतिः /
यथा वै रोचते विश्वं तथेदं परिवर्तते //
338.m:
In the boundless world of poetry, the poet alone is the creator (Prajāpati);
as it pleases him, so indeed this universe revolves.

338.s:
śṛṅgārī cet kaviḥ kāvye jātaṃ rasamayaṃ jagat /
sa cet kavirvītarāgo nīrasaṃ vyaktameva tat //
338.d:
शृङ्गारी चेत् कविः काव्ये जातं रसमयं जगत् /
स चेत् कविर्वीतरागो नीरसं व्यक्तमेव तत् //
338.m:
If the poet is full of love, the world in his poem is full of aesthetic sentiment;
if that poet is free from passion, it is plainly devoid of sentiment.

338.s:
na bhāvahīno 'sti raso na bhāvo rasavarjitaḥ /
bhāvayanti rasānebhirbhāvyante ca rasā iti //
338.d:
न भावहीनो ऽस्ति रसो न भावो रसवर्जितः /
भावयन्ति रसानेभिर्भाव्यन्ते च रसा इति //
338.m:
There is no aesthetic sentiment without a state (bhāva), nor a state devoid of sentiment;
they bring about the sentiments by these, and [thus] sentiments are brought about.

338.s:
sthāyino 'ṣṭau ratimukhāḥ stambhādyā vyabhicāriṇaḥ /
mano 'nukūle 'nubhavaḥ sukhasya ratiriṣyate //
338.d:
स्थायिनो ऽष्टौ रतिमुखाः स्तम्भाद्या व्यभिचारिणः /
मनो ऽनुकूले ऽनुभवः सुखस्य रतिरिष्यते //
338.m:
The dominant states (sthāyin) are eight, beginning with love (rati); those beginning with paralysis (stambha) are transitory states (vyabhicārin).
Experience of happiness in harmony with the mind is regarded as love.

338.s:
harṣādibhiś ca manaso vikāśo hāsa ucyate /
:p 206
citrādidarśanāccetovaiklavyaṃ bruvate bhayam //
338.d:
हर्षादिभिश् च मनसो विकाशो हास उच्यते /
:प् 206
चित्रादिदर्शनाच्चेतोवैक्लव्यं ब्रुवते भयम् //

338.s:
jugupsā ca padārthānāṃ nindā daurbhāgyavāhināṃ /
vismayo 'tiśayenārthadarśanāccittavistṛtiḥ //
338.d:
जुगुप्सा च पदार्थानां निन्दा दौर्भाग्यवाहिनां /
विस्मयो ऽतिशयेनार्थदर्शनाच्चित्तविस्तृतिः //
338.m:
Disgust (jugupsā) is the condemnation of objects that convey misfortune;
wonder (vismaya) is the expansion of the mind from seeing an extraordinary object.

338.s:
aṣṭau stambhādayaḥ sattvādrajasastamasaḥ param /
stambhaśceṣṭāpratīghāto bhayarāgādyupāhitaḥ(1) //
338.d:
अष्टौ स्तम्भादयः सत्त्वाद्रजसस्तमसः परम् /
स्तम्भश्चेष्टाप्रतीघातो भयरागाद्युपाहितः(1) //
338.m:
The eight beginning with paralysis arise from sattva, rajas, and then tamas:
paralysis is obstruction of movement caused by fear, passion, and the like.

338.s:
śramarāgādyupetāntaḥkṣobhajanma vapurjalaṃ /
svedo harṣādibhirdehocchāso 'ntaḥpulakodgamaḥ //
338.d:
श्रमरागाद्युपेतान्तःक्षोभजन्म वपुर्जलं /
स्वेदो हर्षादिभिर्देहोच्छासो ऽन्तःपुलकोद्गमः //
338.m:
Sweat (sveda) is body-water born of inner agitation combined with fatigue, passion, and the like;
horripilation is the swelling of the body through joy and the like, the arising of inner bristling of hair.

338.s:
harṣādijanmavāksaṅgaḥ svarabhedo bhayādibhiḥ /
manovaiklavyamicchanti śokamiṣṭakṣayādibhiḥ //
338.d:
हर्षादिजन्मवाक्सङ्गः स्वरभेदो भयादिभिः /
मनोवैक्लव्यमिच्छन्ति शोकमिष्टक्षयादिभिः //
338.m:
Obstruction of speech born of joy and the like [is stammering]; change of voice (svarabheda) is from fear and the like;
they consider sorrow (śoka) to be distress of the mind from the destruction of what is dear and the like.

338.s:
krodhastaikṣṇaprabodhaś ca pratikūlānukāriṇi /
puruṣārthasamāptyārtho yaḥ sa utsāha ucyate //
338.d:
क्रोधस्तैक्ष्णप्रबोधश् च प्रतिकूलानुकारिणि /
पुरुषार्थसमाप्त्यार्थो यः स उत्साह उच्यते //
338.m:
Anger (krodha) is an awakening of sharpness toward one who acts adversely;
energy (utsāha) is that which has for its purpose the completion of the aims of life.

338.s:
cittakṣobhabhavottambho vepathuḥ parikīrtitaḥ /
vaivarṇyañca viṣādādijanmā kāntiviparyayaḥ //
338.d:
चित्तक्षोभभवोत्तम्भो वेपथुः परिकीर्तितः /
वैवर्ण्यञ्च विषादादिजन्मा कान्तिविपर्ययः //
338.m:
Trembling (vepathu) is proclaimed to be agitation arising from mental disturbance;
change of colour (vaivarṇya) is the reverse of radiance born of dejection and the like.

338.s:
duḥkhānandādijannetrajalamaśru ca viśrutam /
indrayāṇāmastamayaḥ pralayo laṅghanādibhiḥ //
338.d:
दुःखानन्दादिजन्नेत्रजलमश्रु च विश्रुतम् /
इन्द्रयाणामस्तमयः प्रलयो लङ्घनादिभिः //
338.m:
Tears (aśru) are renowned as eye-water born of sorrow, joy, and the like;
fainting (pralaya) is the cessation of the senses due to fasting and the like.

338.s:
vairāgyādirmanaḥkhedo nirveda iti kathyate /
manaḥpīḍādijanmā ca sādo glāniḥ śarīragā //
338.d:
वैराग्यादिर्मनःखेदो निर्वेद इति कथ्यते /
मनःपीडादिजन्मा च सादो ग्लानिः शरीरगा //
338.m:
Dejection of mind from detachment and the like is called self-disparagement (nirveda);
languor (glāni) in the body is exhaustion arising from mental pain and the like.

338.s:
śaṅkāniṣṭāgamotprekṣā syādasūyā ca matsaraḥ /
madirādyupayogotthaṃ manaḥsaṃmohanaṃ madaḥ //
338.d:
शङ्कानिष्टागमोत्प्रेक्षा स्यादसूया च मत्सरः /
मदिराद्युपयोगोत्थं मनःसंमोहनं मदः //
338.m:
Apprehension (śaṅkā) is the anticipation of unwanted arrival; envy (asūyā) is jealousy;
intoxication (mada) is mental stupefaction arising from the consumption of wine and the like.

338.s:
kriyātiśayajanmāntaḥśarīrotthaklamaḥ śramaḥ /
śṛṅgārādikriyādveṣaścittasyālasyamucyate //
:n
1 bhayarāgādyupasthita iti kha..
:p 207
338.d:
क्रियातिशयजन्मान्तःशरीरोत्थक्लमः श्रमः /
शृङ्गारादिक्रियाद्वेषश्चित्तस्यालस्यमुच्यते //
:न्
1 भयरागाद्युपस्थित इति ख..
:प् 207
338.m:
Fatigue (śrama) is exhaustion arising internally in the body from excessive action;
indolence (ālasya) is called the mind's aversion to erotic and other actions.
[Footnote]
[Footnote: 1. "bhayarāgādyupasthitaḥ" in manuscript kha.] / [Page 207]

338.s:
dainyaṃ sattvādapabhraṃśaścintārthaparibhāvanaṃ /
itikartavyatopāyādraśanaṃ moha ucyate //
338.d:
दैन्यं सत्त्वादपभ्रंशश्चिन्तार्थपरिभावनं /
इतिकर्तव्यतोपायाद्रशनं मोह उच्यते //
338.m:
Wretchedness (dainya) is a fall from strength (sattva); anxiety (cintā) is contemplation of an object;
distraction (moha) is called non-perception of the means of what ought to be done.

338.s:
smṛtiḥ syādanubhūtasya vastunaḥ prativimbanaṃ /
matirarthaparicchedastattvajñānopanāyitaḥ //
338.d:
स्मृतिः स्यादनुभूतस्य वस्तुनः प्रतिविम्बनं /
मतिरर्थपरिच्छेदस्तत्त्वज्ञानोपनायितः //
338.m:
Remembrance (smṛti) is the reflection of an experienced object;
resolve (mati) is determination of an object brought about by knowledge of truth.

338.s:
vrīḍānurāgādibhavaḥ saṅkocaḥ kopi cetasaḥ /
bhaveccapalātāsthairyaṃ harṣaścittaprasannatā //
338.d:
व्रीडानुरागादिभवः सङ्कोचः कोपि चेतसः /
भवेच्चपलातास्थैर्यं हर्षश्चित्तप्रसन्नता //
338.m:
Shame (vrīḍā) is a certain contraction of the mind arising from affection and the like;
inconstancy (capalatā) is instability; joy (harṣa) is mental serenity.

338.s:
āveśaś ca pratīkāraḥ śayo vaidhuryamātmanaḥ /
kartavye pratibhābhraṃśo jaḍatetyabhidhīyate //
338.d:
आवेशश् च प्रतीकारः शयो वैधुर्यमात्मनः /
कर्तव्ये प्रतिभाभ्रंशो जडतेत्यभिधीयते //
338.m:
Agitation (āveśa) is an active reaction; helplessness is distress of oneself;
loss of creative wit regarding one's duty is termed stupor (jaḍatā).

338.s:
iṣṭaprāpterūpacitaḥ sampadābhyudayo dhṛtiḥ /
garvāḥ pareṣvavajñānamātmanyutkarṣabhāvanā //
338.d:
इष्टप्राप्तेरूपचितः सम्पदाभ्युदयो धृतिः /
गर्वाः परेष्ववज्ञानमात्मन्युत्कर्षभावना //
338.m:
Contentment (dhṛti) is the expansion of prosperity enhanced by obtaining what is desired;
pride (garva) is contempt for others and conceiving superiority in oneself.

338.s:
bhavedviṣādo daivādervighāto 'bhīṣṭavastuni /
autsukyamīpsitāprāptervāñchayā taralā sthitiḥ //
338.d:
भवेद्विषादो दैवादेर्विघातो ऽभीष्टवस्तुनि /
औत्सुक्यमीप्सिताप्राप्तेर्वाञ्छया तरला स्थितिः //
338.m:
Despondency (viṣāda) is the obstruction of a desired object by fate or the like;
longing (autsukya) is an unsteady state through desire, due to non-attainment of what is wished for.

338.s:
cittendriyāṇāṃ staimityamapasmāro 'calā sthitiḥ /
yuddhe bādhādibhīstrāso vīpsā cittacamatkṛtiḥ //
338.d:
चित्तेन्द्रियाणां स्तैमित्यमपस्मारो ऽचला स्थितिः /
युद्धे बाधादिभीस्त्रासो वीप्सा चित्तचमत्कृतिः //
338.m:
Stupefaction (apasmāra) is immobility, numbness of mind and senses;
fright (trāsa) is fear of harm and the like in battle; repetition (vīpsā) is wonder of the mind.

338.s:
krodhasyāpraśamo 'marṣaḥ prabodhaścetanodayaḥ /
avahitthaṃ bhavedguptiriṅgitākāragocarā //
338.d:
क्रोधस्याप्रशमो ऽमर्षः प्रबोधश्चेतनोदयः /
अवहित्थं भवेद्गुप्तिरिङ्गिताकारगोचरा //
338.m:
Indignation (amarṣa) is non-appeasement of anger; awakening (prabodha) is the rising of consciousness;
dissimulation (avahittha) is concealment pertaining to gestures and physical appearances.

338.s:
roṣato guruvāgdaṇḍapāruṣyaṃ vidurugratāṃ /
ūho vitarkaḥsyādvyādhirmanovapuravagrahaḥ //
338.d:
रोषतो गुरुवाग्दण्डपारुष्यं विदुरुग्रतां /
ऊहो वितर्कःस्याद्व्याधिर्मनोवपुरवग्रहः //
338.m:
They know ferocity (ugratā) to be harshness of grave speech and punishment born of wrath;
conjecture (vitarka) is deduction; disease (vyādhi) is affliction of mind and body.

338.s:
anibaddhapralāpādirunmādo madanādibhiḥ /
tattvajñānādinā cetaḥkaṣāyo paramaḥ śamaḥ //
338.d:
अनिबद्धप्रलापादिरुन्मादो मदनादिभिः /
तत्त्वज्ञानादिना चेतःकषायो परमः शमः //
338.m: Unconnected rambling and so forth is madness, caused by love and other passions; / through knowledge of ultimate reality and the like, the mind's passion is quieted: that is supreme tranquility.

338.s:
kavibhiryojanīyā vai bhāvāḥ kāvyādike rasāḥ /
vibhāvyate hi ratyādiryatra yena vibhāvyate //
338.d:
कविभिर्योजनीया वै भावाः काव्यादिके रसाः /
विभाव्यते हि रत्यादिर्यत्र येन विभाव्यते //
338.m: Emotional states and aesthetic sentiments are indeed to be employed by poets in poetry and the rest; / for where and by what love and the other states are brought to mind,

338.s:
vibhāvo nāma sadvedhālambanoddīpanātmakaḥ /
:p 208
ratyādibhāvavargo 'yaṃ yamājīvyopajāyate //
338.d:
विभावो नाम सद्वेधालम्बनोद्दीपनात्मकः /
:प् 208
रत्यादिभाववर्गो ऽयं यमाजीव्योपजायते //
338.m:
that is called an excitant determinant; it is of two kinds: having the nature of an essential support and of an inflaming stimulus.
[Page 208]
That group of emotional states, love and the rest, which arises depending upon someone:

338.s:
ālambanavibhāvo 'sau nāyakādibhavas tathā /
dhīrodātto dhīroddhataḥ syāddhīralalitas tathā //
338.d:
आलम्बनविभावो ऽसौ नायकादिभवस् तथा /
धीरोदात्तो धीरोद्धतः स्याद्धीरललितस् तथा //
338.m: that is the essential-support excitant determinant, arising from the hero and other characters. / The hero is remembered as fourfold: firm and noble, firm and haughty, firm and sportive,

338.s:
dhīrapraśānta ity evaṃ caturdhā nāyakaḥ smṛtaḥ /
anukūlo dakṣiṇaś ca śaṭho dhṛṣṭaḥ pravartitaḥ //
338.d:
धीरप्रशान्त इत्य् एवं चतुर्धा नायकः स्मृतः /
अनुकूलो दक्षिणश् च शठो धृष्टः प्रवर्तितः //
338.m: and firm and calm. / [As a lover] he is classified as faithful, impartial, deceitful, and brazen.

338.s:
pīṭhamardo viṭaś caiva vidūṣaka iti trayaḥ /
śṛṅgāre narmasacivā nāyakasyānunāyakāḥ //
338.d:
पीठमर्दो विटश् चैव विदूषक इति त्रयः /
शृङ्गारे नर्मसचिवा नायकस्यानुनायकाः //
338.m: The companion, the gallant, and the jester—these three / are companions in amusement in erotic sentiment, secondary heroes to the hero.

338.s:
pīṭhamardaḥ sambalakaḥ śrīmāṃstadveśajo viṭaḥ /
vidūṣako vaihasikastvaṣṭanāyakanāyikāḥ //
338.d:
पीठमर्दः सम्बलकः श्रीमांस्तद्वेशजो विटः /
विदूषको वैहसिकस्त्वष्टनायकनायिकाः //
338.m: The companion is a matchmaker; the gallant is prosperous and frequents courtesans; / the jester is a comedian; and there are eight heroines for the hero.

338.s:
svakīyā parakīyā ca punarbhūriti kauśikāḥ /
sāmānyā na punarbhūrirityādyā bahubhedataḥ //
338.d:
स्वकीया परकीया च पुनर्भूरिति कौशिकाः /
सामान्या न पुनर्भूरिरित्याद्या बहुभेदतः //
338.m: One's own wife, another's wife, and a remarried woman: these are the basic classes; / the courtesan is not a remarried woman; thus they have many subdivisions.

338.s:
uddipanavibhāvāste saṃskārair vividhaiḥ sthitaiḥ /
ālambanavibhāveṣu bhāvānudvīpayanti ye //
338.d:
उद्दिपनविभावास्ते संस्कारैर् विविधैः स्थितैः /
आलम्बनविभावेषु भावानुद्वीपयन्ति ये //
338.m: Those are the inflaming excitant determinants which, existing through manifold latent impressions, / kindle the emotional states in the essential-support excitant determinants.

338.s:
catuḥṣaṣṭikalā dvedhā karmādyair gītikādibhiḥ /
kuhakaṃ smṛtirapyeṣāṃ prāyo hāsopahārakaḥ //
338.d:
चतुःषष्टिकला द्वेधा कर्माद्यैर् गीतिकादिभिः /
कुहकं स्मृतिरप्येषां प्रायो हासोपहारकः //
338.m: The sixty-four arts are twofold, by actions and by songs and so forth; / deception and even memory of these is generally an offering of laughter.

338.s:
ālambanavibhāvasya bhāvair udbuddhasaṃskṛtaiḥ /
manovāgbuddhivapuṣāṃ smṛtīchādveṣayatnataḥ //
338.d:
आलम्बनविभावस्य भावैर् उद्बुद्धसंस्कृतैः /
मनोवाग्बुद्धिवपुषां स्मृतीछाद्वेषयत्नतः //
338.m: Of the essential-support excitant determinant, through the emotional states whose latent impressions are awakened, / through memory, desire, aversion, and effort of mind, speech, intellect, and body,

338.s:
ārambha eva viduṣāmanubhāva iti smṛtaḥ /
sa cānubhūyate cātra bhavatyuta nirucyate //
338.d:
आरम्भ एव विदुषामनुभाव इति स्मृतः /
स चानुभूयते चात्र भवत्युत निरुच्यते //
338.m: the commencement itself is recalled by the wise as the consequent expression; / and it is experienced here, it comes into being, and it is defined.

338.s:
manovyāpārabhūyiṣṭho mana ārambha ucyate /
dvividhaḥ pauruṣastraiṇa īdṛśo 'pi prasidhyati //
338.d:
मनोव्यापारभूयिष्ठो मन आरम्भ उच्यते /
द्विविधः पौरुषस्त्रैण ईदृशो ऽपि प्रसिध्यति //
338.m: Abounding in mental activity, it is called the mental commencement; / it is known as twofold: masculine and feminine, of such a character.

338.s:
śobhā vilāso mādhuryaṃ sthairyaṃ gāmbhīryameva ca /
lalitañca tathaudāryantejo 'ṣṭāviti pauruṣāḥ //
:p 209
338.d:
शोभा विलासो माधुर्यं स्थैर्यं गाम्भीर्यमेव च /
ललितञ्च तथौदार्यन्तेजो ऽष्टाविति पौरुषाः //
:प् 209
338.m:
Radiance, sportive charm, sweetness, steadfastness, gravity, / grace, nobility, and fiery spirit: these eight are the masculine [qualities].
[Page 209]

338.s:
nīcanindottamaspardhā śauryaṃ dākṣādikāraṇaṃ /
manodharme bhavecchobhā śobhate bhavanaṃ yathā //
338.d:
नीचनिन्दोत्तमस्पर्धा शौर्यं दाक्षादिकारणं /
मनोधर्मे भवेच्छोभा शोभते भवनं यथा //
338.m: Reproach of the base, emulation of the noble, heroism, the cause of capability and so forth / exist as mental attributes: this is radiance, just as a mansion shines.

338.s:
bhāvo hāvaś ca helā ca śobhā kāntistathaiva ca /
dīptirmādhuryaśaurye ca prāgalbhyaṃ syādudāratā //
338.d:
भावो हावश् च हेला च शोभा कान्तिस्तथैव च /
दीप्तिर्माधुर्यशौर्ये च प्रागल्भ्यं स्यादुदारता //
338.m: Incipient emotion, involuntary expression of desire, playful affectation, beauty, charm, / brilliance, sweetness, bravery, boldness, and generosity,

338.s:
sthairyaṃ gambhīratā strīṇāṃ vibhāvā dvādaśeritāḥ /
bhāvo vilāso hāvaḥsyādbhāvaḥ kiñcicca harṣajaḥ //
338.d:
स्थैर्यं गम्भीरता स्त्रीणां विभावा द्वादशेरिताः /
भावो विलासो हावःस्याद्भावः किञ्चिच्च हर्षजः //
338.m: steadfastness, and gravity: these twelve are stated as the determinative qualities of women. / Incipient emotion, graceful affectation, and involuntary expression of desire: incipient emotion is born of a slight joy.

338.s:
vāco yuktirbhavedvāgārambho dvādaśa eva saḥ /
tatrābhāṣaṇamālāpaḥ pralāpo vacanaṃ vahu(1) //
338.d:
वाचो युक्तिर्भवेद्वागारम्भो द्वादश एव सः /
तत्राभाषणमालापः प्रलापो वचनं वहु(1) //
338.m: The application of speech is the verbal commencement, and it is twelvefold: / conversation is speech addressing someone; rambling is profuse talking;

338.s:
vilāpo duḥkhavacanamanulāpo 'sakṛdvacaḥ /
saṃlāpa uktapratyuktamapalāpo 'nyathāvacaḥ //
338.d:
विलापो दुःखवचनमनुलापो ऽसकृद्वचः /
संलाप उक्तप्रत्युक्तमपलापो ऽन्यथावचः //
338.m: lamentation is words of sorrow; repetition is words repeated often; / dialogue is exchange of speech; denial is speaking otherwise;

338.s:
vārtāprayāṇaṃ sandeśo nirdeśaḥ pratipādanam /
tattvadeśo 'tideśo 'yamapadeśo 'nyavarṇanam //
338.d:
वार्ताप्रयाणं सन्देशो निर्देशः प्रतिपादनम् /
तत्त्वदेशो ऽतिदेशो ऽयमपदेशो ऽन्यवर्णनम् //
338.m: a message is conveying news; instruction is presentation of facts; / correct determination is this, extension of application, pretext is describing something else,

338.s:
upadeśaś ca śikṣāvāk vyājoktirvyapadeśakaḥ /
bodhāya eṣa vyāpāraḥsubuddhyārambha iṣyate /
tasya bhedāstrayaste ca rītivṛttipravṛttayaḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe alaṅkāre śṛṅgārādirasanirūpaṇaṃ
nāmāṣṭatriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 muhuriti kha..
:p 210
:ś athonacatvāriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
rītinirūpaṇaṃ
agnirucāca
338.d:
उपदेशश् च शिक्षावाक् व्याजोक्तिर्व्यपदेशकः /
बोधाय एष व्यापारःसुबुद्ध्यारम्भ इष्यते /
तस्य भेदास्त्रयस्ते च रीतिवृत्तिप्रवृत्तयः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे अलङ्कारे शृङ्गारादिरसनिरूपणं
नामाष्टत्रिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 मुहुरिति ख..
:प् 210
:श् अथोनचत्वारिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
रीतिनिरूपणं
अग्निरुचाच
338.m:
and advice is didactic speech; prevarication is an insinuation. / This activity intended for understanding is considered the intellectual commencement; / its subdivisions are three, and they are styles of diction, dramatic styles, and regional trends.
Thus ends the three hundred and thirty-eighth chapter, named "Examination of the Erotic and Other Aesthetic Sentiments" under Poetics, in the great Agni Purāṇa.
[Footnote]
[Variant reading for 'muhur' in manuscript kha]
[Page 210]
Now, the three hundred thirty-ninth chapter.
Exposition of poetic styles.
Agni said:

339.s:
vāgvidyāsampratijñāne rītiḥ sāpi caturvidhā /
pāñcālī gauḍadeśīyā vaidarbhī lāṭajā tathā //
339.d:
वाग्विद्यासम्प्रतिज्ञाने रीतिः सापि चतुर्विधा /
पाञ्चाली गौडदेशीया वैदर्भी लाटजा तथा //
339.m: In the proper understanding of the lore of speech, poetic style (rīti) is also of four kinds: / Pāñcālī, Gauḍadeśīyā, Vaidarbhī, and likewise that born in Lāṭa (Lāṭī).

339.s:
upacārayutā mṛdvī pāñcālī hrasvavigrahā /
anavasthitasandarbhā gauḍīyā dīrghavigrahā //
339.d:
उपचारयुता मृद्वी पाञ्चाली ह्रस्वविग्रहा /
अनवस्थितसन्दर्भा गौडीया दीर्घविग्रहा //
339.m: Endowed with metaphorical expressions, soft, and having short compounds is Pāñcālī; / having unstable composition and long compounds is Gauḍīyā.

339.s:
upacārair na bahubhirupacārair vivarjitā /
nātikomalasandarbhā vaidarbhī muktavigrahā //
339.d:
उपचारैर् न बहुभिरुपचारैर् विवर्जिता /
नातिकोमलसन्दर्भा वैदर्भी मुक्तविग्रहा //
339.m: Devoid of metaphorical expressions, or not with many metaphorical expressions, / having a composition that is not overly delicate, and free from compounds, is Vaidarbhī.

339.s:
lāṭīyā sphuṭasandharbhā nātivisphuravigrahā /
parityaktāpi bhūyobhirupacārair udāhṛtā //
339.d:
लाटीया स्फुटसन्धर्भा नातिविस्फुरविग्रहा /
परित्यक्तापि भूयोभिरुपचारैर् उदाहृता //
339.m: Lāṭīyā is spoken of as having clear composition, compounds that are not excessively prominent, / and being largely free from metaphorical expressions.

339.s:
kriyāsvaviṣamā vṛttirbhāratyārabhaṭī tathā /
kauśikī sātvatī ceti sā caturdhā pratiṣṭhitā //
339.d:
क्रियास्वविषमा वृत्तिर्भारत्यारभटी तथा /
कौशिकी सात्वती चेति सा चतुर्धा प्रतिष्ठिता //
339.m: The dramatic style (vṛtti), which is not uneven in actions, is established as fourfold: / Bhāratī, Ārabhaṭī, Kauśikī, and Sātvatī.

339.s:
vākpradhānā naraprāyā strīyuktā prākṛtoktitā /
bharatena praṇītatvād bhāratī rītirucyate //
339.d:
वाक्प्रधाना नरप्राया स्त्रीयुक्ता प्राकृतोक्तिता /
भरतेन प्रणीतत्वाद् भारती रीतिरुच्यते //
339.m: Predominant in speech, mostly using men, accompanied by women, having Prakrit speech, / [and] because it was produced by Bharata, it is called the Bhāratī style.

339.s:
catvāryaṅgāni bhāratyā vīthī prahasanantathā /
prastāvanā nāṭakādervīthyaṅgāś ca trayodaśa //
339.d:
चत्वार्यङ्गानि भारत्या वीथी प्रहसनन्तथा /
प्रस्तावना नाटकादेर्वीथ्यङ्गाश् च त्रयोदश //
339.m: The Bhāratī has four limbs: vīthī, prahasana, / and the prologue (prastāvanā) of a drama and the like; and the limbs of vīthī are thirteen:

339.s:
udghātakaṃ tathaiva syāllapitaṃ syāddvitīyakam /
asatpralāpo vākśreṇī(1) nālikā vipaṇantathā //
339.d:
उद्घातकं तथैव स्याल्लपितं स्याद्द्वितीयकम् /
असत्प्रलापो वाक्श्रेणी(1) नालिका विपणन्तथा //
339.m: udghātaka, and likewise lapita would be the second; / asatpralāpa, vākśreṇī, nālikā, and likewise vipaṇa,

339.s:
vyāhārastimatañcaiva(2) chalāvaskandite tathā /
:n
1 vāgveṇīti ka.. , ña.. , ṭa.. ca
2 vyāhārastrigatañcaiveti kha..
:p 211
gaṇḍo 'tha mṛdavaś caiva trayodaśamathācitam //
339.d:
व्याहारस्तिमतञ्चैव(2) छलावस्कन्दिते तथा /
:न्
1 वाग्वेणीति क.. , ञ.. , ट.. च
2 व्याहारस्त्रिगतञ्चैवेति ख..
:प् 211
गण्डो ऽथ मृदवश् चैव त्रयोदशमथाचितम् //
339.m:
vyāhāra, stimata, and likewise chala and avaskandita,
[Footnote]
[Variant reading 'vāgveṇī' in manuscripts ka, ña, and ṭa]
[Variant reading 'vyāhārastrigatañcaiva' in manuscript kha]
[Page 211]
then gaṇḍa, and mṛdava, and the thirteenth is acita.

339.s:
tāpasādeḥ prahasanaṃ parihāsaparaṃ vacaḥ /
māyendrajālayuddhādibahulārabhaṭī smṛtā /
maṅkṣiptakārapātau ca(1) vastūtthāpanameva ca //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe alaṅkāre rītinirūpaṇaṃ
nāmonacatvāriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha catvāriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
nṛtyādāvaṅgakarmanirūpaṇaṃ
339.d:
तापसादेः प्रहसनं परिहासपरं वचः /
मायेन्द्रजालयुद्धादिबहुलारभटी स्मृता /
मङ्क्षिप्तकारपातौ च(1) वस्तूत्थापनमेव च //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे अलङ्कारे रीतिनिरूपणं
नामोनचत्वारिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ चत्वारिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
नृत्यादावङ्गकर्मनिरूपणं
339.m:
The speech of ascetics and others, intent on mockery, is prahasana. / Ārabhaṭī is known as abounding in magic, illusion, battles, and the like; / and [its limbs are] saṅkṣiptaka, avapāta, and vastūtthāpana.
Thus ends the three hundred thirty-ninth chapter, named 'Exposition of Poetic Styles', in the section on poetics in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now, the three hundred fortieth chapter.
Exposition of bodily actions in dance and related arts.

340.s:
agnir uvāca
ceṣṭāviśeṣamapyaṅgapratyaṅge karma cānayoḥ /
śarīrārambhamicchanti prāyaḥ pūrvo 'valāśrayaḥ //
340.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
चेष्टाविशेषमप्यङ्गप्रत्यङ्गे कर्म चानयोः /
शरीरारम्भमिच्छन्ति प्रायः पूर्वो ऽवलाश्रयः //
340.m: Agni said: / They regard the specific movement in the major limbs and minor limbs, and the action of these two, / as the origin of bodily expression; the former usually belongs to women:

340.s:
līlā vilāso vichittirvibhramaṃ kilakiñcitaṃ /
moṭṭāyitaṃ kuṭṭamitaṃ vivvoko lalitantathā //
340.d:
लीला विलासो विछित्तिर्विभ्रमं किलकिञ्चितं /
मोट्टायितं कुट्टमितं विव्वोको ललितन्तथा //
340.m: līlā, vilāsa, vicchitti, vibhrama, kilakiñcita, / moṭṭāyita, kuṭṭamita, vivvoka, and likewise lalita,

340.s:
vikṛtaṃ krīḍitaṃ keliriti dvādaśadhaiva saḥ /
līleṣṭajanaceṣṭānukaraṇaṃ saṃvṛtakṣaye //
340.d:
विकृतं क्रीडितं केलिरिति द्वादशधैव सः /
लीलेष्टजनचेष्टानुकरणं संवृतक्षये //
340.m: vikṛta, krīḍita, and keli—thus it is twelvefold. / Līlā is the imitation of the gestures of a beloved person upon the disappearance of reserve.

340.s:
viśeṣān darśayan kiñcidvilāsaḥ sadbhiriṣyate /
hasitakrānditādīnāṃ saṅkaraḥ kilakiñcitaṃ //
340.d:
विशेषान् दर्शयन् किञ्चिद्विलासः सद्भिरिष्यते /
हसितक्रान्दितादीनां सङ्करः किलकिञ्चितं //
340.m: Vilāsa is considered by the wise to be displaying some slight distinction [in movement]. / The mingling of laughter, weeping, and the like is kilakiñcita.

340.s:
vikāraḥ kopi vivvoko lalitaṃ saukumāryataḥ /
śiraḥ pāṇiruraḥ pārśvaṅkaṭiraṅghririti kramāt //
340.d:
विकारः कोपि विव्वोको ललितं सौकुमार्यतः /
शिरः पाणिरुरः पार्श्वङ्कटिरङ्घ्रिरिति क्रमात् //
340.m: Any transformation [of haughty indifference] is vivvoka; lalita is [graceful movement] arising from delicacy. / Head, hands, chest, flanks, waist, and feet in order—

340.s:
aṅgāni bhrūlatādīni pratyaṅgānyabhijānate /
:n
1 saṅkṣiptakarapātau ceti ja..
:p 212
aṅgapratyaṅgayoḥ karma prayatnajanitaṃ vinā //
340.d:
अङ्गानि भ्रूलतादीनि प्रत्यङ्गान्यभिजानते /
:न्
1 सङ्क्षिप्तकरपातौ चेति ज..
:प् 212
अङ्गप्रत्यङ्गयोः कर्म प्रयत्नजनितं विना //
340.m:
they recognise these as the major limbs; the creeper-like brows and the like are the minor limbs.
[Footnote]
[Variant reading 'saṅkṣiptakarapātau ca' in manuscript ja]
[Page 212]
Without the action of the major and minor limbs produced by effort,

340.s:
na prayogaḥ kvacinmukhyantiraścīnañca tat kvacit /
ākampitaṃ kampitañca(1) dhūtaṃ vidhūtameva ca //
340.d:
न प्रयोगः क्वचिन्मुख्यन्तिरश्चीनञ्च तत् क्वचित् /
आकम्पितं कम्पितञ्च(1) धूतं विधूतमेव च //
340.m: a performance is nowhere prominent, and it is sometimes oblique. / [The movements of the head are:] ākampita, kampita, dhūta, and vidhūta,

340.s:
parivāhitamādhūtamavadhūtamathācitaṃ /
nikuñcitaṃ parāvṛttamutkṣiptañcāpyadhogatam //
340.d:
परिवाहितमाधूतमवधूतमथाचितं /
निकुञ्चितं परावृत्तमुत्क्षिप्तञ्चाप्यधोगतम् //
340.m: parivāhita, ādhūta, avadhūta, and acita, / nikuñcita, parāvṛtta, utkṣipta, and adhogata.

340.s:
lalitañceti vijñeyaṃ trayodaśavidhaṃ śiraḥ /
bhrūkarma saptadhā jñeyaṃ pātanaṃ bhrūkuṭīmukhaṃ //
340.d:
ललितञ्चेति विज्ञेयं त्रयोदशविधं शिरः /
भ्रूकर्म सप्तधा ज्ञेयं पातनं भ्रूकुटीमुखं //
340.m: and Lalita: thus the [movements of the] head should be known as thirteenfold. / The movement of the brows is known to be of seven kinds: dropping, knitting the brows, and the like.

340.s:
dṛṣtistridhā ramasthāyisañcāripratibandhanā /
ṣaṭtriṃśadbhedavidhurā rasajā tatra cāṣṭadhā //
340.d:
दृष्तिस्त्रिधा रमस्थायिसञ्चारिप्रतिबन्धना /
षट्त्रिंशद्भेदविधुरा रसजा तत्र चाष्टधा //
340.m: Gaze is threefold, tied to the rasas, enduring states, and transitory states; / [the gaze] consists of thirty-six divisions, and that arising from the rasas is of eight kinds.

340.s:
navadhā tārakākarma bhramaṇañcalanādikaṃ /
ṣoḍhā ca nāsikā jñeyā niśvāso navadhā mataḥ //
340.d:
नवधा तारकाकर्म भ्रमणञ्चलनादिकं /
षोढा च नासिका ज्ञेया निश्वासो नवधा मतः //
340.m: The movement of the pupils is of nine kinds, such as rolling and trembling; / the nose should be known as sixfold, and breathing is considered ninefold.

340.s:
ṣoṭauṣṭhakarmakaṃ pāpaṃ saptadhā civukakriyā /
kaluṣādimukhaṃ ṣoḍhā grīvā navavidhā smṛtā //
340.d:
षोटौष्ठकर्मकं पापं सप्तधा चिवुकक्रिया /
कलुषादिमुखं षोढा ग्रीवा नवविधा स्मृता //
340.m: Lip action is sixfold, chin action is of seven kinds; / the mouth, [classified as] foul and so forth, is sixfold, and the neck is considered ninefold.

340.s:
asaṃyutaḥ saṃyutaś ca bhūmnā hastaḥ pramucyate /
patākastripātākaś ca tathā vai kartarīmukhaḥ //
340.d:
असंयुतः संयुतश् च भूम्ना हस्तः प्रमुच्यते /
पताकस्त्रिपाताकश् च तथा वै कर्तरीमुखः //
340.m: A hand gesture is broadly declared to be single-handed or combined: / Patāka, Tripatāka, and likewise Kartarīmukha,

340.s:
ardhacandrotkarālaś ca śukatuṇḍastathaiva ca /
suṣṭiś ca śikharaś caiva kapitthaḥ kheṭakāmukhaḥ //
340.d:
अर्धचन्द्रोत्करालश् च शुकतुण्डस्तथैव च /
सुष्टिश् च शिखरश् चैव कपित्थः खेटकामुखः //
340.m: Ardhacandra, Arāla, Śukatuṇḍa as well, / Muṣṭi, Śikhara, Kapittha, Khaṭakāmukha,

340.s:
sūcyāsyaḥ padmakoṣo hi śirāḥ samṛgaśīrṣakāḥ /
kāṃmūlakālapadmau(2)* ca caturabhramarau tathā //
340.d:
सूच्यास्यः पद्मकोषो हि शिराः समृगशीर्षकाः /
कांमूलकालपद्मौ(2)* च चतुरभ्रमरौ तथा //
340.m: Sūcyāsya, Padmakośa, Sarpaśīrṣa, Mṛgaśīrṣa, / Kāṅgūla, Alapadma, Catura, and Bhramara,

340.s:
haṃsāsyahaṃsapakṣau ca sandaṃśamukulau tathā /
:n
1 ākalpitaṃ kalpitañceti kha..
2 kāṅgūlakālapadmāviti ña..
kāṃmūlakālapadmau kāṅgūlakālapadmau etatpāṭhadvayaṃ na
samīcīnaṃ
:p 213
urṇanābhastāmracūḍaś caturviṃśatirityamī //
340.d:
हंसास्यहंसपक्षौ च सन्दंशमुकुलौ तथा /
:न्
1 आकल्पितं कल्पितञ्चेति ख..
2 काङ्गूलकालपद्माविति ञ..
कांमूलकालपद्मौ काङ्गूलकालपद्मौ एतत्पाठद्वयं न
समीचीनं
:प् 213
उर्णनाभस्ताम्रचूडश् चतुर्विंशतिरित्यमी //
340.m:
Haṃsāsya, Haṃsapakṣa, Sandaṃśa, Mukula,
[Footnote]
[Apparatus note: 1. Ākalpitaṃ kalpitañca, in manuscript kha.]
[Apparatus note: 2. Kāṅgūlakālapadmau, in manuscript ña.]
[Editorial note: The two readings kāṃmūlakālapadmau and kāṅgūlakālapadmau are not correct.]
Ūrṇanābha, and Tāmracūḍa: these are the twenty-four

340.s:
asaṃyutakarāḥ proktāḥ saṃyutāstu trayodaśa /
añjaliś ca kapotaś ca karkaṭaḥ svastikas tathā //
340.d:
असंयुतकराः प्रोक्ताः संयुतास्तु त्रयोदश /
अञ्जलिश् च कपोतश् च कर्कटः स्वस्तिकस् तथा //
340.m: single hand gestures that are taught; the combined [gestures] are thirteen: / Añjali, Kapota, Karkaṭa, and Svastika,

340.s:
kaṭako vardhamānaścāpyasaṅgo niṣadhas tathā /
dolaḥ puṣpapuṭaś caiva tathā makara eva ca //
340.d:
कटको वर्धमानश्चाप्यसङ्गो निषधस् तथा /
दोलः पुष्पपुटश् चैव तथा मकर एव च //
340.m: Kaṭakāvardhamāna, Utsaṅga, Niṣadha, / Dola, Puṣpapuṭa, and Makara,

340.s:
gajadanto vahistambho vardhamāno 'pare karāḥ /
uraḥ pañcavidhaṃ syāttu ābhugnanartanādikam //
340.d:
गजदन्तो वहिस्तम्भो वर्धमानो ऽपरे कराः /
उरः पञ्चविधं स्यात्तु आभुग्ननर्तनादिकम् //
340.m: Gajadanta, Avahittha, and Vardhamāna are the other hands. / The chest is of five kinds: bent, dancing, and so forth.

340.s:
udaranduratikṣāmaṃ khaṇḍaṃ pūrṇamiti tridhā /
pārśvayoḥ pañcakarmāṇi jaṅghākarma ca pañcadhā /
anekadhā pādakarma nṛtyādau nāṭake smṛtam //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe alaṅkāre
nṛtyādāvaṅgakarmanirūpaṇam nāma catvariṃśadadhikatriśatatamo
'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś athaikacatvāriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
abhinayādinirūpaṇaṃ
340.d:
उदरन्दुरतिक्षामं खण्डं पूर्णमिति त्रिधा /
पार्श्वयोः पञ्चकर्माणि जङ्घाकर्म च पञ्चधा /
अनेकधा पादकर्म नृत्यादौ नाटके स्मृतम् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे अलङ्कारे
नृत्यादावङ्गकर्मनिरूपणम् नाम चत्वरिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो
ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथैकचत्वारिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
अभिनयादिनिरूपणं
340.m:
The belly is threefold: slender, depressed, and full. / The actions of the flanks are five, the actions of the calves are of five kinds, / and the actions of the feet in dance and drama are declared to be manifold.
Thus in the great Agni Purāṇa, in [the section on] poetics, the three hundred and fortieth chapter, entitled "The Description of Bodily Actions in Dance and the Like."
Now, the three hundred and forty-first chapter:
Description of dramatic representation and the like.

341.s:
agnir uvāca
ābhimukhyannayannarthānvijñeyo 'bhinayo budhaiḥ /
caturdhā sambhavaḥ sattvavāgaṅgāharaṇāśrayaḥ //
341.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
आभिमुख्यन्नयन्नर्थान्विज्ञेयो ऽभिनयो बुधैः /
चतुर्धा सम्भवः सत्त्ववागङ्गाहरणाश्रयः //
341.m: Agni said: / Bringing the meanings [of a text] forward [to the spectators], it is to be understood by the wise as dramatic representation (abhinaya); / its arising is fourfold, resting upon inner temperament, speech, bodily limbs, and external ornamentation.

341.s:
stambhādiḥ sāttviko vāgārambho vācika āṅgikaḥ /
śarīrārambha āhāryo buddhyārambhapravṛttayaḥ //
341.d:
स्तम्भादिः सात्त्विको वागारम्भो वाचिक आङ्गिकः /
शरीरारम्भ आहार्यो बुद्ध्यारम्भप्रवृत्तयः //
341.m: Stupefaction and the like is sāttvika; the exertion of voice is vācika; / the movement of the body is āṅgika; the production of intelligence and costumes is āhārya.

341.s:
rasādiviniyogo 'tha kathyate hy abhimānataḥ /
tamantareṇa sarve ṣāmapārthaiva svatantratā //
341.d:
रसादिविनियोगो ऽथ कथ्यते ह्य् अभिमानतः /
तमन्तरेण सर्वे षामपार्थैव स्वतन्त्रता //
341.m: Then the application of the rasas and the like is explained through ego-consciousness; / without it, independence for all [rasas] is entirely meaningless.

341.s:
sambhogo vipralambhaś ca śṛṅgāro dvividhaḥ smṛtaḥ /
:p 214
pracchannaś ca prakāśaś ca tāvapi dvividhau punaḥ //
341.d:
सम्भोगो विप्रलम्भश् च शृङ्गारो द्विविधः स्मृतः /
:प् 214
प्रच्छन्नश् च प्रकाशश् च तावपि द्विविधौ पुनः //
341.m:
The erotic (śṛṅgāra) is remembered as twofold: in union (sambhoga) and in separation (vipralambha).
[Page 214]
These two are further of two kinds: hidden and open.

341.s:
vipralambhābhidhāno yaḥ śṛṅgāraḥ sa caturvidhaḥ /
pūrvānurāgānākhyaḥ pravāmakaruṇātmakaḥ //
341.d:
विप्रलम्भाभिधानो यः शृङ्गारः स चतुर्विधः /
पूर्वानुरागानाख्यः प्रवामकरुणात्मकः //
341.m: The erotic [rasa] known as separation is of four kinds: / that called first love, travel, [separation], and of the nature of compassion.

341.s:
etebhyo 'nyataraṃ jāyamānamambhogalakṣaṇam /
vivartate caturdhaiva na ca prāgativartate //
341.d:
एतेभ्यो ऽन्यतरं जायमानमम्भोगलक्षणम् /
विवर्तते चतुर्धैव न च प्रागतिवर्तते //
341.m: Arising from these, another characterized by union / unfolds in four ways, and it does not proceed beforehand.

341.s:
strīpuṃsayostadudayastasya nirvirtikā ratiḥ /
nikhilāḥ sāttvikāstatra vaivarṇyapralayau vinā //
341.d:
स्त्रीपुंसयोस्तदुदयस्तस्य निर्विर्तिका रतिः /
निखिलाः सात्त्विकास्तत्र वैवर्ण्यप्रलयौ विना //
341.m: Its arising belongs to a man and a woman; its productive cause is love (rati). / All the involuntary states (sāttvika) are present there, except paleness and fainting.

341.s:
dharmārthakāmamokṣaiś ca śṛṅgāra upacīyate /
ālamvanaviśeṣaiś ca tadviśeṣair nirantaraḥ //
341.d:
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षैश् च शृङ्गार उपचीयते /
आलम्वनविशेषैश् च तद्विशेषैर् निरन्तरः //
341.m: The erotic [rasa] is heightened by duty, wealth, pleasure, and liberation, / and constantly by specific primary determinants and their particulars.

341.s:
śṛṅgāraṃ dvividhaṃ vidyādvāṅnepathyakriyātmakam /
hāsaś ca turvidho 'lakṣyadantaḥ smita itīritaḥ //
341.d:
शृङ्गारं द्विविधं विद्याद्वाङ्नेपथ्यक्रियात्मकम् /
हासश् च तुर्विधो ऽलक्ष्यदन्तः स्मित इतीरितः //
341.m: One should know laughter to be twofold: consisting of speech, costumes, and action. / Laughter is of four kinds; when the teeth are invisible, it is called a smile (smita);

341.s:
kiñcillakṣitadantāgraṃ hasitaṃ phullalocanam /
vihasitaṃ sasvanaṃ syājjihmopahasitantu tat //
341.d:
किञ्चिल्लक्षितदन्ताग्रं हसितं फुल्ललोचनम् /
विहसितं सस्वनं स्याज्जिह्मोपहसितन्तु तत् //
341.m: with the tips of the teeth slightly visible and the eyes blossoming, it is gentle laughter (hasita); / vihasita is accompanied by sound, while mocking laughter (upahasita) is crooked;

341.s:
saśabdaṃ pāpahasitamaśabdamatihāsitaṃ /
yaścāsau karuṇo nāma sa rasastrividho bhavet //
341.d:
सशब्दं पापहसितमशब्दमतिहासितं /
यश्चासौ करुणो नाम स रसस्त्रिविधो भवेत् //
341.m: loud laughter (apahasita) has sound, and excessive laughter (atihāsita) is without sound. / And that which is called the pathetic (karuṇa), that rasa is threefold:

341.s:
dharmopaghātajaścittavilāsajanitas tathā /
śokaḥ śokādbhavet sthāyī kaḥ sthāyī pūrvajo mataḥ //
341.d:
धर्मोपघातजश्चित्तविलासजनितस् तथा /
शोकः शोकाद्भवेत् स्थायी कः स्थायी पूर्वजो मतः //
341.m: arising from the destruction of righteousness, and produced from agitation of the mind; / sorrow arises from sorrow; the permanent state [is sorrow]—the first-born is considered a permanent state.

341.s:
aṅganepathyavākyaiś ca raudro 'pi trividho rasaḥ /
tasya nirvartakaḥ krodhaḥ svedo romāñcavapathuḥ //
341.d:
अङ्गनेपथ्यवाक्यैश् च रौद्रो ऽपि त्रिविधो रसः /
तस्य निर्वर्तकः क्रोधः स्वेदो रोमाञ्चवपथुः //
341.m: The furious (raudra) rasa is also threefold, through body, costume, and words; / its productive cause is anger (krodha), [accompanied by] sweat, horripilation, and trembling.

341.s:
dānavīro dharmavīro yuddhavīra iti trayam /
vīrastasya ca niṣpattiheturutsāha iṣyate //
341.d:
दानवीरो धर्मवीरो युद्धवीर इति त्रयम् /
वीरस्तस्य च निष्पत्तिहेतुरुत्साह इष्यते //
341.m: Heroism in charity, heroism in righteousness, and heroism in battle: this is the triad / of the heroic (vīra), and zeal (utsāha) is accepted as the cause of its accomplishment.

341.s:
ārambheṣu bhavedyatra vīramevānuvartate /
:p 215
bhayānako nāma rasastasya nirvartakaṃ bhayaṃ //
341.d:
आरम्भेषु भवेद्यत्र वीरमेवानुवर्तते /
:प् 215
भयानको नाम रसस्तस्य निर्वर्तकं भयं //
341.m:
Where in beginnings it occurs, it follows the heroic alone.
[Page 215]
The fearful (bhayānaka) is a rasa whose producing cause is fear.

341.s:
udvejanaḥ kṣobhaṇaś ca vībhatso dvividhaḥ smṛtaḥ /
udvejanaḥ syāt plutyādyaiḥ kṣobhaṇo rudhirādibhiḥ //
341.d:
उद्वेजनः क्षोभणश् च वीभत्सो द्विविधः स्मृतः /
उद्वेजनः स्यात् प्लुत्याद्यैः क्षोभणो रुधिरादिभिः //
341.m: The odious (bībhatsa) is considered twofold: agitating and repulsive; / it is agitating by leaps and the like, and repulsive by blood and the like.

341.s:
jagupsārambhikā tasya sāttvikāṃśo nivartate /
kāvyaśobhākarān dharmānalaṅkārān pracakṣyate //
341.d:
जगुप्सारम्भिका तस्य सात्त्विकांशो निवर्तते /
काव्यशोभाकरान् धर्मानलङ्कारान् प्रचक्ष्यते //
341.m: Disgust (jugupsā) is its initiator, and its involuntary component recedes. / The attributes that produce beauty in poetry are declared to be ornaments (alaṅkāra).

341.s:
alaṅkariṣṇavaste ca śabdamarthamubhau tridhā /
ye vyutpattyādinā śabdamalaṅkartumiha kṣamāḥ //
341.d:
अलङ्करिष्णवस्ते च शब्दमर्थमुभौ त्रिधा /
ये व्युत्पत्त्यादिना शब्दमलङ्कर्तुमिह क्षमाः //
341.m: Desiring to ornament, they [ornament] sound, sense, or both, in three ways. / Those which, through derivation and the like, are capable here of ornamenting sound—

341.s:
śabdālaṅkāramāhustān kāvyamīmāṃsakā vidaḥ /
chāyā mudrā tathoktiś ca yuktirgumphanayā saha //
341.d:
शब्दालङ्कारमाहुस्तान् काव्यमीमांसका विदः /
छाया मुद्रा तथोक्तिश् च युक्तिर्गुम्फनया सह //
341.m: the knowers and critics of poetry call them ornaments of sound (śabdālaṅkāra). / Chāyā (reflection), Mudrā (seal), likewise Ukti (expression), Yukti (union) together with Gumphanā (weaving),

341.s:
vākovākyamanuprāsaścitraṃ duṣkarameva ca /
jṇeyā navālaṅkṛtayaḥ śabdānāmityasaṅkarāt //
341.d:
वाकोवाक्यमनुप्रासश्चित्रं दुष्करमेव च /
ज्णेया नवालङ्कृतयः शब्दानामित्यसङ्करात् //
341.m: Vākovākya (dialogue), Anuprāsa (alliteration), Citra (pictorial poetry), and Duṣkara (difficult composition): / these are to be known as the nine ornaments of sound, without confusion.

341.s:
tatrānyokteranukṛtiśchāyā sāpi catruvvidhā /
lokacchekārbhakoktīnāmekokteranukārataḥ //
341.d:
तत्रान्योक्तेरनुकृतिश्छाया सापि चत्रुव्विधा /
लोकच्छेकार्भकोक्तीनामेकोक्तेरनुकारतः //
341.m: Among them, Chāyā is the imitation of another's utterance, and it is fourfold, / through the imitation of the speech of common folk, the clever, children, and a single speaker:

341.s:
ābhāṇakoktirlokoktiḥ sarvasāmānya eva tāḥ /
yānudhāvati lokoktiśchāyāmicchanti tāṃ budhāḥ //
341.d:
आभाणकोक्तिर्लोकोक्तिः सर्वसामान्य एव ताः /
यानुधावति लोकोक्तिश्छायामिच्छन्ति तां बुधाः //
341.m: Common speech is proverbial speech; those [proverbs] are common to everyone. / That which follows common speech, the wise consider to be the Chāyā [of common folk].

341.s:
chekā vidagdhā vaidagdhyaṃ kalāsu kuśalā matiḥ /
tāmullikhantī chekoktiśchāyā kavibhiriṣyate //
341.d:
छेका विदग्धा वैदग्ध्यं कलासु कुशला मतिः /
तामुल्लिखन्ती छेकोक्तिश्छाया कविभिरिष्यते //
341.m: The clever (cheka) are the witty, and wit is an intellect skilled in the arts; / portraying that, the Chāyā of clever speech is intended by the poets.

341.s:
avyutpannoktirakhilair arbhakoktyopalakṣyate /
tenārbhakoktiśchāyā tanmātroktimanukurvatī //
341.d:
अव्युत्पन्नोक्तिरखिलैर् अर्भकोक्त्योपलक्ष्यते /
तेनार्भकोक्तिश्छाया तन्मात्रोक्तिमनुकुर्वती //
341.m: Uncultivated speech is characterized by all as the speech of children; / thus the Chāyā of children's speech imitates their speech alone.

341.s:
viplutākṣaramaślīlaṃ vaco mattasya tādṛśī /
yā sā bhavati mattoktiśchāyoktāpyatiśobhate //
341.d:
विप्लुताक्षरमश्लीलं वचो मत्तस्य तादृशी /
या सा भवति मत्तोक्तिश्छायोक्ताप्यतिशोभते //
341.m: The words of an intoxicated person have confused syllables and improper content; / that which is the Chāyā of an intoxicated person's speech, when spoken, shines brightly.

341.s:
abhiprāyaviśeṣeṇa kaviśaktiṃ vivṛṇvatī /
:p 216
mutpradāyinīti sā mudrā saiva śayyāpi no mate //
341.d:
अभिप्रायविशेषेण कविशक्तिं विवृण्वती /
:प् 216
मुत्प्रदायिनीति सा मुद्रा सैव शय्यापि नो मते //
341.m:
Revealing the power of the poet through a particular intention,
[Page 216]
giving delight—that is Mudrā; and that same [quality] is also called repose (śayyā) in our view.

341.s:
uktiḥ sā kathyate yasyāmarthako 'pyupapattimān /
lokayātrārthavidhinā dhinoti hṛdayaṃ satāṃ //
341.d:
उक्तिः सा कथ्यते यस्यामर्थको ऽप्युपपत्तिमान् /
लोकयात्रार्थविधिना धिनोति हृदयं सतां //
341.m: Ukti (expression) is said to be that in which even an insignificant meaning possesses plausibility, / and through the rule of the ways of the world delights the hearts of the virtuous.

341.s:
ubhau vidhiniṣedhau ca niyamāniyamāvapi /
vikalpaparisaṅkhye ca tadīyāḥ ṣaḍathoktayaḥ //
341.d:
उभौ विधिनिषेधौ च नियमानियमावपि /
विकल्पपरिसङ्ख्ये च तदीयाः षडथोक्तयः //
341.m: Injunction and prohibition, both restriction and absence of restriction, / option and exclusion: these are its six modes of expression.

341.s:
ayuktayoriva mitho vācyavācakayordvayoḥ /
yojanāyai kalpyamānā yuktiruktā manīṣibhiḥ //
341.d:
अयुक्तयोरिव मिथो वाच्यवाचकयोर्द्वयोः /
योजनायै कल्प्यमाना युक्तिरुक्ता मनीषिभिः //
341.m: The joining together of two words—expressed sense and expressing word—/ that seem unconnected, devised [by a poet], is called Yukti by the wise.

341.s:
padañcaiva padārthaś ca vākyaṃ vākyarthameva ca /
viṣayo 'styāḥ prakaraṇaṃ prapañcaśceti ṣaḍvidhaḥ //
341.d:
पदञ्चैव पदार्थश् च वाक्यं वाक्यर्थमेव च /
विषयो ऽस्त्याः प्रकरणं प्रपञ्चश्चेति षड्विधः //
341.m: A word, the meaning of a word, a sentence, and the meaning of a sentence, / a topic, and an expansion: its scope is of six kinds.

341.s:
gumphanā racanācaryā śabdārthakramagocarā /
śabdānukārādarthānupūrvārtheyaṃ kramāttridhā //
341.d:
गुम्फना रचनाचर्या शब्दार्थक्रमगोचरा /
शब्दानुकारादर्थानुपूर्वार्थेयं क्रमात्त्रिधा //
341.m: Gumphanā (weaving) is the practice of composition pertaining to the arrangement of sound and sense; / by imitation of sounds, and by sequence of senses, this is threefold in succession.

341.s:
uktipratyuktimadvākyaṃ vākovākyaṃ dvidhaiva tat /
ṛjuvakroktibhedena tatrādyaṃ sahajaṃ vacaḥ //
341.d:
उक्तिप्रत्युक्तिमद्वाक्यं वाकोवाक्यं द्विधैव तत् /
ऋजुवक्रोक्तिभेदेन तत्राद्यं सहजं वचः //
341.m: A speech consisting of utterance and reply is Vākovākya (dialogue); it is of two kinds, / through the division of straightforward and crooked speech; among them, the first is natural speech.

341.s:
sā pūrvapraśnikā praśnapūrviketi dvidhā bhavet /
vakroktistu bhaveḍbhaṅgyā kākustena kṛtā dvidhā //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe alaṅkāre abhinayādinirūpaṇaṃ
nāmaikacatvāriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:p 217
:ś atha dvicatvāriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
śabdālaṅkārāḥ
agnirucāca
341.d:
सा पूर्वप्रश्निका प्रश्नपूर्विकेति द्विधा भवेत् /
वक्रोक्तिस्तु भवेड्भङ्ग्या काकुस्तेन कृता द्विधा //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे अलङ्कारे अभिनयादिनिरूपणं
नामैकचत्वारिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:प् 217
:श् अथ द्विचत्वारिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
शब्दालङ्काराः
अग्निरुचाच
341.m:
It may be twofold: pūrvapraśnikā and praśnapūrvikā. / But oblique expression (vakrokti) occurs by an indirect turn; intonation (kāku) is made twofold by it.
Thus ends the three hundred forty-first chapter, named 'Exposition of Dramatic Representation and Related Topics', in the section on poetics in the great Agni Purāṇa.
[Page 217]
Now, the three hundred forty-second chapter.
Figures of sound.
Agni said:

342.s:
syādāvṛttiranuprāso varṇānāṃ padavākyayoḥ /
ekavarṇānekavarṇāvṛttervarṇaguṇo dvidhā //
342.d:
स्यादावृत्तिरनुप्रासो वर्णानां पदवाक्ययोः /
एकवर्णानेकवर्णावृत्तेर्वर्णगुणो द्विधा //
342.m: Alliteration (anuprāsa) is the repetition of phonemes in words and sentences; / by the repetition of a single phoneme or many phonemes, the quality of phonemes is twofold.

342.s:
ekavarṇagatāvṛtterjāyante pañca vṛttayaḥ /
madhurā lalitā prauṭā bhadrā paruṣayā saha //
342.d:
एकवर्णगतावृत्तेर्जायन्ते पञ्च वृत्तयः /
मधुरा ललिता प्रौटा भद्रा परुषया सह //
342.m: From the repetition residing in a single phoneme, five diction styles (vṛtti) arise: / Madhurā, Lalitā, Prauḍhā, Bhadrā, along with Paruṣā.

342.s:
madhurāyāś ca vargantādadho vargyā raṇau svanau(1) /
hrasvasvareṇāntaritau saṃyuktatvaṃ nakārayoḥ //
342.d:
मधुरायाश् च वर्गन्तादधो वर्ग्या रणौ स्वनौ(1) /
ह्रस्वस्वरेणान्तरितौ संयुक्तत्वं नकारयोः //
342.m: In Madhurā, consonants belonging to a class occur below the class nasal, r and ṇ are sounded, / separated by a short vowel, and there is a conjunction of n-sounds.

342.s:
na kāryā vargyavarṇānāmāvṛttiḥ pañcamādhikā /
mahāprāṇoṣmasaṃyogapravimuktalaghūttarau(2) //
342.d:
न कार्या वर्ग्यवर्णानामावृत्तिः पञ्चमाधिका /
महाप्राणोष्मसंयोगप्रविमुक्तलघूत्तरौ(2) //
342.m: The repetition of class consonants should not exceed five times; / followed by light syllables free from the conjunction of aspirates and sibilants.

342.s:
lalitā balabhūyiṣṭhā(3) prauṭā yā paṇavargajā /
ūrdhvaṃ repheṇa yujyante naṭavargonapañcamāḥ //
342.d:
ललिता बलभूयिष्ठा(3) प्रौटा या पणवर्गजा /
ऊर्ध्वं रेफेण युज्यन्ते नटवर्गोनपञ्चमाः //
342.m: Lalitā abounds in b and l; Prauḍhā is that born of the labial and retroflex classes; / the retroflex class consonants, excluding the fifth, are conjoined above with r.

342.s:
bhadrāyāṃ pariśiṣṭāḥ syuḥ paruṣā sābhidhīyate /
bhavanti yasyāmūṣmāṇaḥ saṃyuktāstattadakṣaraiḥ //
342.d:
भद्रायां परिशिष्टाः स्युः परुषा साभिधीयते /
भवन्ति यस्यामूष्माणः संयुक्तास्तत्तदक्षरैः //
342.m: In Bhadrā are the remaining [consonants]; Paruṣā is designated as that / in which sibilants are conjoined with their respective letters.

342.s:
akāravarjamāvṛttiḥ svarāṇāmatibhūyasī /
anusvāravisargau ca pāruṣyāya nirantarau //
342.d:
अकारवर्जमावृत्तिः स्वराणामतिभूयसी /
अनुस्वारविसर्गौ च पारुष्याय निरन्तरौ //
342.m: The frequent repetition of vowels with the exception of 'a', / and anusvāra and visarga uninterruptedly, produce harshness (pāruṣya).

342.s:
śaṣasā rephasaṃyuktāścākāraścāpi bhūyasā /
:n
1 raśau ghanāviti ña..
2 mahāprāṇoṣmasaṃyogādaviyuktalaghūttarāviti ṭa..
3 lalitā vanabhūyiṣṭheti kha.. / lalitā vatsabhūyiṣṭheti ṭa..
:p 218
antasthābhinnamābhyāñca haḥ pāruṣyāya saṃyutaḥ //
342.d:
शषसा रेफसंयुक्ताश्चाकारश्चापि भूयसा /
:न्
1 रशौ घनाविति ञ..
2 महाप्राणोष्मसंयोगादवियुक्तलघूत्तराविति ट..
3 ललिता वनभूयिष्ठेति ख.. / ललिता वत्सभूयिष्ठेति ट..
:प् 218
अन्तस्थाभिन्नमाभ्याञ्च हः पारुष्याय संयुतः //
342.m:
Ś, ṣ, and s conjoined with r, and also 'a' abundantly,
[Footnote]
[Variant reading 'raśau ghanau' in manuscript ña]
[Variant reading 'mahāprāṇoṣmasaṃyogādaviyuktalaghūttarau' in manuscript ṭa]
[Variant reading 'lalitā vanabhūyiṣṭhā' in manuscript kha; 'lalitā vatsabhūyiṣṭhā' in manuscript ṭa]
[Page 218]
and h joined with these, not separate from semivowels, leads to harshness.

342.s:
anyathāpi gururvarṇaḥ saṃyukteparipanthini /
pāruṣyāyādimāṃstatra pūjitā na tu pañcamo //
342.d:
अन्यथापि गुरुर्वर्णः संयुक्तेपरिपन्थिनि /
पारुष्यायादिमांस्तत्र पूजिता न तु पञ्चमो //
342.m: Even otherwise, a heavy syllable when an opposing conjunct is present [contributes] / to harshness; there the first consonants are preferred, but not the fifth.

342.s:
kṣepe śabdānukāre ca paruṣāpi prayujyate /
karṇāṭī kauntalī kauntī kauṅkaṇī vāmanāsikā(1) //
342.d:
क्षेपे शब्दानुकारे च परुषापि प्रयुज्यते /
कर्णाटी कौन्तली कौन्ती कौङ्कणी वामनासिका(1) //
342.m: Paruṣā is also employed in abuse and in onomatopoeia. / Karṇāṭī, Kauntalī, Kauntī, Kauṅkaṇī, Vāmanāsikā,

342.s:
drāvaṇī mādhavī pañcavarṇāntasthoṣmabhiḥ kramāt /
anekavarṇāvṛttiryā bhinnārthapratipādikā //
342.d:
द्रावणी माधवी पञ्चवर्णान्तस्थोष्मभिः क्रमात् /
अनेकवर्णावृत्तिर्या भिन्नार्थप्रतिपादिका //
342.m: Drāvaṇī, and Mādhavī [are formed] by the five classes, semivowels, and sibilants in order. / That repetition of multiple phonemes which conveys distinct meanings

342.s:
yamakaṃ sāvyapetañca vyapetañceti taddvidhā /
ānantaryādavyapetaṃ vyapetaṃ vyavadhānataḥ //
342.d:
यमकं साव्यपेतञ्च व्यपेतञ्चेति तद्द्विधा /
आनन्तर्यादव्यपेतं व्यपेतं व्यवधानतः //
342.m: [That repetition of various syllables conveying different meanings is] yamaka; and that is twofold: uninterrupted and interrupted, / uninterrupted by reason of contiguity, and interrupted by reason of an interval.

342.s:
dvaividhyenānayoḥ sthānapādabhedāccaturvidham /
ādipādādimadhyānteṣvekadvitriniyogataḥ //
342.d:
द्वैविध्येनानयोः स्थानपादभेदाच्चतुर्विधम् /
आदिपादादिमध्यान्तेष्वेकद्वित्रिनियोगतः //
342.m: Through the two types of these two, it is of four kinds according to differences of place and line; / by using [it] at the beginning, middle, or end of the lines, starting with the first line, once, twice, or thrice,

342.s:
saptadhā saptapūrveṇa(2) cet pādenottarottaraḥ /
ekadvitripadārambhastulyaḥ ṣoḍhā tadāparaṃ //
342.d:
सप्तधा सप्तपूर्वेण(2) चेत् पादेनोत्तरोत्तरः /
एकद्वित्रिपदारम्भस्तुल्यः षोढा तदापरं //
342.m: it is of seven kinds; if each subsequent line is equal in beginning with one, two, or three words / to the one preceding it, then another [group] is of six kinds.

342.s:
tṛtīyaṃ trividhaṃ pādasyādimadhyāntagocaram /
pādāntayamakañcaiva kāñcīyamakameva ca //
342.d:
तृतीयं त्रिविधं पादस्यादिमध्यान्तगोचरम् /
पादान्तयमकञ्चैव काञ्चीयमकमेव च //
342.m: The third is of three kinds, having its sphere at the beginning, middle, or end of a line: / [namely,] pādāntayamaka, and also kāñcīyamaka,

342.s:
saṃsargayamakañcaiva(3) vikrāntayamakantathā /
pādādiyamakañcaiva tathāmreḍitameva ca //
342.d:
संसर्गयमकञ्चैव(3) विक्रान्तयमकन्तथा /
पादादियमकञ्चैव तथाम्रेडितमेव च //
342.m: and saṃsargayamaka, as well as vikrāntayamaka, / and pādādiyamaka, and likewise āmreḍita,

342.s:
caturvyavasitañcaiva mālāyamakameva ca /
daśadhā yamakaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ tadbhedā bahavo 'pare //
342.d:
चतुर्व्यवसितञ्चैव मालायमकमेव च /
दशधा यमकं श्रेष्ठं तद्भेदा बहवो ऽपरे //
342.m: and caturvyavasita, and also mālāyamaka; / yamaka is considered foremost in ten varieties; there are many other subdivisions of it.

342.s:
svatantrasyānyatantrasya padasyāvartanā dvidhā /
:n
1 bālavāsiketi kha.. , ṭa.. ca / vanavāsiketi ña..
2 pūrvapūrveṇeti ja.. , ña.. , ṭa.. ca
3 sambandhayamakaś caiveti kha..
:p 219
bhinnaprayojanapadasyāvṛttiṃ manujā viduḥ //
342.d:
स्वतन्त्रस्यान्यतन्त्रस्य पदस्यावर्तना द्विधा /
:न्
1 बालवासिकेति ख.. , ट.. च / वनवासिकेति ञ..
2 पूर्वपूर्वेणेति ज.. , ञ.. , ट.. च
3 सम्बन्धयमकश् चैवेति ख..
:प् 219
भिन्नप्रयोजनपदस्यावृत्तिं मनुजा विदुः //
342.m:
The repetition of an independent word or of a dependent word is twofold:
[Footnote]
1. "bālavāsikā" in manuscript kha and manuscript ṭa; "vanavāsikā" in manuscript ña.
2. "pūrvapūrveṇa" in manuscripts ja, ña, and ṭa.
3. "sambandhayamakaś caiva" in manuscript kha. / [Page 219]
men know the repetition of a word having a different purpose [to be of two kinds].

342.s:
dvayorāvṛttapadayoḥ samastā syātsamāsataḥ /
asamāsāttayorvyastā pāde tvekatra vigrahāt //
342.d:
द्वयोरावृत्तपदयोः समस्ता स्यात्समासतः /
असमासात्तयोर्व्यस्ता पादे त्वेकत्र विग्रहात् //
342.m: Between the two repeated words, it is combined through compounding, / and separated between the two through non-compounding, or [partly combined] in a single line through analytical division.

342.s:
vākyasyāvṛttirapyevaṃ yathāsambhavamiṣyate /
alaṅkārādyanuprāso laghumadhyevamarhaṇāt(1) * //
342.d:
वाक्यस्यावृत्तिरप्येवं यथासम्भवमिष्यते /
अलङ्काराद्यनुप्रासो लघुमध्येवमर्हणात्(1) * //
342.m: In the same way, the repetition of a sentence is also accepted as far as possible. / The foremost of ornaments is alliteration, light and middling in this manner due to worthiness […].

342.s:
yayā kayācidvṛtyā yat samānamanubhūyate /
tadrūpādipadāsattiḥ sānuprasā rasāvahā //
342.d:
यया कयाचिद्वृत्या यत् समानमनुभूयते /
तद्रूपादिपदासत्तिः सानुप्रसा रसावहा //
342.m: Whatever is perceived as identical through any verbal function whatsoever, / that proximity of words having such forms brings about aesthetic flavour, [and] it is alliteration.

342.s:
goṣṭhyāṃ kutūhalādhyāyī vāgbandhaścitramucyate /
praśnaḥ prahelikā guptaṃ cyutadatte tathobhayam //
342.d:
गोष्ठ्यां कुतूहलाध्यायी वाग्बन्धश्चित्रमुच्यते /
प्रश्नः प्रहेलिका गुप्तं च्युतदत्ते तथोभयम् //
342.m: A verbal composition that generates wonder in an assembly is called visual poetry (citra); / question (praśna), riddle (prahelikā), concealed meaning (gupta), omitted letter (cyuta), supplied letter (datta), both together (cyutadatta),

342.s:
samasyā sapta tadbhedā nānārthasyānuyogataḥ /
yatra pradīyate tulyavarṇavinyāsamuttaraṃ //
342.d:
समस्या सप्त तद्भेदा नानार्थस्यानुयोगतः /
यत्र प्रदीयते तुल्यवर्णविन्यासमुत्तरं //
342.m: [and] verse completion (samasyā)—its varieties are seven, through inquiry into varied senses. / Where an answer is given possessing identical arrangements of syllables,

342.s:
sa praśnaḥ syādekapṛṣṭadvipṛṣṭottarabhedataḥ /
dvidhaikapṛṣṭo dvividhaḥ samasto vyasta eva ca //
342.d:
स प्रश्नः स्यादेकपृष्टद्विपृष्टोत्तरभेदतः /
द्विधैकपृष्टो द्विविधः समस्तो व्यस्त एव च //
342.m: that is a question (praśna), divided into single-questioned, double-questioned, and [single-]answered; / the single-questioned is twofold: composite and separated.

342.s:
dvayorapyarthayorguhyamānaśabdā prahelikā /
sā dvidhārtho ca śābdī ca tatrārthī cārthabodhataḥ //
342.d:
द्वयोरप्यर्थयोर्गुह्यमानशब्दा प्रहेलिका /
सा द्विधार्थो च शाब्दी च तत्रार्थी चार्थबोधतः //
342.m: A riddle (prahelikā) has words concealed with respect to both meanings; / it is twofold: based on sense (ārthī) and based on sound (śābdī); there, it is based on sense through comprehension of the sense,

342.s:
śabdāvabodhataḥ śābdī prāhuḥ ṣoḍhā prahelikāṃ /
yasmin gupte 'pi vākyāṅge bhāvyartho 'pāramārthikaḥ //
342.d:
शब्दावबोधतः शाब्दी प्राहुः षोढा प्रहेलिकां /
यस्मिन् गुप्ते ऽपि वाक्याङ्गे भाव्यर्थो ऽपारमार्थिकः //
342.m: and based on sound through comprehension of the sound; they declare the riddle to be of six kinds. / In which [composition], even though a component of the sentence is concealed, an unreal sense is to be apprehended,

342.s:
tadaṅgavihitākāṅkṣastadguptaṃ gūḍhamapyadaḥ /
yatrārthāntaranirbhāso vākyāṅgacyavanādibhiḥ //
342.d:
तदङ्गविहिताकाङ्क्षस्तद्गुप्तं गूढमप्यदः /
यत्रार्थान्तरनिर्भासो वाक्याङ्गच्यवनादिभिः //
342.m: and the syntactical expectancy is fulfilled by that very component, that is concealed (gupta); this is also [called] cryptic (gūḍha). / Where a different meaning appears through the dropping of a component of the sentence and the like,

342.s:
tadaṅgavihitākāṅkṣastaccutaṃ syāccaturvidham /
:n
1 laghumapyevamarhaṇāditi ṭa.. / laghumadhyeva varhaṇāditi ja..
laghumadhyevamarhaṇāt, laghumapyevamarhaṇāt, laghumadhyeva
varhaṇāt etat pāṭhatrayaṃ na samyak pratibhāti
:p 220
svaravyañjanavindūnāṃ visargasya ca vicyuteḥ //
342.d:
तदङ्गविहिताकाङ्क्षस्तच्चुतं स्याच्चतुर्विधम् /
:न्
1 लघुमप्येवमर्हणादिति ट.. / लघुमध्येव वर्हणादिति ज..
लघुमध्येवमर्हणात्, लघुमप्येवमर्हणात्, लघुमध्येव
वर्हणात् एतत् पाठत्रयं न सम्यक् प्रतिभाति
:प् 220
स्वरव्यञ्जनविन्दूनां विसर्गस्य च विच्युतेः //
342.m:
and the syntactical expectancy is fulfilled by that component, that is omitted (cyuta), which is of four kinds,
[Footnote]
1. "laghumapyevamarhaṇāt" in manuscript ṭa; "laghumadhyeva varhaṇāt" in manuscript ja.
These three readings—laghumadhyevamarhaṇāt, laghumapyevamarhaṇāt, laghumadhyeva varhaṇāt—do not appear sound. / [Page 220]
through the dropping of vowels, consonants, anusvāras, and the visarga.

342.s:
dattepi yatra vākyāṅge dvitīyorthaḥ pratīyate /
dattantadāhustadbhedāḥ svarādyaiḥ pūrvavanmatāḥ //
342.d:
दत्तेपि यत्र वाक्याङ्गे द्वितीयोर्थः प्रतीयते /
दत्तन्तदाहुस्तद्भेदाः स्वराद्यैः पूर्ववन्मताः //
342.m: Where a second meaning is understood even when a component of the sentence is supplied, / they call that supplied (datta); its varieties are considered as before, based on vowels and the rest.

342.s:
apanītākṣarasthāne nyaste varṇāntare 'pi ca /
bhāsate 'rthāntaraṃ yatra cyutadattaṃ taducyate //
342.d:
अपनीताक्षरस्थाने न्यस्ते वर्णान्तरे ऽपि च /
भासते ऽर्थान्तरं यत्र च्युतदत्तं तदुच्यते //
342.m: Where, when another syllable is placed in the location of a removed syllable, / a different meaning shines forth, that is called omitted-and-supplied (cyutadatta).

342.s:
suśliṣṭapadyamekaṃ yannānāślokāṃśanirmitam /
sā mamasyā parasyātmaparayoḥ kṛtisaṅkarāt //
342.d:
सुश्लिष्टपद्यमेकं यन्नानाश्लोकांशनिर्मितम् /
सा ममस्या परस्यात्मपरयोः कृतिसङ्करात् //
342.m: When a single well-knit verse is constructed from parts of various verses, / that is verse completion (samasyā), through the mingling of another's work with one's own or of the works of two others.

342.s:
duḥkhena kṛtamatyarthaṃ kavisāmarthyasūcakam /
duṣkaraṃ nīrasatvepi vidagdhānāṃ mahotsavaḥ //
342.d:
दुःखेन कृतमत्यर्थं कविसामर्थ्यसूचकम् /
दुष्करं नीरसत्वेपि विदग्धानां महोत्सवः //
342.m: Composed with extreme difficulty, indicating the capability of the poet, / [such] difficult verse (duṣkara), even though devoid of aesthetic flavour, is a great festival for the sophisticated.

342.s:
niyamācca vidarbhāca bandhācca bhavati tridhā /
kaveḥ pratijñā nirmāṇaramyasya niyamaḥ smṛtaḥ //
342.d:
नियमाच्च विदर्भाच बन्धाच्च भवति त्रिधा /
कवेः प्रतिज्ञा निर्माणरम्यस्य नियमः स्मृतः //
342.m: It is threefold: through restriction (niyama), through Vidarbha style (vidarbha), and through pictorial pattern (bandha). / The poet's resolve for charming construction is termed restriction.

342.s:
sthānenāpi svareṇāpi vyañjanenāpi sa tridhā /
vikalpaḥ prātilomyānulomyādevābhidhīyate //
342.d:
स्थानेनापि स्वरेणापि व्यञ्जनेनापि स त्रिधा /
विकल्पः प्रातिलोम्यानुलोम्यादेवाभिधीयते //
342.m: It is threefold: by place of articulation, by vowel, and also by consonant; / the distinction is declared solely through reverse and direct order.

342.s:
pratilomyānulomyañca śabdenārthena jāyate /
anekadhāvṛttavarṇavinyāsaiḥ śilpakalpanā //
342.d:
प्रतिलोम्यानुलोम्यञ्च शब्देनार्थेन जायते /
अनेकधावृत्तवर्णविन्यासैः शिल्पकल्पना //
342.m: Direct and reverse order arises through word and through meaning. / The artistic contrivance through arrangements of manifold repeated syllables

342.s:
tattatprasiddhavastūnāṃ bandha ity abhidhīyate /
gomūtrikārdhabhramaṇe sarvatobhadramambujam //
342.d:
तत्तत्प्रसिद्धवस्तूनां बन्ध इत्य् अभिधीयते /
गोमूत्रिकार्धभ्रमणे सर्वतोभद्रमम्बुजम् //
342.m: representing various well-known objects is designated as pictorial pattern (bandha): / zigzag (gomūtrikā), half-rotation (ardhabhramaṇa), omnidirectional (sarvatobhadra), lotus (ambuja),

342.s:
cakrañcakrābjakaṃ daṇḍo murajāśceti cāṣṭadhā /
pratyardhaṃ pratipādaṃ syādekāntarasamākṣarā //
342.d:
चक्रञ्चक्राब्जकं दण्डो मुरजाश्चेति चाष्टधा /
प्रत्यर्धं प्रतिपादं स्यादेकान्तरसमाक्षरा //
342.m: wheel (cakra), wheel-lotus (cakrābjaka), staff (daṇḍa), and drums (muraja)—it is eightfold. / In every half [verse] or in every line, there may be identical syllables alternately spaced;

342.s:
dvidhā gomūtrikāṃ pūrvāmāhuraśvapadāṃ pare /
antyāṅgomūtrikāṃ dhenuṃ jālabandhaṃ(1) vadanti hi //
342.d:
द्विधा गोमूत्रिकां पूर्वामाहुरश्वपदां परे /
अन्त्याङ्गोमूत्रिकां धेनुं जालबन्धं(1) वदन्ति हि //
342.m: some call the first zigzag (gomūtrikā) twofold, [namely] horse's move (aśvapadā); / indeed, they call the final [variety of] zigzag cow (dhenu) and network-pattern (jālabandha).

342.s:
ardhābhyāmardhapādaiś ca kuryādvinyāsametayoḥ /
:n
1 jānubandhamiti ka.. , kha.. ca
:p 221
nyastānāmiha varṇānāmadhodhaḥ kramabhāgināṃ //
342.d:
अर्धाभ्यामर्धपादैश् च कुर्याद्विन्यासमेतयोः /
:न्
1 जानुबन्धमिति क.. , ख.. च
:प् 221
न्यस्तानामिह वर्णानामधोधः क्रमभागिनां //
342.m:
One should make the arrangement of these two by half-verses and by quarter-verses,
[Footnote]
1. "jānubandham" in manuscripts ka and kha. / [Page 221]
of syllables placed here downward and downward in successive order.

342.s:
adhodhaḥsthitavarṇānāṃ yāvattūryapadannayet /
turyapādānnayedūrdha pādārdhaṃ prātilomyataḥ //
342.d:
अधोधःस्थितवर्णानां यावत्तूर्यपदन्नयेत् /
तुर्यपादान्नयेदूर्ध पादार्धं प्रातिलोम्यतः //
342.m: One should read the syllables placed downward and downward until one reaches the fourth line; / from the fourth line, one should read upward half a line in reverse order.

342.s:
tadeva sarvatobhadraṃ trividhaṃ sarasīruhaṃ /
catuṣpatraṃ tato vighnaṃ catuṣpatre ubhe api //
342.d:
तदेव सर्वतोभद्रं त्रिविधं सरसीरुहं /
चतुष्पत्रं ततो विघ्नं चतुष्पत्रे उभे अपि //
342.m: That very [figure] is omnidirectional (sarvatobhadra). The lotus pattern is threefold: / four-petalled, then [eight-petalled] […], and both [of those] on a four-petalled one.

342.s:
atha prathamapādasya mūrdhanyastripadākṣaraṃ /
sarveṣāmeva pādānāmante tadupajāyate //
342.d:
अथ प्रथमपादस्य मूर्धन्यस्त्रिपदाक्षरं /
सर्वेषामेव पादानामन्ते तदुपजायते //
342.m: Now, the syllable of three lines placed at the head of the first line / occurs at the end of all the lines.

342.s:
prākpadasyāntimaṃ pratyak pādādau prātilomyataḥ /
antyapādāntimañcādyapādādāvakṣaradvayaṃ //
342.d:
प्राक्पदस्यान्तिमं प्रत्यक् पादादौ प्रातिलोम्यतः /
अन्त्यपादान्तिमञ्चाद्यपादादावक्षरद्वयं //
342.m: The final [syllable] of the first line is at the beginning of the subsequent line in reverse order; / the final [syllable] of the last line and the two syllables at the beginning of the first line

342.s:
catuśchade bhavedaṣṭacchade varṇatrayaṃ punaḥ /
syāt ṣoḍaśacchade tvekāntarañcedekamakṣaraṃ //
342.d:
चतुश्छदे भवेदष्टच्छदे वर्णत्रयं पुनः /
स्यात् षोडशच्छदे त्वेकान्तरञ्चेदेकमक्षरं //
342.m: occur in a four-petalled [lotus]; in an eight-petalled one, there are three syllables again; / in a sixteen-petalled one, however, there is one syllable spaced by an interval.

342.s:
karṇikāṃ tolayedūrdhvaṃ patrākārākṣarāvaliṃ /
praveśayet karṇikāyāñcatuṣpatrasaroruhe //
342.d:
कर्णिकां तोलयेदूर्ध्वं पत्राकाराक्षरावलिं /
प्रवेशयेत् कर्णिकायाञ्चतुष्पत्रसरोरुहे //
342.m: One should draw the pericarp in the centre above; one should introduce the row of syllables / in the form of petals into the pericarp in the four-petalled lotus.

342.s:
karṇikāyāṃ likhedekaṃ dve dve dikṣu vidikṣu ca /
praveśanirgamau dikṣu kuryādaṣṭacchade 'mbuje //
342.d:
कर्णिकायां लिखेदेकं द्वे द्वे दिक्षु विदिक्षु च /
प्रवेशनिर्गमौ दिक्षु कुर्यादष्टच्छदे ऽम्बुजे //
342.m: One should write one [syllable] in the pericarp, and two each in the cardinal directions and intermediate directions; / in the eight-petalled lotus, one should make the entrance and exit in the cardinal directions.

342.s:
viśvagviṣamavarṇānāṃ tāvat patrābalījuṣāṃ /
