madhye samākṣaranyāsaḥsaroje ṣoḍaśacchade //
342.d:
विश्वग्विषमवर्णानां तावत् पत्राबलीजुषां /
मध्ये समाक्षरन्यासःसरोजे षोडशच्छदे //
342.m: In the sixteen-petalled lotus, there is the placement of identical syllables in the middle / for the odd syllables that everywhere occupy the row of petals.

342.s:
dvidhā cakraṃ caturaraṃ ṣaḍarantatra cādimaṃ /
pūrvārdhe sadṛśā varṇāḥ pādaprathamapañcamāḥ //
342.d:
द्विधा चक्रं चतुररं षडरन्तत्र चादिमं /
पूर्वार्धे सदृशा वर्णाः पादप्रथमपञ्चमाः //
342.m: The wheel is twofold: four-spoked and six-spoked; therein, in the first, / the syllables identical in the first half are the first and fifth of the line,

342.s:
ayujo 'śvayujaś caiva turyāvapyaṣṭamāvapi /
tasyopapādaprākpratyagareṣu ca yathākramaṃ //
342.d:
अयुजो ऽश्वयुजश् चैव तुर्यावप्यष्टमावपि /
तस्योपपादप्राक्प्रत्यगरेषु च यथाक्रमं //
342.m: the odd ones, the Aśvin-numbered ones (second), as well as the fourth and the eighth; / in the spokes from east to west of its sub-lines, in due order,

342.s:
syātpādārdhacatuṣkantu nābhau tasyādyamakṣaraṃ /
paścimārāvadhi nayennemau śeṣe padadvayī //
:p 222
342.d:
स्यात्पादार्धचतुष्कन्तु नाभौ तस्याद्यमक्षरं /
पश्चिमारावधि नयेन्नेमौ शेषे पदद्वयी //
:प् 222
342.m:
there are four half-lines; its initial syllable is in the hub; / one should carry [it] up to the western spoke, and the remaining pair of words to the rim.
[Page 222]

342.s:
tṛtīyaṃ turyapādānte prathamau sadṛśāvubhau /
varṇau pādatrayasyāpi daśamaḥ sadṛśo yadi //
342.d:
तृतीयं तुर्यपादान्ते प्रथमौ सदृशावुभौ /
वर्णौ पादत्रयस्यापि दशमः सदृशो यदि //
342.m: The third [syllable], the two initial syllables at the end of the fourth line are both identical; / if the tenth syllable of all three lines is also identical,

342.s:
prathame carame tasya ṣaḍtarṇāḥ pathime yadi /
bhavanti dvyantaraṃ tarhi vṛhacca kramudāhṛtaṃ //
342.d:
प्रथमे चरमे तस्य षड्तर्णाः पथिमे यदि /
भवन्ति द्व्यन्तरं तर्हि वृहच्च क्रमुदाहृतं //
342.m: and if there are six syllables in its first and last [lines] in the western [spoke] / separated by two intervals, then the great wheel is illustrated.

342.s:
sammukhāradvaye pādamekaikaṃ kramaśo likhet /
nābhau tu varṇaṃ daśamaṃ nemau tūryapadannayet //
342.d:
सम्मुखारद्वये पादमेकैकं क्रमशो लिखेत् /
नाभौ तु वर्णं दशमं नेमौ तूर्यपदन्नयेत् //
342.m: One should write each line successively on two opposing spokes; / in the hub, however, the tenth syllable; one should carry the fourth line to the rim.

342.s:
ślokasyādyantadaśamāḥ samā ādyantimau yujoḥ /
ādau varṇaḥ samau turyapañcamāvādyataryayoḥ //
342.d:
श्लोकस्याद्यन्तदशमाः समा आद्यन्तिमौ युजोः /
आदौ वर्णः समौ तुर्यपञ्चमावाद्यतर्ययोः //
342.m: The initial, final, and tenth [syllables] of the verse are identical; the initial and final ones of the even [lines] / are identical at the beginning; the fourth and fifth syllables of the first and fourth [lines are identical].

342.s:
dvitīyaprātilomyena tṛtīyaṃ jāyate yadi /
padaṃ vidadhyāt patrasya daṇḍaś cakrābjakaṃ kṛteḥ //
342.d:
द्वितीयप्रातिलोम्येन तृतीयं जायते यदि /
पदं विदध्यात् पत्रस्य दण्डश् चक्राब्जकं कृतेः //
342.m: If the third line arises / from the reverse reading of the second line, / one should construct the word of the petal; the staff (daṇḍa) and wheel-lotus (cakrābjaka) are formed [in this manner].

342.s:
dvitīyau prāgdale tulyau saptamau ca tathāparau /
sadṛśāvuttaradalau dvitīyābhyāmathārdhayoḥ //
342.d:
द्वितीयौ प्राग्दले तुल्यौ सप्तमौ च तथापरौ /
सदृशावुत्तरदलौ द्वितीयाभ्यामथार्धयोः //
342.m: The two second [syllables] in the first petal are identical, and likewise the other two seventh [syllables]; / the two [syllables] in the subsequent petal are similar to the two second [syllables] of the two halves.

342.s:
dvitīyaṣaṣṭhāḥ sadṛśāś caturthapañcamāvapi /
ādyantapādayostulyau parārdhasaptamāvapi //
342.d:
द्वितीयषष्ठाः सदृशाश् चतुर्थपञ्चमावपि /
आद्यन्तपादयोस्तुल्यौ परार्धसप्तमावपि //
342.m: The second and sixth [syllables] are identical, and likewise the fourth and fifth; / identical in the first and final quarters, and also the two seventh [syllables] of the latter half.

342.s:
samau turyaṃ pañcamantu krameṇa viniyojayet /
turyau yojyau tu tadvacca dalāntāḥ kramapādayoḥ //
342.d:
समौ तुर्यं पञ्चमन्तु क्रमेण विनियोजयेत् /
तुर्यौ योज्यौ तु तद्वच्च दलान्ताः क्रमपादयोः //
342.m: The fourth and fifth should be arranged in order as identical; / and likewise the two fourth [syllables] should be joined, [as well as] the ends of the petals in the quarters in succession.

342.s:
ardhayorantimādyau tu muraje sadṛśāvabhau /
pādārdhapatito varṇaḥ prātilomyānulomataḥ //
342.d:
अर्धयोरन्तिमाद्यौ तु मुरजे सदृशावभौ /
पादार्धपतितो वर्णः प्रातिलोम्यानुलोमतः //
342.m: In the muraja [drum design], the final and initial [syllables] of the two halves are both identical; / the syllable occurring in the half of the quarter, in reverse and in regular order,

342.s:
antimaṃ paribadhnīyādyāvatturyamihādimat /
pādātturyādyadevādyaṃ navamāt ṣoḍaśādapi //
342.d:
अन्तिमं परिबध्नीयाद्यावत्तुर्यमिहादिमत् /
पादात्तुर्याद्यदेवाद्यं नवमात् षोडशादपि //
342.m: should bind the final one up to the fourth here, beginning from the first; / just as from the fourth quarter the first [syllable is taken], from the ninth and also from the sixteenth

342.s:
akṣarāt puṭake madhye madhye 'kṣaracatuṣṭayam /
kṛtvā kuryādyathaitasya murajākāratā bhavet //
342.d:
अक्षरात् पुटके मध्ये मध्ये ऽक्षरचतुष्टयम् /
कृत्वा कुर्याद्यथैतस्य मुरजाकारता भवेत् //
342.m: syllable, placing four syllables in the middle and in the middle of each compartment, / one should construct it in such a way that it assumes the shape of a muraja drum.

342.s:
dvitīyaṃ cakraśārdūlavikrīḍitakasampadam /
:p 223
gomūtrikā sarvavṛttair anye bandhāstvanuṣṭubhā //
342.d:
द्वितीयं चक्रशार्दूलविक्रीडितकसम्पदम् /
:प् 223
गोमूत्रिका सर्ववृत्तैर् अन्ये बन्धास्त्वनुष्टुभा //
342.m:
A second [variety] has the richness of the cakra and śārdūlavikrīḍita meters.
[Page 223]
The gomūtrikā [zigzag pattern] may be formed with all meters; but the other bandhas are composed in anuṣṭubh.

342.s:
nāmadheyaṃ yadi na cedamīṣu kavikāvyayoḥ /
mitradheyābhituṣyanti nāmitraḥ khidyate tathā //
342.d:
नामधेयं यदि न चेदमीषु कविकाव्ययोः /
मित्रधेयाभितुष्यन्ति नामित्रः खिद्यते तथा //
342.m: If the names of the poet and the poem are not [inscribed] in these [figures], / [only] the circle of friends will be pleased, and an enemy will not be made sorrowful in that way.

342.s:
vāṇavāṇāsanavyomakhaḍgamudgaraśaktayaḥ /
dvicaturthatriśṛṅgāṭā dambholimuṣalāṅkuśāḥ //
342.d:
वाणवाणासनव्योमखड्गमुद्गरशक्तयः /
द्विचतुर्थत्रिशृङ्गाटा दम्भोलिमुषलाङ्कुशाः //
342.m: The arrow, bow, sky, sword, mallet, spear, / two-, four-, and three-peaked shapes, thunderbolt, pestle, and goad;

342.s:
padaṃ rathasya nāgasya puṣkariṇyasiputrikā /
ete bandhās tathā cānye evaṃ jñeyāḥ svayaṃ budhaiḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe alaṅkāre śabdālaṅkāranirūpaṇaṃ
nāma dvicatvāriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha tricatvāriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
arthālaṅkārāḥ
342.d:
पदं रथस्य नागस्य पुष्करिण्यसिपुत्रिका /
एते बन्धास् तथा चान्ये एवं ज्ञेयाः स्वयं बुधैः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे अलङ्कारे शब्दालङ्कारनिरूपणं
नाम द्विचत्वारिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ त्रिचत्वारिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
अर्थालङ्काराः
342.m:
the footprint of a chariot, of an elephant, a lotus-pool, and a dagger— / these pictorial arrangements and others should thus be understood by the wise on their own.
Thus ends the three hundred and forty-second chapter in the great Agni Purāṇa, on Poetics, titled "Exposition of Verbal Figures of Speech".
Now begins the three hundred and forty-third chapter.
Figures of Sense

343.s:
agnir uvāca
alaṅkaraṇamarthānāmarthālaṅkāra iṣyate /
taṃ vinā śabdasaundaryamapi nāsti manoharam //
343.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
अलङ्करणमर्थानामर्थालङ्कार इष्यते /
तं विना शब्दसौन्दर्यमपि नास्ति मनोहरम् //
343.m: Agni said: / The embellishment of meanings is regarded as a figure of sense; / without it, even beauty of words is not charming.

343.s:
arthālaṅkārarahitā vidhaveva(1) sarasvatī /
svarūpamatha sādṛśyamutprekṣātiśayāvapi //
343.d:
अर्थालङ्काररहिता विधवेव(1) सरस्वती /
स्वरूपमथ सादृश्यमुत्प्रेक्षातिशयावपि //
343.m: Devoid of figures of sense, eloquence is like a widow. / Nature, similarity, poetic fancy, hyperbole,

343.s:
vibhāvanā virodhaś ca hetuś ca samamaṣṭadhā /
svabhāva eva bhāvānāṃ svarūpamabhidhīyate //
343.d:
विभावना विरोधश् च हेतुश् च सममष्टधा /
स्वभाव एव भावानां स्वरूपमभिधीयते //
343.m: peculiar causation, contradiction, and reason are eightfold together [with these]. / The intrinsic nature of entities is termed their own form.

343.s:
nijamāgantukañceti dvividhaṃ tadudāhṛtam /
sāṃsiddhikaṃ niyaṃ naimittikamāgantukaṃ tathā //
:n
1 vidhureveti kha.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 224
343.d:
निजमागन्तुकञ्चेति द्विविधं तदुदाहृतम् /
सांसिद्धिकं नियं नैमित्तिकमागन्तुकं तथा //
:न्
1 विधुरेवेति ख.. , ट.. च
:प् 224
343.m:
It is declared to be of two kinds: innate and adventitious; / the innate is natural, and the adventitious is occasional.
[Footnote]
1. "vidhureva" in manuscripts kha and ṭa. / [Page 224]

343.s:
sādṛśyaṃ dharmasāmānyamupamā rūpakaṃ tathā /
mahoktyarthāntaranyāsāviti syāttu caturvidham //
343.d:
सादृश्यं धर्मसामान्यमुपमा रूपकं तथा /
महोक्त्यर्थान्तरन्यासाविति स्यात्तु चतुर्विधम् //
343.m: Similarity is community of attributes; it is of four kinds: / simile, metaphor, connected expression, and corroboration.

343.s:
upamā nāma sā yasyāmupamānopameyayoḥ /
sattā cāntarasāmānyayogitvepi vivakṣitaṃ //
343.d:
उपमा नाम सा यस्यामुपमानोपमेययोः /
सत्ता चान्तरसामान्ययोगित्वेपि विवक्षितं //
343.m: A simile is that in which, between the standard of comparison and the object compared, / existence and connection with a shared commonality is intended to be expressed.

343.s:
kiñcidādāya sārūpyaṃ lokayātrā pravartate /
samāsenāsamāsena sā dvidhā pratiyoginaḥ //
343.d:
किञ्चिदादाय सारूप्यं लोकयात्रा प्रवर्तते /
समासेनासमासेन सा द्विधा प्रतियोगिनः //
343.m: Depending upon some measure of conformity, worldly interaction proceeds. / With respect to the counter-entity, it is of two kinds: compounded and uncompounded.

343.s:
vigrahādabhidhānasya sasamāsānyathottarā /
upamādyotakapadenopameyapadenaca //
343.d:
विग्रहादभिधानस्य ससमासान्यथोत्तरा /
उपमाद्योतकपदेनोपमेयपदेनच //
343.m: From the analytical resolution of the expression, it is compounded; otherwise it is the latter. / By means of a word indicating simile and by means of the word denoting the object compared,

343.s:
tābhyāñca vigrahāttredhā sasamāsāntimāt tridhā /
viśiṣyamāṇā upamā bhavantyaṣṭādaśa sphuṭāḥ //
343.d:
ताभ्याञ्च विग्रहात्त्रेधा ससमासान्तिमात् त्रिधा /
विशिष्यमाणा उपमा भवन्त्यष्टादश स्फुटाः //
343.m: and through analytical resolution of both, it is threefold; through the latter, compounded form, it is threefold. / Thus differentiated, similes clearly become eighteen.

343.s:
yatra sādhāraṇo dharmaḥ kathyate gamyate 'pi vā /
te dharmavastuprādhānyāddharmavastūpame ubhe //
343.d:
यत्र साधारणो धर्मः कथ्यते गम्यते ऽपि वा /
ते धर्मवस्तुप्राधान्याद्धर्मवस्तूपमे उभे //
343.m: Where a common property is explicitly stated or even implied, / these, through the prominence of the property or the object, are both similes of property and of object.

343.s:
tulyamevopamīyete yatrānyonyena dharmiṇau /
parasparopamā sā syāt prasiddheranyathā tayoḥ //
343.d:
तुल्यमेवोपमीयेते यत्रान्योन्येन धर्मिणौ /
परस्परोपमा सा स्यात् प्रसिद्धेरन्यथा तयोः //
343.m: Where two subjects of attributes are compared equally to each other, / that is mutual simile; from their being otherwise than conventional,

343.s:
viparītopamā sā syādvyāvṛtter niyamopamā /
anyatrāpyanuvṛttestu bhavedaniyamopamā //
343.d:
विपरीतोपमा सा स्याद्व्यावृत्तेर् नियमोपमा /
अन्यत्राप्यनुवृत्तेस्तु भवेदनियमोपमा //
343.m: that is inverted simile; through exclusion, it is restrictive simile; / but through applicability elsewhere as well, it becomes unrestrictive simile.

343.s:
samuccayopamāto 'nyadharmavāhulyakīrtanāt /
vahordhammasya sāmyepi vailakṣṇyaṃ vivakṣitaṃ //
343.d:
समुच्चयोपमातो ऽन्यधर्मवाहुल्यकीर्तनात् /
वहोर्धम्मस्य साम्येपि वैलक्ष्ण्यं विवक्षितं //
343.m: It is an aggregative simile from stating an abundance of other qualities; / even when there is similarity of many properties, distinction is intended to be expressed.

343.s:
yaducyate 'tiriktatvaṃ vyatirekopamā tu sā /
yatropamā syādvahubhiḥ sadṛśaiḥ sā bahūpamā //
dharmāḥ pratyupamānañcedanye mālopamaiva sāAP_343.015ab/
343.d:
यदुच्यते ऽतिरिक्तत्वं व्यतिरेकोपमा तु सा /
यत्रोपमा स्याद्वहुभिः सदृशैः सा बहूपमा //
धर्माः प्रत्युपमानञ्चेदन्ये मालोपमैव साअप्_343.015अब्/
343.m:
That which is stated as superiority is indeed simile of contrast; / where the comparison is made with many similar things, that is multiple simile.
If there are different attributes for each standard of comparison, that is a garland-simile;

343.s: upamānavikāreṇa tulanā vikriyopamā //
343.d: उपमानविकारेण तुलना विक्रियोपमा //
343.m: a comparison made through the alteration of the standard of comparison is a simile of transformation.

343.s:
trilokyāsambhavi kimapyāropya pratiyogini /
:p 225
kavinopamīyate yā prathate sādbhutopamā //
343.d:
त्रिलोक्यासम्भवि किमप्यारोप्य प्रतियोगिनि /
:प् 225
कविनोपमीयते या प्रथते साद्भुतोपमा //
343.m:
Superimposing something impossible in the three worlds onto the counter-entity,
[Page 225]
that comparison which is made by a poet is known as a simile of wonder.

343.s:
pratiyoginamāropya tadabhedena kīrtanam /
upameyasya sā mohopamāsau bhrāntimadvacaḥ //
343.d:
प्रतियोगिनमारोप्य तदभेदेन कीर्तनम् /
उपमेयस्य सा मोहोपमासौ भ्रान्तिमद्वचः //
343.m: Superimposing the counter-entity, declaring identity with it / for the object compared is a simile of delusion; it is an utterance involving error.

343.s:
ubhayordharmiṇostathyāniś cayāt saṃśayopamā /
upameyasya saṃśayya niś cayānniś cayopamā //
343.d:
उभयोर्धर्मिणोस्तथ्यानिश् चयात् संशयोपमा /
उपमेयस्य संशय्य निश् चयान्निश् चयोपमा //
343.m: From the non-determination of the truth of both subjects of attributes, it is a simile of doubt; / from the determination of the object compared after doubting, it is a simile of certainty.

343.s:
vākyārthanaiva vākyārthopamā syādupamānataḥ /
ātmanopamānādupamā sādhāraṇyatiśāyinī //
343.d:
वाक्यार्थनैव वाक्यार्थोपमा स्यादुपमानतः /
आत्मनोपमानादुपमा साधारण्यतिशायिनी //
343.m: Through sentence-meaning itself, there is a simile of sentence-meaning derived from a standard of comparison; / through comparison with oneself, it is an extraordinary commonality.

343.s:
upameyaṃ yadnyasya tadnyasyopamā matā /
yadyuttarottaraṃ yāti tadāsau gaganopamā(1) //
343.d:
उपमेयं यद्न्यस्य तद्न्यस्योपमा मता /
यद्युत्तरोत्तरं याति तदासौ गगनोपमा(1) //
343.m: Where the object compared of one becomes the standard of comparison for another, / if it proceeds progressively, then it is a sky-simile.

343.s:
praśaṃsā caiva nindā ca kalpitā sadṛśī tathā /
kiñcicca sadṛśī jñeyā upamā pañcadhā puraḥ //
343.d:
प्रशंसा चैव निन्दा च कल्पिता सदृशी तथा /
किञ्चिच्च सदृशी ज्ञेया उपमा पञ्चधा पुरः //
343.m: Praise, censure, imagined, similar, / and partially similar: simile should be known as fivefold previously [in another classification].

343.s:
upamānena yattatvamupameyasya rūpyate /
guṇānāṃ samatāṃ dṛṣṭvā rūpakaṃ nāma tadviduḥ //
343.d:
उपमानेन यत्तत्वमुपमेयस्य रूप्यते /
गुणानां समतां दृष्ट्वा रूपकं नाम तद्विदुः //
343.m: When the nature of the object compared is represented by the standard of comparison / upon observing equality of attributes, the wise know that as metaphor.

343.s:
upamaiva tirobhūtabhedā rūpakameva vā /
sahoktiḥ sahabhāvena kathanaṃ tulyadharmiṇāṃ //
343.d:
उपमैव तिरोभूतभेदा रूपकमेव वा /
सहोक्तिः सहभावेन कथनं तुल्यधर्मिणां //
343.m: Metaphor is indeed simile with difference concealed. / Connected expression is the statement together of things having equal attributes.

343.s:
bhavedarthāntaranyāsaḥ sādṛśyenottareṇa saḥ /
anyathopasthitā vṛttiścetanasyetarasya ca //
343.d:
भवेदर्थान्तरन्यासः सादृश्येनोत्तरेण सः /
अन्यथोपस्थिता वृत्तिश्चेतनस्येतरस्य च //
343.m: Corroboration arises through similarity or through a subsequent [general statement]. / When the behavior of a sentient or non-sentient entity, being presented in one way,

343.s:
anyathā manyate yatra tāmutprekṣāṃ pracakṣate /
lokasīmānvṛttasya vastudharmasya kīrtanam //
343.d:
अन्यथा मन्यते यत्र तामुत्प्रेक्षां प्रचक्षते /
लोकसीमान्वृत्तस्य वस्तुधर्मस्य कीर्तनम् //
343.m: is imagined in another way, they call that poetic fancy. / The declaration of a property of an entity that transcends worldly boundaries

343.s:
bhavedatiśayo nāma sambhavāsambhavāddvidhā /
guṇajātikriyādīnāṃ yatra vaikalyardarśanaṃ //
343.d:
भवेदतिशयो नाम सम्भवासम्भवाद्द्विधा /
गुणजातिक्रियादीनां यत्र वैकल्यर्दर्शनं //
343.m: is hyperbole; it is of two kinds: through possibility and impossibility. / Where there is an exhibition of deficiency in qualities, genus, action, and the like,

343.s:
viśeṣadarśanāyaiva sā viśeṣoktirucyate /
:n
1 pavanopameti kha.. / gamanopameti ka.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 226
prasiddhahetuvyāvṛtyā yat kiñcit kāraṇāntaram //
343.d:
विशेषदर्शनायैव सा विशेषोक्तिरुच्यते /
:न्
1 पवनोपमेति ख.. / गमनोपमेति क.. , ट.. च
:प् 226
प्रसिद्धहेतुव्यावृत्या यत् किञ्चित् कारणान्तरम् //
343.m:
solely to show excellence, that is called statement of distinction.
[Footnote]
1. "pavanopamā" in manuscript kha; "gamanopamā" in manuscripts ka and ṭa. / [Page 226]
When, by setting aside an established cause, some other cause

343.s:
yatra svābhāvikatvaṃ vā vibhāvyaṃ sā vibhāvanā /
saṅgatīkaraṇaṃ yuktyā yadasaṃgacchamānayoḥ //
343.d:
यत्र स्वाभाविकत्वं वा विभाव्यं सा विभावना /
सङ्गतीकरणं युक्त्या यदसंगच्छमानयोः //
343.m: or naturalness is to be conceived, that is peculiar causation. / The reconciliation through reasoning of two things that are incompatible,

343.s:
virodhapūrvakatvena tadvirodha iti smṛtaṃ /
sisādhayiṣitārthasya heturbhavati sādhakaḥ //
343.d:
विरोधपूर्वकत्वेन तद्विरोध इति स्मृतं /
सिसाधयिषितार्थस्य हेतुर्भवति साधकः //
343.m: because it is preceded by contradiction, is remembered as contradiction. / A reason is that which establishes a matter intended to be proved.

343.s:
kārako jñāpaka iti dvidhā so 'pyupajāyate /
pravartate kārakākhyaḥ prāk paścāt kāryajanmanaḥ //
343.d:
कारको ज्ञापक इति द्विधा सो ऽप्युपजायते /
प्रवर्तते कारकाख्यः प्राक् पश्चात् कार्यजन्मनः //
343.m: That too arises twofold: producing and indicating. / That named 'producing' operates before and after the birth of the effect,

343.s:
pūrvaśeṣa iti khyātastayoreva viśeṣayoḥ /
kāryakāraṇabhāvādvā svamāvādvā niyāmakāt //
343.d:
पूर्वशेष इति ख्यातस्तयोरेव विशेषयोः /
कार्यकारणभावाद्वा स्वमावाद्वा नियामकात् //
343.m: and is known as antecedent and consequent in those two distinctions; / either from the relation of cause and effect, or from inherent nature as a determinant,

343.s:
jñāpakākhyasya bhedo 'sti nadīpūrādidarśanāt /
avinābhāvaniyamo hy avinābhāvadarśanāt //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe alaṅkāre arthālaṅkāranirūpaṇaṃ
nāma tricatvāriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha catuś catvāriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
śabdārthālaṅkārāḥ
343.d:
ज्ञापकाख्यस्य भेदो ऽस्ति नदीपूरादिदर्शनात् /
अविनाभावनियमो ह्य् अविनाभावदर्शनात् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे अलङ्कारे अर्थालङ्कारनिरूपणं
नाम त्रिचत्वारिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ चतुश् चत्वारिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
शब्दार्थालङ्काराः
343.m:
there is a division of the indicator, as from the observation of a river-flood and the like; / for the rule of invariable concomitance exists because of the observation of invariable concomitance.
Thus ends the three hundred and forty-third chapter in the great Agni Purāṇa, on Poetics, titled "Exposition of Figures of Sense".
Now begins the three hundred and forty-fourth chapter.
Figures of Sound and Sense

344.s:
agnir uvāca
śabdārthayoralaṅkāro dvāvalaṅkurute samaṃ /
ekatra nihito hāraḥ stanaṃ grīvāmiva striyāḥ //
344.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
शब्दार्थयोरलङ्कारो द्वावलङ्कुरुते समं /
एकत्र निहितो हारः स्तनं ग्रीवामिव स्त्रियाः //
344.m: Agni said: / An ornament of both word and meaning adorns both equally, / like a necklace placed in one spot [adorns] both the breast and the neck of a woman.

344.s:
praśastiḥ kāntiraucityaṃ saṃkṣepo yāvadarthatā /
abhivyaktiriti vyaktaṃ ṣaḍbhedāstasya jāgrati //
344.d:
प्रशस्तिः कान्तिरौचित्यं संक्षेपो यावदर्थता /
अभिव्यक्तिरिति व्यक्तं षड्भेदास्तस्य जाग्रति //
344.m: Praise, grace, propriety, conciseness, exact measure of meaning, / and manifestation: clearly these six divisions are recognised.

344.s:
praśastiḥ paravanmarmadravīkaraṇakarmaṇaḥ /
vāco yuktirdvidhā sā ca premoktistutibhedataḥ //
:p 227
344.d:
प्रशस्तिः परवन्मर्मद्रवीकरणकर्मणः /
वाचो युक्तिर्द्विधा सा च प्रेमोक्तिस्तुतिभेदतः //
:प् 227
344.m:
Praise is the application of speech that melts the innermost heart of another; / and that is twofold, divided into words of affection and eulogy.
[Page 227]
Words of affection and eulogy are synonyms for speaking lovingly and reciting virtues. / Grace is the harmonious connection of the expressed and the unexpressed pleasing to everyone’s mind.

344.s:
yathā vastu tathā rītiryathā vṛttis tathā rasaḥ /
ūrjasvimṛdusandarbhādaucityamupajāyate //
344.d:
यथा वस्तु तथा रीतिर्यथा वृत्तिस् तथा रसः /
ऊर्जस्विमृदुसन्दर्भादौचित्यमुपजायते //
344.m: As is the subject matter, so is the style; as is the dramatic mode, so is the aesthetic sentiment. / Propriety arises from forceful or soft composition.

344.s:
saṃkṣepo vācakair alpair vahorarthasya saṃgrahaḥ /
anyūnādhikatā śabdavastunoryāvadarthatā //
344.d:
संक्षेपो वाचकैर् अल्पैर् वहोरर्थस्य संग्रहः /
अन्यूनाधिकता शब्दवस्तुनोर्यावदर्थता //
344.m: Conciseness is the comprehension of much meaning through few expressive words. / Exact measure of meaning is the absence of deficiency or excess between word and subject matter.

344.s:
prakaṭatvamabhivyaktiḥ śrutirākṣepa ity api /
tasyā bhedau śrutistatra śabdaṃ svārthasamarpaṇam //
344.d:
प्रकटत्वमभिव्यक्तिः श्रुतिराक्षेप इत्य् अपि /
तस्या भेदौ श्रुतिस्तत्र शब्दं स्वार्थसमर्पणम् //
344.m: Manifestation is clarity; it has two varieties: / literal sense and implied sense. There, literal sense is the word's delivery of its own meaning.

344.s:
bhavennaimittikī pāribhāṣikī dvividhaiva sā /
saṅketaḥ paribhāṣeti tataḥ syāt pāribhāṣikī //
344.d:
भवेन्नैमित्तिकी पारिभाषिकी द्विविधैव सा /
सङ्केतः परिभाषेति ततः स्यात् पारिभाषिकी //
344.m: It is twofold: causal and conventional. / Convention is technical usage; arising from that, it is conventional.

344.s:
mukhyaupacārikī ceti sā ca sā ca dvidhā dvidhā /
svābhidheyaskhaladvṛttiramukhyārthasya vācakaḥ //
344.d:
मुख्यौपचारिकी चेति सा च सा च द्विधा द्विधा /
स्वाभिधेयस्खलद्वृत्तिरमुख्यार्थस्य वाचकः //
344.m: And both of those are twofold: primary and metaphorical. / When the function of its primary designation slips, the signifier expresses a secondary meaning.

344.s:
yayā śabdo nimittena kenacitsaupacārikī /
sā ca lākṣaṇikī gauṇī lakṣaṇāguṇayogataḥ //
344.d:
यया शब्दो निमित्तेन केनचित्सौपचारिकी /
सा च लाक्षणिकी गौणी लक्षणागुणयोगतः //
344.m: The function through which a word operates by some occasion is metaphorical; / and that is twofold: indicative and qualitative, based on indication and association of qualities.
An apprehension inextricably bound up with the primary meaning is called indication. / From relation to the designated, from proximity, from inherence,
from opposition, and from connection with action, indication is held to be fivefold. / The qualitative is endless because qualities are endless according to the speaker’s intention.

344.s:
anyadharmastato 'nyatra lokasīmānurodhinā /
samyagādhīyate yatra sa samādhiriha smṛtaḥ //
344.d:
अन्यधर्मस्ततो ऽन्यत्र लोकसीमानुरोधिना /
सम्यगाधीयते यत्र स समाधिरिह स्मृतः //
344.m: Where an attribute belonging to one thing is properly superinduced upon another, / conforming to worldly convention, that is remembered here as superimposition.

344.s:
śrūteralabhyamāno 'rtho yasmādbhāti sacetanaḥ /
sa ākṣepo dhaniḥ syācca dhvaninā vyajyate yataḥ //
344.d:
श्रूतेरलभ्यमानो ऽर्थो यस्माद्भाति सचेतनः /
स आक्षेपो धनिः स्याच्च ध्वनिना व्यज्यते यतः //
344.m: Because a meaning not directly obtained from hearing shines forth as endowed with consciousness, / that is paralipsis; and it is suggestion, because it is manifested through resonance.

344.s:
śabdenārthena yatrārthaḥ kṛtvā svayamupārjanam /
:p 228
pratiṣedha iveṣṭasya yo viśeṣo 'bhidhitsayā //
344.d:
शब्देनार्थेन यत्रार्थः कृत्वा स्वयमुपार्जनम् /
:प् 228
प्रतिषेध इवेष्टस्य यो विशेषो ऽभिधित्सया //
344.m:
Where, having effected its own acquisition by means of word and meaning,
[Page 228]
a seeming prohibition of what is desired [is used] in order to express a distinction,

344.s:
tamākṣepaṃ vruvantyatra stutaṃ stotramidaṃ punaḥ /
adhikārādapetasya vastuno 'nyasya yā stutiḥ //
344.d:
तमाक्षेपं व्रुवन्त्यत्र स्तुतं स्तोत्रमिदं पुनः /
अधिकारादपेतस्य वस्तुनो ऽन्यस्य या स्तुतिः //
344.m: they call that paralipsis. Again, this praise is laudation; / when there is praise of another subject that lies outside the immediate scope,

344.s:
yatroktaṃ gamyate nārthastatsamānaviśeṣaṇaṃ /
sā samāsokitiruditā saṅkṣepārthatayā budhaiḥ //
344.d:
यत्रोक्तं गम्यते नार्थस्तत्समानविशेषणं /
सा समासोकितिरुदिता सङ्क्षेपार्थतया बुधैः //
344.m: and where a meaning not directly stated is understood through identical adjectives, / that has been declared by the wise as concise speech on account of its brevity of meaning.

344.s:
apahnutirapahnutya kiñcidanyārthasūcanam /
paryāyoktaṃ yadanyena prakārenābhidhīyate /
eṣāmekaṃtamasyeva samākhyā dhvanirityataḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe alaṅkāre śabdarthālaṅkāranirūpaṇaṃ
nāma catuś catvāriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha pañcacatvāriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
kāvyaguṇavivekaḥ
344.d:
अपह्नुतिरपह्नुत्य किञ्चिदन्यार्थसूचनम् /
पर्यायोक्तं यदन्येन प्रकारेनाभिधीयते /
एषामेकंतमस्येव समाख्या ध्वनिरित्यतः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे अलङ्कारे शब्दर्थालङ्कारनिरूपणं
नाम चतुश् चत्वारिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ पञ्चचत्वारिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
काव्यगुणविवेकः
344.m:
Concealment is the indication of some other meaning by concealing [the actual one]. / Periphrasis is when something is expressed in an alternative manner. / Therefore, the single designation for these is suggestion.
Thus ends the three hundred and forty-fourth chapter, named 'The Exposition of the Ornaments of Word and Meaning in Poetics,' in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the three hundred and forty-fifth chapter:
Examination of poetic excellences.

345.s:
agnir uvāca
alaṃkṛtamapi prītyai na kāvyaṃ nirguṇaṃ bhavet /
vapuṣyalalite strīṇāṃ hāro bhārāyate paraṃ //
345.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
अलंकृतमपि प्रीत्यै न काव्यं निर्गुणं भवेत् /
वपुष्यललिते स्त्रीणां हारो भारायते परं //
345.m: Agni said: / Even if ornamented, a poem devoid of excellences will not cause delight; / on the charming body of women, a necklace is merely a burden.

345.s:
na ca vācyaṃ guṇo doṣo bhāva eva bhaviṣyati /
guṇāḥ śleṣādayo doṣā gūḍārthādyāḥ pṛthakkṛtāḥ //
345.d:
न च वाच्यं गुणो दोषो भाव एव भविष्यति /
गुणाः श्लेषादयो दोषा गूडार्थाद्याः पृथक्कृताः //
345.m: Nor should it be said that excellence is merely the absence of fault; / the excellences, such as cohesion, and the faults, such as obscurity of meaning, are distinguished.

345.s:
yaḥ kāvye mahatīṃ chāyāmanugṛhṇātyasau guṇaiḥ /
sambhavatyeṣa sāmānyo vaiśeṣika iti dvidhā //
345.d:
यः काव्ये महतीं छायामनुगृह्णात्यसौ गुणैः /
सम्भवत्येष सामान्यो वैशेषिक इति द्विधा //
345.m: That which confers great brilliance upon a poem is an excellence; / it is twofold: common and specific.

345.s:
sarvasādhāraṇībhūtaḥ sāmanya iti manyate /
śabdamarthamubhau prāptaḥ sāmānyo bhavati tridhā //
345.d:
सर्वसाधारणीभूतः सामन्य इति मन्यते /
शब्दमर्थमुभौ प्राप्तः सामान्यो भवति त्रिधा //
345.m: The common [excellence] is considered universal to all. / Pertaining to word, meaning, or both, the common is threefold.

345.s:
śabdamāśrayate kāvyaṃ śarīraṃ yaḥ sa tadguṇaḥ /
:p 229
śloṣo lālityāgāmbhīryasaukumāryamudāratā //
345.d:
शब्दमाश्रयते काव्यं शरीरं यः स तद्गुणः /
:प् 229
श्लोषो लालित्यागाम्भीर्यसौकुमार्यमुदारता //
345.m:
That which inheres in the word—the body of poetry—is its verbal excellence:
[Page 229]
cohesion, gracefulness, depth, smoothness, nobility,

345.s:
satyeva yaugikī ceti guṇāḥ śabdasya saptadhā /
suśliṣṭasanniveśatvaṃ śabdānāṃ śleṣa ucyate //
345.d:
सत्येव यौगिकी चेति गुणाः शब्दस्य सप्तधा /
सुश्लिष्टसन्निवेशत्वं शब्दानां श्लेष उच्यते //
345.m: truthfulness, and syntactical coherence—thus the verbal excellences are of seven kinds. / The well-knit arrangement of words is called cohesion.

345.s:
guṇādeśādinā pūrvaṃ padasambaddhamakṣaraṃ /
yatrasandhīyate naiva tallālityamudāhṛtaṃ //
345.d:
गुणादेशादिना पूर्वं पदसम्बद्धमक्षरं /
यत्रसन्धीयते नैव तल्लालित्यमुदाहृतं //
345.m: Where a syllable previously joined in a word by quality, substitute, or the like / does not combine [further] into euphonic union, that is cited as gracefulness.

345.s:
viśiṣṭalakṣaṇollekhalekhyamuttānaśabdakam /
gāmbhīryaṃ kathayantyāryāstadevānyeṣu śabdatāṃ //
345.d:
विशिष्टलक्षणोल्लेखलेख्यमुत्तानशब्दकम् /
गाम्भीर्यं कथयन्त्यार्यास्तदेवान्येषु शब्दतां //
345.m: Noble persons call depth that which consists of superficial words capable of being interpreted with distinguished characteristics; / and others call it verbality in other contexts.

345.s:
aniṣṭhurākṣaraprāyaśabdatā sukumāratā /
uttānapadataudaryayutaślāghyair viśeṣaṇaiḥ //
345.d:
अनिष्ठुराक्षरप्रायशब्दता सुकुमारता /
उत्तानपदतौदर्ययुतश्लाघ्यैर् विशेषणैः //
345.m: Smoothness is a phrasing predominantly composed of unharsh syllables. / Nobility consists of clear words accompanied by praiseworthy qualifying adjectives.

345.s:
ojaḥ samāsabhūyastvametatpadyādijīvitaṃ /
ābrahma stambhaparyantamojasaikena pauruṣaṃ //
345.d:
ओजः समासभूयस्त्वमेतत्पद्यादिजीवितं /
आब्रह्म स्तम्भपर्यन्तमोजसैकेन पौरुषं //
345.m: Vigour is an abundance of compounds; this is the very life of metrical verse and the like. / From Brahmā down to a clump of grass, virility is achieved through vigour alone.

345.s:
ucyamānasya śabdena yena kenāpi vastunaḥ /
utkarṣamāvahannartho guṇa ity abhidhīyate //
345.d:
उच्यमानस्य शब्देन येन केनापि वस्तुनः /
उत्कर्षमावहन्नर्थो गुण इत्य् अभिधीयते //
345.m: A meaning that brings excellence to any subject whatsoever / that is being spoken of by a word is called an ideal excellence.

345.s:
mādhuryaṃ sambidhānañca komalatvamudāratā /
prauḍhiḥ sāmayikatvañca tadbhedāḥ ṣaṭcakāśati //
345.d:
माधुर्यं सम्बिधानञ्च कोमलत्वमुदारता /
प्रौढिः सामयिकत्वञ्च तद्भेदाः षट्चकाशति //
345.m: Sweetness, orderly arrangement, delicacy, nobility, / maturity, and conventional correctness: its six varieties shine forth.

345.s:
krodherṣyākāragāmbhīryātmādhuryaṃ dhairyagāhitā /
sambidhānaṃ parikaraḥ syādapekṣitasiddhaye //
345.d:
क्रोधेर्ष्याकारगाम्भीर्यात्माधुर्यं धैर्यगाहिता /
सम्बिधानं परिकरः स्यादपेक्षितसिद्धये //
345.m: Sweetness is the plunging into fortitude out of profundity despite wrath, jealousy, and passion. / Orderly arrangement is the preparation [of elements] for the attainment of the desired effect.

345.s:
yatkāṭhinyādinirmuktasanniveśaviśiṣṭatā /
tiraskṛtyaiva mṛdutā bhāti komalateti sā //
345.d:
यत्काठिन्यादिनिर्मुक्तसन्निवेशविशिष्टता /
तिरस्कृत्यैव मृदुता भाति कोमलतेति सा //
345.m: When a distinction of composition freed from harshness and the like / shines forth, having set aside all softness, that is delicacy.

345.s:
lakṣyate sthūlalakṣatvapravṛtteryatra lakṣaṇam /
guṇasya tadudāratvamāśayasyātisauṣṭhavaṃ //
345.d:
लक्ष्यते स्थूललक्षत्वप्रवृत्तेर्यत्र लक्षणम् /
गुणस्य तदुदारत्वमाशयस्यातिसौष्ठवं //
345.m: Where the characteristic mark of the operation of generosity is observed, / that is the excellence of nobility, the supreme soundness of intention.

345.s:
abhipretaṃ prati yato nirvāhasyopapādikāḥ /
yuktayo hetugarbhiṇyaḥ prauḍhāprauḍhirudāhṛtā //
:p 230
345.d:
अभिप्रेतं प्रति यतो निर्वाहस्योपपादिकाः /
युक्तयो हेतुगर्भिण्यः प्रौढाप्रौढिरुदाहृता //
:प् 230
345.m:
Reasonings pregnant with causes which demonstrate the accomplishment / of what is intended: this maturity is cited as mature.
[Page 230]

345.s:
svatantrasyānyatantrasya vāhyāntaḥsamayogataḥ /
tatra vyutpattirarthasya yā sāmayikateti sā //
345.d:
स्वतन्त्रस्यान्यतन्त्रस्य वाह्यान्तःसमयोगतः /
तत्र व्युत्पत्तिरर्थस्य या सामयिकतेति सा //
345.m: When, through the union of external and internal relations of what is independent or dependent, / there is understanding of the meaning, that is conventional correctness.

345.s:
śabdārthavupakurvāṇo nāmnobhayaguṇaḥ smṛtaḥ /
tasya prasādaḥ saubhāgyaṃ yathāsaṅkhyaṃ praśastatā //
345.d:
शब्दार्थवुपकुर्वाणो नाम्नोभयगुणः स्मृतः /
तस्य प्रसादः सौभाग्यं यथासङ्ख्यं प्रशस्तता //
345.m: That which benefits both word and meaning is known by the name 'excellence of both.' / Clarity, elegance, numerical correspondence, laudableness,

345.s:
pāko rāga iti prājñaiḥ ṣaṭprapañcavipañcitāḥ /
suprasiddharthapadatā prasāda iti gīyate //
345.d:
पाको राग इति प्राज्ञैः षट्प्रपञ्चविपञ्चिताः /
सुप्रसिद्धर्थपदता प्रसाद इति गीयते //
345.m: ripeness, and colour: [these] six are expounded in detail by the wise. / The use of words with well-known meanings is celebrated as clarity.

345.s:
utkarṣavān guṇaḥ kaścidyasminnukte pratīyate /
tatsaubhāgyamudāratvaṃ pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ //
345.d:
उत्कर्षवान् गुणः कश्चिद्यस्मिन्नुक्ते प्रतीयते /
तत्सौभाग्यमुदारत्वं प्रवदन्ति मनीषिणः //
345.m: When an utterance is spoken and some exalted quality is perceived therein, / wise men declare that to be elegance and nobility.

345.s:
yathāsaṅkhyamanuddeśaḥ sāmanyamatidiśyate /
samaye varṇanīyasya dāruṇasyāpi vastunaḥ //
345.d:
यथासङ्ख्यमनुद्देशः सामन्यमतिदिश्यते /
समये वर्णनीयस्य दारुणस्यापि वस्तुनः //
345.m: Numerical correspondence is the parallel ordering [of items] matching each other. / When, at the time [of narration], even a terrifying subject

345.s:
adāruṇena śabdena prāśastyamupavarṇanaṃ /
uccaiḥ pariṇatiḥ kāpi pāka ity abhidhīyate //
345.d:
अदारुणेन शब्देन प्राशस्त्यमुपवर्णनं /
उच्चैः परिणतिः कापि पाक इत्य् अभिधीयते //
345.m: is described in un-terrifying language, that laudableness is praise. / A certain lofty maturation is designated as ripeness.

345.s:
mṛdvīkānārikelāmbupākabhedāccaturvidhaḥ /
ādāvante ca saurasyaṃ mṛdvīkāpāka eva saḥ //
345.d:
मृद्वीकानारिकेलाम्बुपाकभेदाच्चतुर्विधः /
आदावन्ते च सौरस्यं मृद्वीकापाक एव सः //
345.m: It is of four kinds through the divisions of grape ripeness, coconut-water ripeness, and so forth. / That which possesses delicious flavor at the beginning and at the end is grape ripeness.

345.s:
kāvyecchayā viśeṣo yaḥ sarāga iti gīyate /
abhyāsopahitaḥ kāntiṃ sahajāmapi vartate //
345.d:
काव्येच्छया विशेषो यः सराग इति गीयते /
अभ्यासोपहितः कान्तिं सहजामपि वर्तते //
345.m: That distinctive trait which is sung through the desire of the poem is called colour; / brought about by constant practice, it surpasses even natural beauty.

345.s:
hāridraś caiva kausumbho nīlī rāgaś ca sa tridhā /
vaiśeṣikaḥ parijñeyo yaḥ svalakṣaṇagocaraḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe kāvyaguṇaviveko nāma
pañcacatvāriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:p 231
:ś atha ṣaṭcatvāriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
kāvyadoṣavivekaḥ
345.d:
हारिद्रश् चैव कौसुम्भो नीली रागश् च स त्रिधा /
वैशेषिकः परिज्ञेयो यः स्वलक्षणगोचरः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे काव्यगुणविवेको नाम
पञ्चचत्वारिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:प् 231
:श् अथ षट्चत्वारिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
काव्यदोषविवेकः
345.m:
And that colour is threefold: like turmeric, safflower, or indigo. / The specific excellence should be understood as that which falls within the sphere of its own definition.
Thus ends the three hundred and forty-fifth chapter, named 'The Examination of Poetic Excellences,' in the great Agni Purāṇa. / [Page 231]
Now begins the three hundred and forty-sixth chapter:
Examination of poetic faults.

346.s:
agnir uvāca
udvegajanako doṣaḥ sabhyānāṃ sa ca saptadhā /
vaktṛvācakavācyānāmekadvitriniyogataḥ //
346.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
उद्वेगजनको दोषः सभ्यानां स च सप्तधा /
वक्तृवाचकवाच्यानामेकद्वित्रिनियोगतः //
346.m: Agni said: / A fault is that which causes distress to cultured critics; and it is sevenfold, / through the application of one, two, or all three of speaker, expression, and the expressed.

346.s:
tatra vaktā kavirnāma prathate sa ca bhedataḥ /
sandihāno 'vinītaḥ sannajño jñātā caturvidhaḥ //
346.d:
तत्र वक्ता कविर्नाम प्रथते स च भेदतः /
सन्दिहानो ऽविनीतः सन्नज्ञो ज्ञाता चतुर्विधः //
346.m: Therein, the speaker is known as the poet, and he is distinguished / as fourfold: doubtful, ill-mannered, ignorant, and learned.

346.s:
nimittaparibhāṣābhyāmarthasaṃsparśivācakam /
tadbhedo padavākye dve kathitaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ dvayoḥ //
346.d:
निमित्तपरिभाषाभ्यामर्थसंस्पर्शिवाचकम् /
तद्भेदो पदवाक्ये द्वे कथितं लक्षणं द्वयोः //
346.m: The signifier touches the meaning through its occasion and conventional usage; / its divisions are twofold, word and sentence; the definition of both has been declared.

346.s:
asādhutvāprayuktve dvāveva padanigrahau /
śabdaśāstraviruddhatvamasādhutvaṃ vidurbudhāḥ //
346.d:
असाधुत्वाप्रयुक्त्वे द्वावेव पदनिग्रहौ /
शब्दशास्त्रविरुद्धत्वमसाधुत्वं विदुर्बुधाः //
346.m: Ungrammaticality and lack of usage are indeed two faults of a word; / the wise know ungrammaticality to be contrariety to grammar.

346.s:
vyutpannair anibadvatvamaprayuktatvamucyate /
chāndasatvamavispaṣṭatvañca kaṣṭatvameva ca //
346.d:
व्युत्पन्नैर् अनिबद्वत्वमप्रयुक्तत्वमुच्यते /
छान्दसत्वमविस्पष्टत्वञ्च कष्टत्वमेव च //
346.m: Lack of usage is said to be absence of employment by the learned; / archaism, unclearness, and harshness,

346.s:
tadasāmayikatvañca grāmyatvañceti pañcadhā /
chāndasatvaṃ na bhāṣāyāmavispaṣṭamabodhataḥ //
346.d:
तदसामयिकत्वञ्च ग्राम्यत्वञ्चेति पञ्चधा /
छान्दसत्वं न भाषायामविस्पष्टमबोधतः //
346.m: unconventionality, and vulgarity—thus it is fivefold. / Archaism belongs not to ordinary speech; unclearness arises from non-comprehension.

346.s:
gūḍārthatā viparyastārthatā saṃśayitārthatā /
aviṣpaṣṭārthatā bhedāstatra gūḍhārthateti sā //
346.d:
गूडार्थता विपर्यस्तार्थता संशयितार्थता /
अविष्पष्टार्थता भेदास्तत्र गूढार्थतेति सा //
346.m: Obscure meaning, perverse meaning, doubtful meaning, / and unclear meaning are its varieties; among these, obscure meaning is that

346.s:
yatrārtho duḥkhasavedyo viparyastārthatā punaḥ /
vivakṣitānyaśabdārthapratipātirmalīmasā(1) //
346.d:
यत्रार्थो दुःखसवेद्यो विपर्यस्तार्थता पुनः /
विवक्षितान्यशब्दार्थप्रतिपातिर्मलीमसा(1) //
346.m: wherein the meaning is understood with difficulty; perverse meaning, again, / is an impure cognition of a meaning of a word other than the intended one.

346.s:
anyārthatvāsamarthatve etāmevopasarpataḥ /
:n
1 manīṣayeti ja..
:p 232
sandihyamānavācyatvamāhuḥ saṃśayitārthatāṃ //
346.d:
अन्यार्थत्वासमर्थत्वे एतामेवोपसर्पतः /
:न्
1 मनीषयेति ज..
:प् 232
सन्दिह्यमानवाच्यत्वमाहुः संशयितार्थतां //
346.m:
Having an unintended meaning and incapacity verge upon this very [fault].
[Footnote]
1 [Variant] "by the intellect" in the manuscript ja..
[Page 232]
They declare doubtful meaning to be that wherein the signified is dubious.

346.s:
doṣatvamanubadhnāti sajjanodvejanādṛte /
asukhoccāryamāṇatvaṃ kaṣṭatvaṃ samayācyutiḥ //
346.d:
दोषत्वमनुबध्नाति सज्जनोद्वेजनादृते /
असुखोच्चार्यमाणत्वं कष्टत्वं समयाच्युतिः //
346.m: It incurs faultiness without distressing the cultured; / harshness is difficulty of pronunciation; lapse from convention

346.s:
asāmayikatā neyāmetāñca munayo jaguḥ /
grāmyatā tu jaghanyārthapratipātiḥ khalīkṛtā //
346.d:
असामयिकता नेयामेताञ्च मुनयो जगुः /
ग्राम्यता तु जघन्यार्थप्रतिपातिः खलीकृता //
346.m: is unconventionality, which sages have declared must be deduced. / Vulgarity, however, is a vile cognition of a base meaning.

346.s:
vaktavyagrāmyavācyasya vacanātsmaraṇādapi /
tadvācakapadenābhisāmyādbhavati sā tridhā //
346.d:
वक्तव्यग्राम्यवाच्यस्य वचनात्स्मरणादपि /
तद्वाचकपदेनाभिसाम्याद्भवति सा त्रिधा //
346.m: It is threefold: through the utterance or even recollection of an unmentionable vulgar signified, / and through phonetic similarity with the word signifying that.

346.s:
doṣaḥ sādhāraṇaḥ prātisviko 'rthasya sa tu dvidhā /
anekabhāgupālambhaḥ sādhāraṇa iti smṛtaḥ //
346.d:
दोषः साधारणः प्रातिस्विको ऽर्थस्य स तु द्विधा /
अनेकभागुपालम्भः साधारण इति स्मृतः //
346.m: The fault of meaning is twofold: common and specific. / That which touches many parts is traditionally considered common.

346.s:
kriyākārakayorbhraṃśo visandhiḥ punaruktā /
vyastasambandhatā ceti pañca sādhāraṇā matāḥ(1) //
346.d:
क्रियाकारकयोर्भ्रंशो विसन्धिः पुनरुक्ता /
व्यस्तसम्बन्धता चेति पञ्च साधारणा मताः(1) //
346.m: Loss of verb and syntactic factor, hiatus, tautology, / and broken connection—these five are regarded as common.

346.s:
akriyatvaṃ kriyābhraṃśo bhraṣṭakārakatā punaḥ /
kartryādikārakābhāvo visandhiḥsandhidūṣaṇam //
346.d:
अक्रियत्वं क्रियाभ्रंशो भ्रष्टकारकता पुनः /
कर्त्र्यादिकारकाभावो विसन्धिःसन्धिदूषणम् //
346.m: Absence of a verb is loss of verb; loss of syntactic factor, again, / is absence of the agent and other factors; hiatus is a defect of euphonic junction.

346.s:
vigato vā viruddho vā sandhiḥ sa bhavati dvidhā /
sandherviruddhatā kaṣṭapādādarthāntarāgamāt(2) //
346.d:
विगतो वा विरुद्धो वा सन्धिः स भवति द्विधा /
सन्धेर्विरुद्धता कष्टपादादर्थान्तरागमात्(2) //
346.m: It is twofold: absent junction or contradictory junction; / contrariety of junction arises from a harsh metrical foot or the intrusion of an inappropriate meaning.

346.s:
punaruktatvamābhīkṣṇyādabhidhānaṃ dvidhaiva tat /
arthāvṛttiḥ padāvṛttirarthāvṛttirapi dvidhā //
346.d:
पुनरुक्तत्वमाभीक्ष्ण्यादभिधानं द्विधैव तत् /
अर्थावृत्तिः पदावृत्तिरर्थावृत्तिरपि द्विधा //
346.m: Tautology is an utterance made repeatedly; it is twofold: / repetition of meaning and repetition of words; repetition of meaning is also twofold,

346.s:
prayuktavaraśabdena(3) tathā śabdāntareṇa ca /
nāvartate padāvṛttau vācyamāvartate padam //
346.d:
प्रयुक्तवरशब्देन(3) तथा शब्दान्तरेण च /
नावर्तते पदावृत्तौ वाच्यमावर्तते पदम् //
346.m: through the very word previously used, or by another word; / in repetition of words, the signified is not repeated, but the word is repeated.

346.s:
vyastasambandhatā suṣṭhusambandho vyavadhānataḥ /
sambandhāntaranirbhāṣāt sambandhāntarajanmanaḥ //
:n
1 malā iti ka.. , ja.. ca
2 kaṣṭapādādarthāntarakramāditi ṭa..
3 prayuktacaraśabdeneti ja.. , ña.. ca
:p 233
346.d:
व्यस्तसम्बन्धता सुष्ठुसम्बन्धो व्यवधानतः /
सम्बन्धान्तरनिर्भाषात् सम्बन्धान्तरजन्मनः //
:न्
1 मला इति क.. , ज.. च
2 कष्टपादादर्थान्तरक्रमादिति ट..
3 प्रयुक्तचरशब्देनेति ज.. , ञ.. च
:प् 233
346.m:
Broken connection is [where] a well-formed syntactical connection [is disrupted] due to separation, / the manifestation of another connection, or the generation of another connection.
[Footnote]
1 [Variant] "faults" in manuscripts ka.. and ja..
2 [Variant] "from a harsh metrical foot through a succession of another meaning" in manuscript ṭa..
3 [Variant] "through a word used before" in manuscripts ja.. and ña..
[Page 233]

346.s:
abhāvepi tayorantarvyavadhānāstridhaiva sā /
antarā padavākyābhyāṃ pratibhedaṃ punardvidhā //
346.d:
अभावेपि तयोरन्तर्व्यवधानास्त्रिधैव सा /
अन्तरा पदवाक्याभ्यां प्रतिभेदं पुनर्द्विधा //
346.m: Even in the absence of both, it is threefold through intermediate separation; / between words and sentences, it is subdivided into two.

346.s:
vācyamarthārthyamānatvāttaddvidhā padavākyayoḥ /
vyutpāditapūrvavācyaṃ vyutpādyañceti bhidyate //
346.d:
वाच्यमर्थार्थ्यमानत्वात्तद्द्विधा पदवाक्ययोः /
व्युत्पादितपूर्ववाच्यं व्युत्पाद्यञ्चेति भिद्यते //
346.m: Because it is sought as the object of meaning, the signified is twofold in words and sentences; / it is divided into that which has already been derived and that which is yet to be derived.

346.s:
iṣṭavyāghātakāritvaṃ hetoḥ syādasamarthatā /
asiddhatvaṃ viruddhatvamanaikāntikatā tathā //
346.d:
इष्टव्याघातकारित्वं हेतोः स्यादसमर्थता /
असिद्धत्वं विरुद्धत्वमनैकान्तिकता तथा //
346.m: Incapacity of the logical reason is that which brings about the subversion of the thesis; / likewise, unprovenness, contrariety, and inconclusiveness,

346.s:
evaṃ satpratipakṣatvaṃ kālātītatvasaṅkaraḥ /
pakṣe sapakṣenāstitatvaṃ vipakṣe 'stitvameva tat //
346.d:
एवं सत्प्रतिपक्षत्वं कालातीतत्वसङ्करः /
पक्षे सपक्षेनास्तितत्वं विपक्षे ऽस्तित्वमेव तत् //
346.m: similarly, having an equally valid counter-thesis, being vitiated by time, and fallacious confusion; / presence in the subject and in the positive instance, and presence in the negative instance.

346.s:
kāvyeṣu pariṣadyānāṃ na bhavedapyaruntudam /
ekādaśanirarthatvaṃ(1) duṣkarādau na duṣyati //
346.d:
काव्येषु परिषद्यानां न भवेदप्यरुन्तुदम् /
एकादशनिरर्थत्वं(1) दुष्करादौ न दुष्यति //
346.m: In poetry, this may not be painful even to members of an assembly; / elevenfold meaninglessness is not a fault in difficult verses and the like.

346.s:
duḥkhīkaroti doṣajñāngūḍhārthatvaṃ na duṣkare /
na grāmyatodvegakārī prasiddher lokaśāstrayoḥ //
346.d:
दुःखीकरोति दोषज्ञान्गूढार्थत्वं न दुष्करे /
न ग्राम्यतोद्वेगकारी प्रसिद्धेर् लोकशास्त्रयोः //
346.m: Obscure meaning does not distress critics in difficult compositions; / vulgarity does not cause agitation because of its currency in worldly speech and treatises.

346.s:
kriyābhraṃśena lakṣmāsti kriyādhyāhārayogataḥ /
bhraṣṭakārakatākṣepabalādhyāhṛtakārake //
346.d:
क्रियाभ्रंशेन लक्ष्मास्ति क्रियाध्याहारयोगतः /
भ्रष्टकारकताक्षेपबलाध्याहृतकारके //
346.m: Grace exists despite the loss of a verb through the ellipsis and supply of the verb, / and despite the loss of a syntactic factor when the factor is supplied by force of implication.

346.s:
pragṛhye gṛhyate naiva kṣataṃ vigatasandhinā /
kaṣṭapāṭhādvisandhitvaṃ durvacādau na durbhagam //
346.d:
प्रगृह्ये गृह्यते नैव क्षतं विगतसन्धिना /
कष्टपाठाद्विसन्धित्वं दुर्वचादौ न दुर्भगम् //
346.m: In a non-coalescing vowel, a defect is not at all perceived through hiatus; / hiatus due to harsh reading is not unpleasing in difficult-to-pronounce passages and the like.

346.s:
anuprāse padāvṛttirvyastasambandhatā śubhā /
nārthasaṃgrahaṇe doṣo vyutkramādyair na lipyate //
346.d:
अनुप्रासे पदावृत्तिर्व्यस्तसम्बन्धता शुभा /
नार्थसंग्रहणे दोषो व्युत्क्रमाद्यैर् न लिप्यते //
346.m: In alliteration, repetition of words and broken connection are auspicious; / in conveying the meaning, a fault does not attach through inverted order and the like.

346.s:
vibhaktisaṃjñāliṅgānāṃ yatrodvego na dhīmatāṃ /
saṃkhyāyāstatra bhinnatvamupamānopameyayoḥ //
346.d:
विभक्तिसंज्ञालिङ्गानां यत्रोद्वेगो न धीमतां /
संख्यायास्तत्र भिन्नत्वमुपमानोपमेययोः //
346.m: Where there is no agitation to the wise regarding case-ending, nominal base, and gender, / there, difference in number between the standard and subject of comparison

346.s:
anekasya tathaikena bahūnāṃ bahubhiḥ śubhā /
kavīmāṃ samudācāraḥ samayo nāma gīyate //
:n
1 ekādaśanirastatvamiti ña..
:p 234
346.d:
अनेकस्य तथैकेन बहूनां बहुभिः शुभा /
कवीमां समुदाचारः समयो नाम गीयते //
:न्
1 एकादशनिरस्तत्वमिति ञ..
:प् 234
346.m:
is auspicious: of many with one, and likewise of many with many. / The traditional usage of poets is celebrated as convention.
[Footnote]
1 [Variant] "elevenfold rejection" in manuscript ña..
[Page 234]

346.s:
samānyaś ca viśiṣṭaś ca dharmavadbhavati dvidhā /
siddhasaiddhāntikānāñca kavīnāñcāvivādataḥ //
346.d:
समान्यश् च विशिष्टश् च धर्मवद्भवति द्विधा /
सिद्धसैद्धान्तिकानाञ्च कवीनाञ्चाविवादतः //
346.m: It is twofold, like properties: general and particular; / that which is established without dispute among proven theorists

346.s:
yaḥ prasidhyati sāmānya ity asau samayo mataḥ /
sarvesiddhāntikā yena sañcaranti niratyayaṃ //
346.d:
यः प्रसिध्यति सामान्य इत्य् असौ समयो मतः /
सर्वेसिद्धान्तिका येन सञ्चरन्ति निरत्ययं //
346.m: and poets is regarded as the general convention, / by which all theorists move without transgression,

346.s:
kiyanta eva vā yena sāmānyastena sadvidhā /
chedasiddhantato 'nyaḥ syāt keṣāñcidbhrāntito yathā //
346.d:
कियन्त एव वा येन सामान्यस्तेन सद्विधा /
छेदसिद्धन्ततो ऽन्यः स्यात् केषाञ्चिद्भ्रान्तितो यथा //
346.m: or by which only some move; thus it is twofold. / Another may arise from differing doctrinal tenets, or from the delusion of some, such as:

346.s:
tarkajñānaṃ muneḥ kasya kasyacit kṣaṇabhaṅgikā /
bhūtacaitanyatā kasya jñānasya suprakāśatā //
346.d:
तर्कज्ञानं मुनेः कस्य कस्यचित् क्षणभङ्गिका /
भूतचैतन्यता कस्य ज्ञानस्य सुप्रकाशता //
346.m: the logical knowledge of one sage, the momentariness of another, / the sentience of the material elements of one, the self-luminosity of knowledge,

346.s:
prajñātasthūlatāśabdānekāntatvaṃ tathārhataḥ /
śaivavaiṣṇavaśākteyasaurasiddhāntināṃ matiḥ //
346.d:
प्रज्ञातस्थूलताशब्दानेकान्तत्वं तथार्हतः /
शैववैष्णवशाक्तेयसौरसिद्धान्तिनां मतिः //
346.m: the perceived grossness [of consciousness], the manifoldness of words for the Jaina, / and the doctrine of the adherents of the Śaiva, Vaiṣṇava, Śākta, and Saura systems,

346.s:
jagataḥ kāraṇaṃ brahma sāṅkhyānāṃ sapradhānakaṃ /
asmin sarasvatīloke sañcarantaḥ parasparam //
346.d:
जगतः कारणं ब्रह्म साङ्ख्यानां सप्रधानकं /
अस्मिन् सरस्वतीलोके सञ्चरन्तः परस्परम् //
346.m: Brahman as the cause of the universe, and for the followers of Sāṅkhya together with the Pradhāna. / Moving among one another in this realm of Sarasvatī,

346.s:
badhnanti vyatipaśyanto yadviśiṣṭaiḥ sa ucyate /
parigrahādapyasatāṃ satāmevāparigrahāt //
346.d:
बध्नन्ति व्यतिपश्यन्तो यद्विशिष्टैः स उच्यते /
परिग्रहादप्यसतां सतामेवापरिग्रहात् //
346.m: what they compose discerning [it] through specific [conventions] is declared; / through the acceptance even of the unreal, and the non-acceptance of the real,

346.s:
bhidyamānasya tasyāyaṃ dvaividhyamupagīyate /
pratyakṣādipramāṇair yad bādhitaṃ tadasadviduḥ //
346.d:
भिद्यमानस्य तस्यायं द्वैविध्यमुपगीयते /
प्रत्यक्षादिप्रमाणैर् यद् बाधितं तदसद्विदुः //
346.m: its twofold nature is sung when it is differentiated. / That which is contradicted by means of valid knowledge such as perception, they know as unreal.

346.s:
kavibhistat pratigrāhyaṃ jñānasya dyotamānatā /
yadevārthakriyākāri tadeva paramārthasat //
346.d:
कविभिस्तत् प्रतिग्राह्यं ज्ञानस्य द्योतमानता /
यदेवार्थक्रियाकारि तदेव परमार्थसत् //
346.m: That is to be accepted by poets, [such as] the luminosity of knowledge; / whatever produces causal efficacy, that alone is ultimately real.

346.s:
ajñānājjñānatastvekaṃ brahmaiva paramārthasat /
viṣṇuḥ svargādihetuḥ sa śabdālaṅkārarūpavān /
aparā ca parā vidyā tāṃ jñātvā mucyate bhavāt //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe alaṅkāre kāvyadoṣaviveko nāma
ṣaṭcatvāriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:p 235
:ś atha adhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
ekākṣarābhidhānaṃ
346.d:
अज्ञानाज्ज्ञानतस्त्वेकं ब्रह्मैव परमार्थसत् /
विष्णुः स्वर्गादिहेतुः स शब्दालङ्काररूपवान् /
अपरा च परा विद्या तां ज्ञात्वा मुच्यते भवात् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे अलङ्कारे काव्यदोषविवेको नाम
षट्चत्वारिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:प् 235
:श् अथ अधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
एकाक्षराभिधानं
346.m:
From ignorance, but by knowledge, the one Brahman alone is ultimately real; / that Viṣṇu is the cause of heaven and other realms, embodied as verbal ornament; / there is the lower and the higher knowledge; knowing that, one is liberated from worldly existence.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, in the [section on] poetics, the three hundred and forty-sixth chapter, named "Examination of Poetic Faults."
[Page 235]
Now, the [three hundred and forty-seventh] chapter.
The Lexicon of Monosyllables.

347.s:
agnir uvāca
ekākṣarābhidhanañca mātṛkāntaṃ vadāmi te /
a viṣṇuḥ pratiṣedhaḥ syādā pitāmahavākyayoḥ //
347.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
एकाक्षराभिधनञ्च मातृकान्तं वदामि ते /
अ विष्णुः प्रतिषेधः स्यादा पितामहवाक्ययोः //
347.m:
Agni said:
I shall explain to you the lexicon of monosyllables up to the end of the alphabet: / 'a' is Viṣṇu, or negation; 'ā' is in the sense of Brahmā or speech,

347.s:
sīmāyāmathāvyayaṃ ā bhavetsaṃkrodhapīḍayoḥ /
iḥ kāme ratilakṣmyorī uḥ śive rakṣakādya ūḥ(1) //
347.d:
सीमायामथाव्ययं आ भवेत्संक्रोधपीडयोः /
इः कामे रतिलक्ष्म्योरी उः शिवे रक्षकाद्य ऊः(1) //
347.m: or the indeclinable 'ā' may be in the sense of a boundary, intense anger, and distress; / 'i' is Kāma; 'ī' is Rati and Lakṣmī; 'u' is Śiva; 'ū' is the foremost of protectors and the like;

347.s:
ṛ śabde cāditau ṛsyāt ḷ ḹ te vai ditau guhe /
e devī ai yoginī syādo brahmā au maheśvaraḥ //
347.d:
ऋ शब्दे चादितौ ऋस्यात् ऌ ॡ ते वै दितौ गुहे /
ए देवी ऐ योगिनी स्यादो ब्रह्मा औ महेश्वरः //
347.m: 'ṛ' is sound and Aditi; 'ṝ' is [the same]; 'ḷ' and 'ḹ' indeed denote Diti and Guha; / 'e' is Devī; 'ai' is a Yoginī; 'o' is Brahmā; 'au' is Maheśvara;

347.s:
aṅkāmaḥ aḥ praśastaḥ syāt(2) ko brahmādau ku kutsite /
khaṃ śūnyendriyaṃ khaṅgo gandharve ca vināyake //
347.d:
अङ्कामः अः प्रशस्तः स्यात्(2) को ब्रह्मादौ कु कुत्सिते /
खं शून्येन्द्रियं खङ्गो गन्धर्वे च विनायके //
347.m: 'aṃ' is Kāma; 'aḥ' is auspicious; 'ka' denotes Brahmā and others; 'ku' is in the sense of vile; / 'kha' is empty space, an organ of sense; 'khaṅga' denotes a Gandharva and Vināyaka.

347.s:
gaṅgīte go gāyane syad gho ghaṇṭā kiṅkiṇīmukhe /
tāḍane ṅaś ca viṣaye spṛhāyāñcaiva bhairave //
347.d:
गङ्गीते गो गायने स्यद् घो घण्टा किङ्किणीमुखे /
ताडने ङश् च विषये स्पृहायाञ्चैव भैरवे //
347.m: Ga [signifies] song; go is in the sense of a singer; gha is a bell, [and] on the face of a small bell; / and ṅa is in beating, sense-object, longing, and Bhairava.

347.s:
co durjane nirmale chaśchede jirjayane tathā /
jaṃ gīte jhaḥ praśaste syādbale(3) ño gāyane ca ṭaḥ //
347.d:
चो दुर्जने निर्मले छश्छेदे जिर्जयने तथा /
जं गीते झः प्रशस्ते स्याद्बले(3) ञो गायने च टः //
347.m: Ca is in a wicked person, [and] in pure; cha is in cutting; ji likewise in victory; / ja is in song; jha is in praiseworthy; ña is in strength and in a singer; and ṭa—

347.s:
ṭhaś candramaṇḍale śūnye śive codbandhane mataḥ /
ḍaś ca rudre dhvanau trāse ḍhakvāyāṃ ḍho dhvanau mataḥ //
347.d:
ठश् चन्द्रमण्डले शून्ये शिवे चोद्बन्धने मतः /
डश् च रुद्रे ध्वनौ त्रासे ढक्वायां ढो ध्वनौ मतः //
347.m: ṭha is considered [to mean] lunar orb, void, Śiva, and hanging; / ḍa is in Rudra, sound, [and] terror; ḍha is considered in a drum [and] in sound.

347.s:
ṇo niṣkarṣe niś caye ca taś caure kroḍapucchake /
bhakṣaṇe thaśchedane do dhāraṇe śobhane mataḥ //
:n
1 brahmakādya ūriti kha..
2 praśāntaḥsyāditi kha..
3 dhane iti ña..
:p 236
347.d:
णो निष्कर्षे निश् चये च तश् चौरे क्रोडपुच्छके /
भक्षणे थश्छेदने दो धारणे शोभने मतः //
:न्
1 ब्रह्मकाद्य ऊरिति ख..
2 प्रशान्तःस्यादिति ख..
3 धने इति ञ..
:प् 236
347.m:
ṇa is in determination and certainty; ta in a thief [and] the tail of a boar; / tha in eating [and] cutting; da is considered in bearing [and] handsome.
[Footnote mark]
[Footnote:] 1. “brahmakādya ūḥ” according to manuscript kha.
[Footnote:] 2. “praśāntaḥ syāt” according to manuscript kha.
[Footnote:] 3. “dhane” according to manuscript ña.
[Page 236]

347.s:
dho dhātari cadhūstūre no vṛnde sugate tathā /
pa upavane vikhyātaḥ phaś ca jhañjhānile mataḥ //
347.d:
धो धातरि चधूस्तूरे नो वृन्दे सुगते तथा /
प उपवने विख्यातः फश् च झञ्झानिले मतः //
347.m: dha is in the Creator and the thorn-apple; na is in a multitude and likewise in Sugata [the Buddha]; / pa is celebrated in a pleasure-grove; and pha is considered in a stormy gale.

347.s:
phuḥ phutkāre niṣphale ca viḥ pakṣī bhañca tārake /
mā śrīrmānañca mātā syādyāga yo yātṛvīraṇe //
347.d:
फुः फुत्कारे निष्फले च विः पक्षी भञ्च तारके /
मा श्रीर्मानञ्च माता स्याद्याग यो यातृवीरणे //
347.m: phuḥ is in puffing and fruitless; viḥ is a bird; bha is in a star; / mā is Śrī, measure, and mother; yāga [is designated by] ya; ya is also in a traveller and fragrant grass.

347.s:
ro bahnau ca laḥ śakre ca lo vidhātari īritaḥ /
viśleṣaṇe vo varuṇe śayane śaś ca śaṃ sukhe //
347.d:
रो बह्नौ च लः शक्रे च लो विधातरि ईरितः /
विश्लेषणे वो वरुणे शयने शश् च शं सुखे //
347.m: ra is declared in fire; la in Śakra [Indra]; and la in the Ordainer; / va in separation [and] Varuṇa; śa in reclining; and śaṃ in happiness.

347.s:
ṣaḥ śreṣṭhe saḥ parokṣe ca sālakṣmīḥ saṃ kacemataḥ /
dhāraṇe has tathā rudre kṣaḥ kṣattre cākṣare mataḥ //
347.d:
षः श्रेष्ठे सः परोक्षे च सालक्ष्मीः सं कचेमतः /
धारणे हस् तथा रुद्रे क्षः क्षत्त्रे चाक्षरे मतः //
347.m: ṣa is considered in excellent; sa in absent [and] that Lakṣmī; saṃ in hair; / ha in bearing and likewise in Rudra; kṣa in the warrior [caste] and in the imperishable.

347.s:
kṣo nṛsiṃhe harau tadvat kṣetrapālakayorapi /
mantra ekākṣaro devo bhuktimuktipradāyakaḥ //
347.d:
क्षो नृसिंहे हरौ तद्वत् क्षेत्रपालकयोरपि /
मन्त्र एकाक्षरो देवो भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदायकः //
347.m: kṣa is likewise [considered] in Nṛsiṃha, Hari [Viṣṇu], and the two guardians of the field; / the deity of the single-syllable mantra is the bestower of worldly enjoyment and liberation.

347.s:
haihayaśirase namaḥ sarvavidyāprado manuḥ /
akārādyās tathā mantrā mātṛkāmantra uttamaḥ //
347.d:
हैहयशिरसे नमः सर्वविद्याप्रदो मनुः /
अकाराद्यास् तथा मन्त्रा मातृकामन्त्र उत्तमः //
347.m: “Obeisance to Haihayaśiras” is the mantra that bestows all knowledge. / Likewise are the mantras beginning with the letter a; the Mātṛkā mantra is supreme.

347.s:
ekapadme 'rcayedetānnava durgāś ca pūjayet /
bhagavatī kātyāyanī kauśikī cātha caṇḍikā //
347.d:
एकपद्मे ऽर्चयेदेतान्नव दुर्गाश् च पूजयेत् /
भगवती कात्यायनी कौशिकी चाथ चण्डिका //
347.m: One should worship these on a single lotus, and one should worship the nine Durgās: / Bhagavatī, Kātyāyanī, Kauśikī, and Caṇḍikā,

347.s:
pracaṇḍā suranāyikā ugrā pārvatī durgayā /
oṃ caṇḍikāyai vidmahe bhagavatyai dhīmahi tanno durgā
pracodayāt
kramādi tu ṣaḍaṅgaṃ syādgaṇo gururguruḥ kramāt //
347.d:
प्रचण्डा सुरनायिका उग्रा पार्वती दुर्गया /
ओं चण्डिकायै विद्महे भगवत्यै धीमहि तन्नो दुर्गा
प्रचोदयात्
क्रमादि तु षडङ्गं स्याद्गणो गुरुर्गुरुः क्रमात् //
347.m:
Pracaṇḍā, Suranāyikā, Ugrā, Pārvatī, with Durgā.
“Oṃ, we know Caṇḍikā; we meditate upon Bhagavatī; may that Durgā inspire us.”
In order are the six limbs; the group [of letters] is the guru, guru in succession.

347.s:
ajitāparājitā cātha jayā ca vijayā tataḥ /
kātyāyanī bhadrakālī maṅgalā siddhirevatī //
347.d:
अजितापराजिता चाथ जया च विजया ततः /
कात्यायनी भद्रकाली मङ्गला सिद्धिरेवती //
347.m: Ajitā, Aparājitā, and Jayā, then Vijayā, / Kātyāyanī, Bhadrakālī, Maṅgalā, Siddhi, Revatī;

347.s:
siddhādivaṭukāḥ pūjyā hetukaś ca kapālikaḥ /
ekapādo bhīmarūpo dikpālānmadhyato nava //
347.d:
सिद्धादिवटुकाः पूज्या हेतुकश् च कपालिकः /
एकपादो भीमरूपो दिक्पालान्मध्यतो नव //
347.m: the Vaṭukas beginning with Siddha are to be worshipped, and Hetuka, Kapālika, / Ekapāda, Bhīmarūpa, [and] the nine guardians of the directions from the centre.

347.s:
hrīṃ durge durge rakṣaṇi svāhāmantrārthasiddhaye /
gaurī pūjyā ca dharmādyāḥ skandādyāḥ śaktayo yajet //
:p 237
347.d:
ह्रीं दुर्गे दुर्गे रक्षणि स्वाहामन्त्रार्थसिद्धये /
गौरी पूज्या च धर्माद्याः स्कन्दाद्याः शक्तयो यजेत् //
:प् 237
347.m:
“Hrīṃ, O Durgā, O Durgā, O protectress, svāhā,” for the attainment of the purpose of the mantra. / Gaurī is to be worshipped, and the virtues beginning with dharma, and one should worship the powers beginning with Skanda.
[Page 237]

347.s:
prajñā jñānā kriyā vācā vāgīśī jvālinī tathā /
kāminī kāmamālā ca indrādyāḥ śaktipūjanaṃ //
347.d:
प्रज्ञा ज्ञाना क्रिया वाचा वागीशी ज्वालिनी तथा /
कामिनी काममाला च इन्द्राद्याः शक्तिपूजनं //
347.m: Prajñā, Jñānā, Kriyā, Vāc, Vāgīśī, and Jvālinī, / Kāminī, and Kāmamālā, and those beginning with Indra—worship of the Śaktis.

347.s:
oṃgaṃ svāhā mūlamantro 'yaṃ gaṃ vā gaṇapataye namaḥ /
ṣaḍaṅgo raktaśuklaś ca dantākṣaparaśūtakaṭaḥ //
347.d:
ओंगं स्वाहा मूलमन्त्रो ऽयं गं वा गणपतये नमः /
षडङ्गो रक्तशुक्लश् च दन्ताक्षपरशूतकटः //
347.m: “Oṃ gaṃ svāhā” is this root mantra, or “Gaṃ, obeisance to Gaṇapati.” / Having six limbs, red and white, having a tusk, rosary, and axe, exalted,

347.s:
samodako 'tha(1) gandhādigandholkāyeti ca kramāt /
gajo mahāgaṇapatirmaholkaḥ pūjya eva ca //
kuṣmāṇḍāya ekadantatripurāntakāya
śyāmadantavikaṭaharahāsāya
lambanāśānanāya padmadaṃṣṭrāya megholkāya dhūmolkāya
vakratuṇdāya vighneśvarāya vikaṭotkaṭāya gajendragamanāya
bhujagendrahārāya śaśāṅkadharāya gaṇādhipataye svāhā
347.d:
समोदको ऽथ(1) गन्धादिगन्धोल्कायेति च क्रमात् /
गजो महागणपतिर्महोल्कः पूज्य एव च //
कुष्माण्डाय एकदन्तत्रिपुरान्तकाय
श्यामदन्तविकटहरहासाय
लम्बनाशाननाय पद्मदंष्ट्राय मेघोल्काय धूमोल्काय
वक्रतुण्दाय विघ्नेश्वराय विकटोत्कटाय गजेन्द्रगमनाय
भुजगेन्द्रहाराय शशाङ्कधराय गणाधिपतये स्वाहा
347.m:
with a sweetmeat, and with incense and so forth, in order with “to Gandholkā.” / Gaja, Mahāgaṇapati, and Maholka are surely to be worshipped:
“To Kuṣmāṇḍa, to the single-tusked destroyer of Tripura, / to the one whose teeth are dark and laughter fearful like Hara’s,
to the long-nosed-faced one, to the lotus-tusked, to Megholka, to Dhūmolka,
to the curved-trunked one, to the Lord of Obstacles, to the terrible and fierce one, to the one who moves like an elephant king,
to the one wearing the serpent king as a garland, to the bearer of the crescent moon, to the lord of the Gaṇas, svāhā.”

347.s:
etair manubhiḥ svāhāntaiḥ pūjya tilahomādinārthabhāk /
kādyair vā vījasaṃyuktaistair ādyaiś ca namo 'ntakaiḥ //
347.d:
एतैर् मनुभिः स्वाहान्तैः पूज्य तिलहोमादिनार्थभाक् /
काद्यैर् वा वीजसंयुक्तैस्तैर् आद्यैश् च नमो ऽन्तकैः //
347.m: Worshipping with these mantras ending in svāhā by means of fire oblations of sesame and the like, one obtains one’s object; / or with those beginning with ka combined with the seed-syllables, and with those beginning [formulas] ending in namas.

347.s:
mantrāḥ pṛthak pṛthagvā syurdvirephadvirmukhākṣiṇaḥ(2)* /
kātyāyanaṃ akanda āha yattadvyākaraṇaṃ vade //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe ekākṣarābhidhānaṃ nāma
saptacatvāriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:n
same deśe 'theti ja..
2 dve dve rekhātha dakṣiṇā iti ja..
dvirephadvirmūkhākṣiṇa ity ayaṃ pātha ādarśadoṣeṇa
samīcīno bhavituṃ nārhati
:p 238
:ś athāṣṭacatvāriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
vyākaraṇaṃ
347.d:
मन्त्राः पृथक् पृथग्वा स्युर्द्विरेफद्विर्मुखाक्षिणः(2)* /
कात्यायनं अकन्द आह यत्तद्व्याकरणं वदे //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे एकाक्षराभिधानं नाम
सप्तचत्वारिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:न्
समे देशे ऽथेति ज..
2 द्वे द्वे रेखाथ दक्षिणा इति ज..
द्विरेफद्विर्मूखाक्षिण इत्य् अयं पाथ आदर्शदोषेण
समीचीनो भवितुं नार्हति
:प् 238
:श् अथाष्टचत्वारिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
व्याकरणं
347.m:
Or the mantras may be distinct, having two ra-sounds, two faces, and eyes. / What Skanda told to Kātyāyana—that grammar I shall declare.
Thus in the glorious Agni Purāṇa, the three hundred and forty-seventh chapter, entitled “The Explanation of Single Syllables”.
[Footnote mark]
[Footnote:] 1. “same deśe 'tha” according to manuscript ja.
[Footnote:] 2. “dve dve rekhātha dakṣiṇā” according to manuscript ja.
[Footnote:] The reading “dvirephadvirmūkhākṣiṇaḥ” cannot be correct due to an error in the exemplar.
[Page 238]
Now the three hundred and forty-eighth chapter.
Grammar

348.s:
skanda+uvāca
vakṣye vyākaraṇaṃ sāraṃ siddhaśabdasvarūpakam /
kātyāyanavibodhāya bālānāṃ bodhanāya ca //
348.d:
स्कन्द+उवाच
वक्ष्ये व्याकरणं सारं सिद्धशब्दस्वरूपकम् /
कात्यायनविबोधाय बालानां बोधनाय च //
348.m: Skanda said: / I shall declare the essence of grammar, the nature of perfected words, / for the understanding of Kātyāyana and for the instruction of children.

348.s:
pratyāhārādikāḥ saṃjñāḥ śāstrasaṃvyavahāragāḥ /
a i u ṇa ṛ ḷ ka e ṅa ai au ca ha ya va ra ṭa ṇa na ña ma ṅa ṇa
nama jha bha ña gha dha ṣa ja va ga ḍa da śa kha pha cha ṭha tha ca ṭa ta
ka pa ya śa ṣa sa ra ha la iti pratyāhāraḥ
upadeśa iddhalantaṃ bhavedajanunāsikaḥ //
348.d:
प्रत्याहारादिकाः संज्ञाः शास्त्रसंव्यवहारगाः /
अ इ उ ण ऋ ऌ क ए ङ ऐ औ च ह य व र ट ण न ञ म ङ ण
नम झ भ ञ घ ध ष ज व ग ड द श ख फ छ ठ थ च ट त
क प य श ष स र ह ल इति प्रत्याहारः
उपदेश इद्धलन्तं भवेदजनुनासिकः //
348.m:
The technical designations such as the abbreviations (pratyāhāra) employed in the usage of the treatise [are]:
a-i-u-ṇ, ṛ-ḷ-k, e-ṅ, ai-au-c, ha-ya-va-ra-ṭ, la-ṇ, ña-ma-ṅa-ṇa-na-m, jha-bha-ñ, gha-ḍha-dha-ṣ, ja-ba-ga-ḍa-da-ś, kha-pha-cha-ṭha-tha-ca-ṭa-ta-v, ka-pa-y, śa-ṣa-sa-r, ha-l. Such is the abbreviation.
In grammatical instruction, a final consonant is an it, [and so] is a nasalised vowel.

348.s:
ādivarṇo gṛhyamāṇo 'pyantyenetā sahaiva tu /
tayormadhyagatānāṃ syādgrāhakaḥ svasya tadyathā //
aṇ eṅ aṭ yaṅ chav jham bhaṣ ak ik aṇ iṇ yaṇ pareṇa
ṇakāreṇa / am yam ṅam ac ic aic ay may jhay khay jav jhav khav cav śav as
has vas bhas al hal bal ral jhal sal iti pratyāhāraḥ
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe vyākaraṇe pratyāhāro
nāmāṣṭacatvāriṃśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:p 239
:ś athonapañcāśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
sandhisiddharūpaṃ
348.d:
आदिवर्णो गृह्यमाणो ऽप्यन्त्येनेता सहैव तु /
तयोर्मध्यगतानां स्याद्ग्राहकः स्वस्य तद्यथा //
अण् एङ् अट् यङ् छव् झम् भष् अक् इक् अण् इण् यण् परेण
णकारेण / अम् यम् ङम् अच् इच् ऐच् अय् मय् झय् खय् जव् झव् खव् चव् शव् अस्
हस् वस् भस् अल् हल् बल् रल् झल् सल् इति प्रत्याहारः
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे व्याकरणे प्रत्याहारो
नामाष्टचत्वारिंशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:प् 239
:श् अथोनपञ्चाशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
सन्धिसिद्धरूपं
348.m:
An initial phoneme, when apprehended together with the final it, / denotes those situated between them and itself. For example:
aṇ, eṅ, aṭ, yaṅ, chav, jham, bhaṣ, ak, ik, aṇ, iṇ, yaṇ with the second ṇa; / am, yam, ṅam, ac, ic, aic, ay, may, jhay, khay, jav, jhav, khav, cav, śav, as, has, vas, bhas, al, hal, bal, ral, jhal, śal. Such is the abbreviation.
Thus in the glorious Agni Purāṇa, in the section on grammar, the three hundred and forty-eighth chapter, entitled “The Pratyāhāras”.
[Page 239]
Now the three hundred and forty-ninth chapter.
The perfected forms of euphonic combination (sandhi)

349.s:
skanda+uvāca
vakṣye sandhisiddharūpaṃ svarasandhimathāditaḥ /
daṇḍāgramaṃ sāgatā dadhīdaṃ nadīhate madhūdakaṃ //
349.d:
स्कन्द+उवाच
वक्ष्ये सन्धिसिद्धरूपं स्वरसन्धिमथादितः /
दण्डाग्रमं सागता दधीदं नदीहते मधूदकं //
349.m: Skanda said: / I shall declare the perfected forms of sandhi, first vowel sandhi: / daṇḍāgram, aṃsāgatā, dadhīdam, nadīhate, madhūdakam,

349.s:
pitṛṣabhaḥ ḹkāraś ca tavedaṃ sakalodakaṃ /
ardharco 'yaṃ tavalkāraḥ saiṣā saindrī tavaudanam //
349.d:
पितृषभः ॡकारश् च तवेदं सकलोदकं /
अर्धर्चो ऽयं तवल्कारः सैषा सैन्द्री तवौदनम् //
349.m: pitṛṣabhaḥ, and the sound ḹ; tavedam, sakalodakam, / ardharco 'yam, tavalkāraḥ, saiṣā, saindrī, tavaudanam,

349.s:
khaṭṭaugho 'bhavadityevaṃ vyasudhīrvasvalaṅkṛtaṃ /
pitrarthopavanaṃ dātrī nāyako lāvako nayaḥ //
349.d:
खट्टौघो ऽभवदित्येवं व्यसुधीर्वस्वलङ्कृतं /
पित्रर्थोपवनं दात्री नायको लावको नयः //
349.m: khaṭṭaughaḥ, abhavat, just so vyasudhīḥ, vasvalaṅkṛtam, / pitrartham, upavanam, dātrī, nāyakaḥ, lāvakaḥ, nayaḥ,

349.s:
ta+iha tayihetyādi te 'tra yo 'tra jale 'kajaṃ /
prakṛtirno aho ehi a avehi i indrakaṃ //
349.d:
त+इह तयिहेत्यादि ते ऽत्र यो ऽत्र जले ऽकजं /
प्रकृतिर्नो अहो एहि अ अवेहि इ इन्द्रकं //
349.m: ta iha, tayiha, and so on; te 'tra, yo 'tra, jale 'kajam; / the uncombined form: no aho, ehi, a avehi, i indrakam,

349.s:
u uttiṣṭha kavī etau vāyu etau vane ime /
amī ete yajñabhūte ehi deva imannaya //
349.d:
उ उत्तिष्ठ कवी एतौ वायु एतौ वने इमे /
अमी एते यज्ञभूते एहि देव इमन्नय //
349.m: u uttiṣṭha, kavī etau, vāyū etau, vane ime, / amī ete, yajñabhūte, ehi deva imam naya.

349.s:
vakṣye sandhiṃ vyañjanāṇāṃ vāgyato 'jekamātṛkaḥ /
ṣaḍete tadime vādivāṅnītiḥ ṣaṇmukhādikam //
349.d:
वक्ष्ये सन्धिं व्यञ्जनाणां वाग्यतो ऽजेकमातृकः /
षडेते तदिमे वादिवाङ्नीतिः षण्मुखादिकम् //
349.m: I shall declare the sandhi of consonants: vāgyataḥ, ajekamātṛkaḥ, / ṣaḍete, tadime, vādin, vāṅnītiḥ, ṣaṇmukhādikam,

349.s:
vāṅmanasaṃ vagbhāvādirvāk ślakṣṇaṃ taccharīrakaṃ /
tallu nāti taccarecca kruṅṅāste ca sugaṇiha //
349.d:
वाङ्मनसं वग्भावादिर्वाक् श्लक्ष्णं तच्छरीरकं /
तल्लु नाति तच्चरेच्च क्रुङ्ङास्ते च सुगणिह //
349.m: vāṅmanasam, vagbhāva and so on, vāk ślakṣṇam, taccharīrakam, / tallunāti, taccaret and kruṅṅāste, and sugaṇṇiha,

349.s:
bhavāṃś caran bhavāṃśchātro bhavāṃṣṭīkābhavāṃṣṭhakaḥ /
bhavāṃstīrthaṃ bhavāṃstheyāt bhavāṃllekhā bhavāñjayaḥ //
349.d:
भवांश् चरन् भवांश्छात्रो भवांष्टीकाभवांष्ठकः /
भवांस्तीर्थं भवांस्थेयात् भवांल्लेखा भवाञ्जयः //
349.m: bhavāṃś caran, bhavāṃś chātraḥ, bhavāṃṣ ṭīkā, bhavāṃṣ ṭhakaḥ, / bhavāṃs tīrtham, bhavāṃs theyāt, bhavāṃllekhā, bhavāñjayaḥ,

349.s:
bhavāñchete bhavāñcaśete bhavāñśete bhavāṇḍīnaḥ /
svambhartā tvaṅkaroṣyādiḥ sandhirjñeyo visargajaḥ //
:p 240
349.d:
भवाञ्छेते भवाञ्चशेते भवाञ्शेते भवाण्डीनः /
स्वम्भर्ता त्वङ्करोष्यादिः सन्धिर्ज्ञेयो विसर्गजः //
:प् 240
349.m:
bhavāñ śete, bhavāñca śete, bhavāñśete, bhavāṇḍīnaḥ, / svambhartā, tvaṅkaroṣi and so on. The sandhi arising from visarga should be understood:
[Page 240]

349.s:
kaśchindyāt kaś caret kaṣṭaḥ kaṣṭhaḥ kasthaś ca kaś calet /
ka .. khanet ka .. karoti sma ka ,, paṭhet ka ,, vā //
349.d:
कश्छिन्द्यात् कश् चरेत् कष्टः कष्ठः कस्थश् च कश् चलेत् /
क .. खनेत् क .. करोति स्म क ,, पठेत् क ,, वा //
349.m: kaśchindyāt, kaś caret, kaṣṭaḥ, kaṣṭhaḥ, kasthaḥ, and kaś calet; / ka [jihvāmūlīya] khanet, ka [jihvāmūlīya] karoti sma, ka [upadhmanīya] paṭhet, or ka […]

349.s:
kaśśvaśuraḥ kaḥśvaśuraḥ kassāvaraḥ kaḥsāvaraḥ /
kaḥ phaleta kaḥ śayitā ko 'tra yodhaḥ ka uttamaḥ //
349.d:
कश्श्वशुरः कःश्वशुरः कस्सावरः कःसावरः /
कः फलेत कः शयिता को ऽत्र योधः क उत्तमः //
349.m: Who is the father-in-law? Who is the father-in-law? Who is inferior? Who is inferior? / Who would bear fruit? Who will lie down? Who is the warrior here? Who is supreme?

349.s:
devā ete bho iha sodarā yānti bhago vraja /
supūḥ sudūrātriratra vāyuryāti punarna hi //
349.d:
देवा एते भो इह सोदरा यान्ति भगो व्रज /
सुपूः सुदूरात्रिरत्र वायुर्याति पुनर्न हि //
349.m: These gods, O friend, brothers here, they depart; Bhaga, go! / Beautiful city, very distant night; the wind blows here, yet it does not again.

349.s:
punareti sa yātīha eṣa yāti ka īśvaraḥ /
jyotīrūpaṃ tavacchatraṃ mlecchadhīśchidramacchidat //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe vyākaraṇe sandhisiddharūpaṃ
nāmonapañcāśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha pañcāśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
subvibhaktasiddharūpaṃ
349.d:
पुनरेति स यातीह एष याति क ईश्वरः /
ज्योतीरूपं तवच्छत्रं म्लेच्छधीश्छिद्रमच्छिदत् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे व्याकरणे सन्धिसिद्धरूपं
नामोनपञ्चाशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ पञ्चाशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
सुब्विभक्तसिद्धरूपं
349.m:
He comes again; he goes here; this one goes; who is the lord? / Form of light, your umbrella; the barbarous intellect has pierced the flaw.
Thus ends the three hundred and forty-ninth chapter in the Mahāpurāṇa of Agni, in grammar, named 'Accomplished Forms of Sandhi'.
Now begins the three hundred and fiftieth chapter:
Accomplished Forms of Nominal Case Endings.

350.s:
skanda+uvāca
vibhaktisiddharūpañca kātyāyana vadāmi te /
dve vibhaktī suptiṅaś caya supaḥ sapta vibhaktayaḥ //
350.d:
स्कन्द+उवाच
विभक्तिसिद्धरूपञ्च कात्यायन वदामि ते /
द्वे विभक्ती सुप्तिङश् चय सुपः सप्त विभक्तयः //
350.m: Skanda said: / I shall declare to you, O Kātyāyana, the accomplished forms of case endings. / There are two [classes of] endings: SUP and TIṄ; and the SUP endings consist of seven cases.

350.s:
su+aujasiti prathamā amauṭśaso dvitīyā /
ṭābhyāṃ bhisiti tṛtīyā ṅebhyāṃbhyasaś caturthyapi //
350.d:
सु+औजसिति प्रथमा अमौट्शसो द्वितीया /
टाभ्यां भिसिति तृतीया ङेभ्यांभ्यसश् चतुर्थ्यपि //
350.m: sU, au, Jas is the first case; am, auṬ, Śas is the second; / Ṭā, bhyām, bhis is the third; and Ṅe, bhyām, bhyas is the fourth;

350.s:
ṅasibhyāṃbhyasaḥ pañcamī syātṅasomiti ṣaṣṭhyapi /
ṅi+ossuviti saptamī syāt syuḥ prātipadikātparāḥ //
350.d:
ङसिभ्यांभ्यसः पञ्चमी स्यात्ङसोमिति षष्ठ्यपि /
ङि+ओस्सुविति सप्तमी स्यात् स्युः प्रातिपदिकात्पराः //
350.m: Ṅasi, bhyām, bhyas is the fifth; Ṅas, os, ām is the sixth; / Ṅi, os, suP is the seventh; they occur after a nominal stem.

350.s:
dvividhaṃ prātipadikaṃ hy ajantañca halantakaṃ /
:p 241
pratyekaṃ trividhaṃ tat syāt pumāṃstrī ca napuṃsakaṃ //
350.d:
द्विविधं प्रातिपदिकं ह्य् अजन्तञ्च हलन्तकं /
:प् 241
प्रत्येकं त्रिविधं तत् स्यात् पुमांस्त्री च नपुंसकं //
350.m:
A nominal stem is twofold: ending in a vowel and ending in a consonant.
:p 241
Each of these is threefold: masculine, feminine, and neuter.

350.s:
darśyante nāyakāsteṣāmanuktānāñca vīryataḥ /
vṛkṣaḥ sarvo 'tha pūrvaś ca prathamaś ca dvitīyakaḥ //
350.d:
दर्श्यन्ते नायकास्तेषामनुक्तानाञ्च वीर्यतः /
वृक्षः सर्वो ऽथ पूर्वश् च प्रथमश् च द्वितीयकः //
350.m: Their representative models, and by virtue of those not mentioned, are shown: / vṛkṣaḥ, sarvaḥ, then pūrvaḥ, and prathamaḥ, and dvitīyakaḥ,

350.s:
tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍapā vahniḥ sakhāpatiraharpatiḥ /
paṭurnīrgrāmanīndraś ca khalapūrmitrabhūḥ svabhūḥ //
350.d:
तृतीयः खण्डपा वह्निः सखापतिरहर्पतिः /
पटुर्नीर्ग्रामनीन्द्रश् च खलपूर्मित्रभूः स्वभूः //
350.m: tṛtīyaḥ, khaṇḍapāḥ, vahniḥ, sakhā, patiḥ, aharpatiḥ, / paṭuḥ, nīḥ, grāmaṇīḥ, indraḥ, khalapūḥ, mitrabhūḥ, svabhūḥ,

350.s:
auśrīḥ sudhīḥ pitā bhrātā nā karta kroṣṭunaptṛnaptṛkau /
surā rā gaus tathā dyaurglauḥ svarāntāḥ puṃsi nāyakāḥ //
350.d:
औश्रीः सुधीः पिता भ्राता ना कर्त क्रोष्टुनप्तृनप्तृकौ /
सुरा रा गौस् तथा द्यौर्ग्लौः स्वरान्ताः पुंसि नायकाः //
350.m: auśrīḥ, sudhīḥ, pitā, bhrātā, nā, kartā, kroṣṭuḥ, naptā, and naptṛkaḥ, / surāḥ, rāḥ, gauḥ, likewise dyauḥ, glauḥ—[these are] the masculine models ending in vowels.

350.s:
suvāk tvak pṛṣat samrāṭ janmabhāk ca aveḍapi /
āpo marudbhavan dīvyan bhavāṃś ca maghavān pivan //
350.d:
सुवाक् त्वक् पृषत् सम्राट् जन्मभाक् च अवेडपि /
आपो मरुद्भवन् दीव्यन् भवांश् च मघवान् पिवन् //
350.m: suvāk, tvak, pṛṣat, samrāṭ, janmabhāk, and aveṭ as well, / āpaḥ, marut, bhavan, dīvyan, bhavān, maghavān, piban,

350.s:
bhagavānadhavānarvānvahnimat sarvitsupṛt /
susīmā kuṇḍī rājā ca śvā yuvā maghavā tathā //
350.d:
भगवानधवानर्वान्वह्निमत् सर्वित्सुपृत् /
सुसीमा कुण्डी राजा च श्वा युवा मघवा तथा //
350.m: bhagavān, adhavān, arvān, vahnimat, sarvit, supṛt, / susīmā, kuṇḍī, rājā, śvā, yuvā, likewise maghavā,

350.s:
pūṣā sukarmā yajvā ca suvarmā ca sudharmaṇā /
aryamā vṛtrahā panthāḥ sukakudādipañca ca //
350.d:
पूषा सुकर्मा यज्वा च सुवर्मा च सुधर्मणा /
अर्यमा वृत्रहा पन्थाः सुककुदादिपञ्च च //
350.m: pūṣā, sukarmā, yajvā, suvarma, sudharmaṇā, / aryamā, vṛtrahā, panthāḥ, and the five beginning with sukakud,

350.s:
praśān sutāṃś ca pañcādyāḥ sugīḥ surāḥ supūrapi /
candramāḥ suvacāḥ śreyān vidvāṃśceśanasā saha //
350.d:
प्रशान् सुतांश् च पञ्चाद्याः सुगीः सुराः सुपूरपि /
चन्द्रमाः सुवचाः श्रेयान् विद्वांश्चेशनसा सह //
350.m: praśān, sutān, pañcan and the rest, sugīḥ, surāḥ, and supūḥ, / candramāḥ, suvacāḥ, śreyān, vidvān, together with uśanas,

350.s:
pecivān gauravānaḍvān godhūṅmitradruhau śvaliṭ /
striyāṃ jāyā jarā bālā eḍkā saha vṛddhayā //
350.d:
पेचिवान् गौरवानड्वान् गोधूङ्मित्रद्रुहौ श्वलिट् /
स्त्रियां जाया जरा बाला एड्का सह वृद्धया //
350.m: pecivān, gauravān, aḍvān, godhuk, mitradruk, śvaliṭ; / in the feminine: jāyā, jarā, bālā, eḍakā along with vṛddhā,

350.s:
kṣatriyā bahurājā ca bahudā mātha bālikā /
māyā kaumudagandhā ca sarvā pūrvā sahānyayā //
350.d:
क्षत्रिया बहुराजा च बहुदा माथ बालिका /
माया कौमुदगन्धा च सर्वा पूर्वा सहान्यया //
350.m: kṣatriyā, bahurājā, bahudā, mā, then bālikā, / māyā, kaumudagandhā, and sarvā, pūrvā along with anyā,

350.s:
dvitīyā ca tṛtīyā ca buddhiḥ strī śrīr nadī sudhaiḥ /
bhavantī caiva dīvyantī bhātī bhāntī ca yānyapi //
350.d:
द्वितीया च तृतीया च बुद्धिः स्त्री श्रीर् नदी सुधैः /
भवन्ती चैव दीव्यन्ती भाती भान्ती च यान्यपि //
350.m: dvitīyā and tṛtīyā, buddhiḥ, strī, śrīḥ, nadī, sudhā, / bhavantī and dīvyantī, bhātī, bhāntī, and whatever [others],

350.s:
śṛṇvatau tudatī kartrī tudantī kurvatī mahī /
rundhatī krīḍtī dantī pālayantī surāṇyapi //
:p 242
350.d:
शृण्वतौ तुदती कर्त्री तुदन्ती कुर्वती मही /
रुन्धती क्रीड्ती दन्ती पालयन्ती सुराण्यपि //
:प् 242
350.m:
śṛṇvatī, tudatī, kartrī, tudantī, kurvatī, mahī, / rundhatī, krīḍatī, dantī, pālayantī, and surāḥ,
:p 242

350.s:
garurī putravatī nīś ca vadhūrdevatayā bhuvā /
tisro dve kati varṣābhūḥ svasā mātā varā gauḥ //
350.d:
गरुरी पुत्रवती नीश् च वधूर्देवतया भुवा /
तिस्रो द्वे कति वर्षाभूः स्वसा माता वरा गौः //
350.m: gaurī, putravatī, nīḥ, vadhūḥ, devatā, bhūḥ, / tisraḥ, dve, kati, varṣābhūḥ, svasā, mātā, varā, gauḥ,

350.s:
naurvāktvakprācyavākṣīti tiraścī samudīcyapi /
śaradvidyut saridyoṣit agnivit saspadā dṛśat //
350.d:
नौर्वाक्त्वक्प्राच्यवाक्षीति तिरश्ची समुदीच्यपि /
शरद्विद्युत् सरिद्योषित् अग्निवित् सस्पदा दृशत् //
350.m: nauḥ, vāk, tvak, prācī, avācī, tiraścī, and udīcī, / śarat, vidyut, sarit, yoṣit, agnivit, saspad, dṛṣat,

350.s:
yaiṣā sā vedavitsaṃvit bahvī rājñī tvayā mayā /
somā pañcādayo rājī dhūḥ pūś caiva diśā(1) girā //
350.d:
यैषा सा वेदवित्संवित् बह्वी राज्ञी त्वया मया /
सोमा पञ्चादयो राजी धूः पूश् चैव दिशा(1) गिरा //
350.m: yā, eṣā, sā, vedavit, saṃvit, bahvī, rājñī, tvayā, mayā, / somā, pañcan and the rest, rājī, dhūḥ, pūḥ, diś, gir,

350.s:
catasro viduṣī caiva keyaṃ dik dṛkca tādṛśī /
asau striyāṃ nāyakāś ca nāyakāś ca napuṃsake //
350.d:
चतस्रो विदुषी चैव केयं दिक् दृक्च तादृशी /
असौ स्त्रियां नायकाश् च नायकाश् च नपुंसके //
350.m: catasraḥ, viduṣī, kā, iyam, dik, dṛk, and tādṛśī, / asau—[these are] the models in feminine. And the models in neuter [are]:

350.s:
kuṇḍaṃ sarvaṃ somapañca dadhi vāri khalapvatha /
madhu trapu kartṛ bhaktṛ ativaktṛ payaḥ puraḥ //
350.d:
कुण्डं सर्वं सोमपञ्च दधि वारि खलप्वथ /
मधु त्रपु कर्तृ भक्तृ अतिवक्तृ पयः पुरः //
350.m: kuṇḍam, sarvam, somapam, dadhi, vāri, then khalapu, / madhu, trapu, kartṛ, bhaktṛ, ativaktṛ, payaḥ, puraḥ,

350.s:
prākpratyak ca tiryagudak jagad jāgrattathā sakṛt /
susampacca sudaṇḍīha ahaḥ kiñcedamityapi //
350.d:
प्राक्प्रत्यक् च तिर्यगुदक् जगद् जाग्रत्तथा सकृत् /
सुसम्पच्च सुदण्डीह अहः किञ्चेदमित्यपि //
350.m: prāk, pratyak, tiryak, udak, jagat, jāgrat, likewise sakṛt, / susampat, sudaṇḍi here, ahaḥ, kim, and idam as well,

350.s:
ṣaṭsarpiḥ śreyaś catvāri ado 'nye hīdṛśāḥ pare /
etebhyaḥ prathamādayaś ca syuḥ prātipadikātparāḥ //
350.d:
षट्सर्पिः श्रेयश् चत्वारि अदो ऽन्ये हीदृशाः परे /
एतेभ्यः प्रथमादयश् च स्युः प्रातिपदिकात्पराः //
350.m: ṣaṭ, sarpiḥ, śreyaḥ, catvāri, adaḥ, and other such words. / After these nominal stems, the first and other cases occur.

350.s:
dhātupratyayahīnaṃ yatsyāt prātipadikantu tat /
prātipadikāt svaliṅgārthavacane prathamā bhavet //
350.d:
धातुप्रत्ययहीनं यत्स्यात् प्रातिपदिकन्तु तत् /
प्रातिपदिकात् स्वलिङ्गार्थवचने प्रथमा भवेत् //
350.m: That which is devoid of root and affix is a nominal stem. / After a nominal stem, the first case occurs to express the stem's own gender, meaning, and number.

350.s:
sambodhane ca prathamā ukte karmaṇi kartari /
karma yat kriyate tatsyāt dvitīyā karmaṇi smṛtā //
350.d:
सम्बोधने च प्रथमा उक्ते कर्मणि कर्तरि /
कर्म यत् क्रियते तत्स्यात् द्वितीया कर्मणि स्मृता //
350.m: The first case also occurs in the vocative, and when the object or agent is expressed. / The object is that which is acted upon; the second case is prescribed for the object.

350.s:
kriyate yena karaṇaṃ kartā yaś ca karoti saḥ /
anukte tiṅkṛttaddhitaistṛtīyā karaṇe bhavet //
350.d:
क्रियते येन करणं कर्ता यश् च करोति सः /
अनुक्ते तिङ्कृत्तद्धितैस्तृतीया करणे भवेत् //
350.m: The instrument is that by means of which [an action] is done; and the agent is he who does [it]. / When not expressed by verb endings, primary affixes, or secondary affixes, the third case occurs for the instrument,

350.s:
kārake kartari ca sā sampradāne caturthyapi /
yasmai ditsā dhārayate sampradānaṃ tadoritaṃ //
:n
1 diveti ja..
:p 243
350.d:
कारके कर्तरि च सा सम्प्रदाने चतुर्थ्यपि /
यस्मै दित्सा धारयते सम्प्रदानं तदोरितं //
:न्
1 दिवेति ज..
:प् 243
350.m:
and also for the agent in an action; the fourth case occurs for the recipient. / That to which there is a wish to give or an obligation is declared to be the recipient.
[Footnote]
1 [Variant reading:] diva iti ... / :p 243

350.s:
apādānaṃ yato 'paiti ādatte ca bhayaṃ yataḥ /
apādāne pañcamī syāt svasvāmyādau ca ṣaṣṭhyapi //
350.d:
अपादानं यतो ऽपैति आदत्ते च भयं यतः /
अपादाने पञ्चमी स्यात् स्वस्वाम्यादौ च षष्ठ्यपि //
350.m: The ablation is that from which something departs, or from which one receives, or from which there is fear. / The fifth case occurs for ablation; and the sixth case occurs in the relation of owner and property, and so forth.

350.s:
ādhāro yo 'dhikaraṇaṃ vibhaktistatra saptamī /
ekārthe caikavanacaṃ dvyarthe dvivacanaṃ bhavet //
350.d:
आधारो यो ऽधिकरणं विभक्तिस्तत्र सप्तमी /
एकार्थे चैकवनचं द्व्यर्थे द्विवचनं भवेत् //
